jobs.title: Senior Researcher, Research Communication
jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

We're hiring for roles that will help us scale effectively. We expect to make one or more hires from this round, including a leadership-track hire who we believe can scale to build out a new function. This role (or roles) will shape how we communicate about our research, our reasoning, our uncertainties, and our mistakes, in keeping with our commitments to transparency and rigor.

The problem this role would solve and why it matters

GiveWell's Research teams own the work of determining which grants are most cost-effective: investigating existing programs, building and revising cost-effectiveness models, commissioning research to resolve our own uncertainties, and working with implementers to develop opportunities that don't yet exist but should. Our philanthropy and communications teams own the last mile of how we talk about that work, whether through a 1:1 conversation with a donor, a donor event, or scalable communications like blog posts, newsletters, and podcasts.

Between these teams sits a question: what are the most important and accurate things we should say about our work? Answering it requires a nuanced understanding of our research and our theories of change, and it is epistemically demanding, because our external communications are held to the standards of rigor, calibration, and honesty about uncertainty that we apply to our decision-making.

Today, answering these questions runs through a small group of senior leaders. But our funding is growing, and our programs are growing with it. The volume of research we need to cover and translate keeps expanding, as does the volume of complex, sophisticated donor questions, often from people considering making very large donations to our work. The result is a new-to-us problem: producing answers that meet GiveWell’s research bar, at speed and at volume.

The hard part of this work is rarely the phrasing. It's working out what we truly believe and what communicates that most effectively to those who follow our work. This matters far beyond fundraising. Sharing our work is central to our mission: we publish our reasoning so others can challenge it, and we change our minds when the evidence demands it. We believe excellent research communications could materially shape the direction of billions of dollars in funding from GiveWell donors and other actors, potentially saving hundreds of thousands of lives.

We see this role as critical to building a new function at GiveWell. You would help us reimagine and shape the substance of what we share with our donors and the outside world.

About the role

This senior role would own GiveWell's answers to the hardest questions we get about our work. Your responsibilities would include:

  • Working out what statements our research supports, developing what we can claim and defend, testing that against the researchers who own the underlying analysis, and holding a high bar for accuracy when a simpler answer would be more convenient.
  • Prioritizing across a portfolio of questions to deliver answers at the right altitude: which questions need a fast answer with correctly conveyed uncertainty, which warrant deeper research, and which point to gaps in our communication that are best served by published research.
  • Supporting the CEO and our senior leadership in external communications and major donor engagement. A significant portion of the work, especially as this role ramps up, will support Elie Hassenfeld, our co-founder and CEO, in his direct work with our largest supporters. Over time, you would engage with donors directly on research questions.
  • Setting the standard for external communications about GiveWell's research. Some communications go directly to individual donors, but our best work builds a platform that lets us communicate more effectively with everyone: tens of thousands of donors around the world, and partner organizations who may look to our work to inform their own.
  • Producing work yourself to GiveWell’s standards of quality, including long-form write-ups explaining our research, data visualizations, and interactive tools that deepen engagement with our work. As the function scales, we expect this will extend to hiring and leading a team that produces the work. (See “Current and future team structure” below.)

Questions you might take on

More than anything else, this role is about how you engage with questions. Take, as an example, a question we often get from our donors: "How much room for more funding do you have?" We have an answer, but it isn't easy to state simply, because the question nests several others inside it: What, exactly, counts as room for more funding? Over what time frame? How much risk are we willing to take on with respect to future fundraising? Where could we be right, where could we be wrong, and what would change our view?

Answering well means knowing how to answer all of that.

Other questions you might take on include:

  • Why did GiveWell set its moral weights the way it did, and how much would changing them affect our judgments?
  • How much room for more funding does GiveWell have? How much do we need, by when, and to do what?
  • What are the best ways to increase vaccination rates in a given country?
  • Is there a cost-effectiveness bar at which a donor should prefer a peer organization to GiveWell's top charities?
  • What is GiveWell's view on emerging technologies in malaria control?
  • How are we thinking about programs like gene drives to eradicate malaria?
  • How is GiveWell taking AI into account in its grantmaking strategy?

Answering these questions well will take a range of tools and approaches that make our work easier to explain, more accessible, and more compelling to people worldwide.

As a concrete example: our cost-effectiveness models have lived in spreadsheets for years. Given the tools available and our team's capacity, that was the best way to share our work. Now, many tools could make this work much easier to engage with.

For this and other projects, the work will run the gamut:

  • Writing long, detailed research write-ups
  • Creating data visualizations and charts
  • Working with AI to build interactive tools
  • Responsively answering questions from our largest donors
  • Doing public-facing work with donor audiences, including public speaking and answering questions live

Current and future team structure

Where this role sits

This role would report to Alex Cohen, Program Director, Research, and leader of our Cross-Cutting team, and would sit within our Research team. Cross-Cutting owns the research questions that span our portfolio.

Because this function is new to GiveWell, and because it matters so much to how we deliver on our mission, this hire would also have a dotted-line relationship with Elie Hassenfeld, our co-founder and CEO, and would work closely with our Outreach teams. Beyond informing our Outreach work, this role is the entry point for big-picture questions from donors that ultimately bear on our research strategy.

Future team leadership

We may make one hire from this round, or a few. We see this work as building out a function, and we expect it to need a team and a team leader. We think that leader could come from this round. If we make a single hire, we'll weigh team leadership experience more heavily, because that person will be best positioned to grow into leading the function. If we make several hires, we expect them to join as peers at the same level, with the understanding that the team's eventual leader will likely emerge from the cohort.

Because of this, we may make hires who fit different profiles:

  • An exceptional individual contributor who matches the strengths described below. They want to do this work at the highest level, and managing people isn't what draws them in. That is a great outcome for us, as this work rewards depth, and succeeding in this role does not require wanting to manage.
  • A future team lead who has built or led a team before, or is clearly ready to. They are energized by defining a standard, hiring against it, and managing people to it. They're willing to spend their first months or longer producing excellent work with their own hands. They understand that is how they will earn the command of our research that leading this work will require.

About you

You like to understand things deeply – well enough that you can explain them simply and concretely to someone encountering them for the first time. You really like explaining ideas. It's not enough to get an answer that's satisfying to you. You're most excited when you can communicate technical ideas in plain language that helps others understand them.

You get excited about a very wide variety of questions. You're comfortable deciding which of five open questions warrants days of research, which warrants a one-pager, and which requires a fast answer with our uncertainty clearly conveyed.

You'd rather put something rough in front of a colleague after an hour to get feedback and get to a faster answer than spend a week producing something excellent alone. You bring people along in your thinking, and you are interested in getting up to speed with others' perspectives.

You like working on a variety of things. You'd much rather work on five questions over the course of a week than one question over the course of a month.

You love improving. You're more interested in getting the answer right than being right.

You're motivated by global health and development and by finding the most effective ways to improve the lives of people in low-income countries.

You're excited about leading work in a variety of mediums, whether it's long detailed write-ups, data visualizations and charts, or interactive tools.

You operate well in a matrixed environment. Most of the people whose work you depend on won't report to you, and much of your credibility will come from researchers deciding you understand their analysis well enough to speak for it. You have experience earning that kind of standing in an organization, and you're comfortable pushing back on your colleagues, being pushed back on, and holding a line when it is important.

A candidate for the future team lead role has likely built and managed a team before. They are excited to define a mandate for a new team and manage people to it while still producing excellent work themselves for as long as the role requires.

We also expect that people with the qualities below, which we look for across our Research team, will be the most successful and happy in this role.

  • GiveWell's mission and methods personally energize you. You like our approach to research, and you find personal meaning in our story of impact.
  • You're abnormally curious. You ask lots of questions, and you're willing to interrogate others' work. Your curiosity also extends to your own work: you aren't defensive when your work is scrutinized.
  • You dislike it when people express strong confidence in views that don't seem to be backed by commensurate evidence. You communicate your confidence levels carefully and legibly.
  • You love a gnarly problem. You figure out the most important questions to answer, go deep on the details where they matter (and move on where they don't), and reassess your mental models based on what you've learned.

A quantitatively oriented advanced degree is a nice-to-have rather than a must, and a lower priority than the qualities above.

Process

The process for this role will be individualized based on how familiar we already are with a candidate's work abilities in the role areas. For someone whose work we don't know well, that could mean a short call about the role, up to two paid work trials, a longer interview, and reference checks — though it may be shorter or longer depending on the candidate. We only move people to a next step when we're confident it's a good use of their time, and we aim to balance respect for that time with rigor in how we make our hiring decisions.

The details

  • Compensation: We set salaries using a location-based tier system. Our pay for this role:
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $308,000.
    • All other U.S. locations: $280,000.
    • International: Similar to the “all other U.S. locations” salary, based on historical exchange rates and delivered in locally-denominated currency. We can share a precise figure upon request after the first work trial stage.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the U.S. for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • Automatic contribution equal to 5% of your gross salary into your 403(b) retirement plan (for U.S.-based staff)
  • Location: GiveWell's staff work primarily remotely, within the U.S. and abroad. This position is eligible for fully remote work.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California; Brooklyn, New York; or London, UK. We'll cover relocation expenses for candidates who wish to move to any of our physical office locations.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. A successful candidate will need to commit to a work schedule that has some overlap with U.S. working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Working arrangements: We're uncertain about whether non-full-time arrangements are possible and exactly how your work might develop over time — we're happy to discuss both in depth with strong candidates.
  • Visa sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we'll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Travel: Research team members are sometimes required to attend international site visits and conferences (on average 1-2 per year), with additional travel for those interested in traveling more. Additionally, we strongly encourage staff members to attend quarterly whole-org and department retreats to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. We'll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we'll accommodate staff who have conflicting family or other commitments.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

jobs.description:
About KarmaCheck
KarmaCheck was founded by Eric Ly, a co-founder and the original CTO of LinkedIn. We are modernizing background screening, verification, and credentialing for the staffing industry, with a focus on healthcare staffing. Our customers run screening inside the ATS, VMS, and HRIS platforms they already use, through our integrations and our public API, and KarmaCheck is the only background check integration in Bullhorn's investment portfolio.
We are now building an AI workforce: agents that automate the compliance workflows our customers run today by hand. This is hands-on work with vertical AI, not maintenance of a legacy screening platform.
About the opportunity
Building AI agents is half the work. The other half is making them work inside a customer's world: their Bullhorn, Symplr CTM, or Workday instance, their proprietary systems, and the workflows they actually run. This role is the Product team's technical expert on that second half.
Customer Success runs our standard introductions and scripted pitches. When a conversation goes off script, when a workflow does not fit what we planned for, or when someone asks whether our API could support something new, you are the person who works out the answer and then gets it built. Roadmap and prioritization sit with Product leadership; within the integration lane, you own the scoping, the solution, and delivery. This is a small team, and you will do the work with autonomy and ownership.

How you approach the work

  • Generating options: when a customer workflow does not fit a standard pattern, you come up with several workable approaches, weigh the trade-offs, and recommend one, often during the conversation itself
  • Recognizing patterns: you notice when issues across different customers, partners, or implementations share a root cause, and you turn them into standard solutions rather than one-off fixes
  • Thinking in systems: before committing to a solution, you consider its effect on the customer, Customer Success, Implementation, engineering capacity, and our partners
  • Reading people: you pay attention to how customers and colleagues are reacting and adjust your approach. You can deliver news a customer did not want to hear and keep their trust
  • Working independently: you make scoping and solution decisions within agreed guardrails and escalate only what genuinely needs a leadership call

What you will do

  • Be the technical voice on customer and prospect calls once a conversation moves past the standard pitch: customization, non-standard use, troubleshooting, and how our API could support something new
  • Get our AI products live inside customer systems, the role's top priority, working with the product team driving them on what changes in the API or partner integrations and how a customer turns them on
  • Design how KarmaCheck fits into a customer's systems via API and otherwise: data flows, field and status mapping, error handling, and configuration
  • Own customer solutions end to end with engineering: write the requirements, break down the work, track delivery, and keep customers and internal teams informed through go-live
  • Act as the hands-on technical counterpart for Bullhorn, Symplr CTM, Workday, and our VMS and direct sourcing partners
  • Turn the integration questions you answer repeatedly into documentation and configuration guides, so Customer Success and Implementation can handle more on their own. Over time, this role shifts toward turning recurring custom solutions into standard product

Requirements

  • 5+ years in technical product management, integration or solutions architecture, or technical implementation at a software company, with substantial time working directly with customers and/or high EQ
  • Hands-on experience with REST APIs, webhooks, data mapping, and authentication. You can read API documentation, test calls yourself (Postman or similar), and reason about how an integration could work without waiting for an engineer
  • Strong written requirements and project execution: you can turn a messy customer ask into a clear spec engineers can build from, then run the project with them through delivery
  • Integration experience across multiple systems. We care more about the breadth of patterns you have seen than about any one platform

Helpful, and learnable here

  • Healthcare staffing, background screening, credentialing, or compliance. We would rather hire strong integration instincts and ramp the domain than the reverse
  • Credentialing or verification experience
  • Familiarity with ATS, VMS, HCM, or HRIS ecosystems such as Bullhorn, Symplr, or Workday
  • SQL or light scripting for testing, troubleshooting, and reporting
  • Experience deploying AI or automation features into customer environments

jobs.excerpt: About UsInStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it.
jobs.description:
About Us

InStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it. Through this mission, we are expanding access to insurance-based care, increasing engagement in treatment, and improving treatment outcomes. We are doing this by combining research-backed clinical care and innovative technology to eliminate the major problems with care today: difficulty finding providers, months of waiting to be seen, arduous onboarding processes, and inconsistent use of evidence-based therapies and outcomes tracking. Our vision is to become the nation’s most trusted provider of pediatric anxiety and OCD care.

TeamInStride Health: Our Core Values

  • Give Heart: We lead with heart, treating patients and their families the way we want our loved ones to be treated.
  • Work Smart: We find smarter ways to solve hard problems and fix the broken mental health system by leveraging technology, diversity of thought, and innovation.
  • Have Humility: We leave our egos at the door, empowering our team to collaborate, celebrate diversity, and adopt a growth mindset.
  • Embrace Community: We all belong. We are in this together, and we never worry alone. We believe in each other and recognize that every voice matters.

About the Role

We are looking for an Instructional Designer to design, build, and manage learning initiatives for our community of providers, including psychiatrists, therapists, and exposure coaches. As a key member of our Learning and Development team, you will partner with clinical leaders and subject matter experts to turn complex behavioral health protocols into engaging, practical training that strengthens the care our providers deliver to kids, teens, and families. The ideal candidate brings a background in online course creation and project management. This is a fully remote position.

Responsibilities:

Needs Assessment & Instructional Design

  • Conduct front-end needs analyses with clinical leadership to diagnose performance gaps and define measurable, performance-based learning objectives.
  • Apply adult learning theory and instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, SAM, Backward Design) to structure modular asynchronous and synchronous training paths.
  • Partner closely with clinical subject matter experts (SMEs) to translate complex behavioral health protocols into digestible, scenario-based learning experiences.

Content Development & Multimedia Production

  • Design and develop interactive e-learning modules, job aids, and knowledge checks using Articulate 360 (Storyline and Rise).
  • Script, record, and edit multimedia elements, including video walkthroughs, audio voiceovers, screencasts, and graphic assets, using tools such as Camtasia.
  • Use generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, AI voiceover platforms) responsibly to accelerate storyboarding, draft scenario scripts, build assessment items, and streamline authoring workflows.
  • Stay current on emerging technologies and trends in digital learning.

Measurement, Quality Assurance & Iteration

  • Build assessments that evaluate learner comprehension, retention, and clinical application.
  • Conduct rigorous quality assurance reviews of AI-assisted drafts and finalized modules to confirm clinical accuracy, tone, instructional integrity, and technical functionality before deployment.
  • Gather post-training analytics and learner feedback to continuously refine and improve curriculum assets.

Project Management

  • Deliver work against defined project timelines, share regular progress updates with cross-functional partners, and keep project tracking tools (e.g., ClickUp) current in real time.

What You Need to Succeed in the Role

  • Bachelor's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Instructional Technology, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of professional experience in instructional design and digital course development, ideally for specialized, technical, or clinical adult audiences.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in rapid e-learning authoring tools (specifically Articulate 360) and video/audio editing software (e.g., TechSmith Camtasia, Audacity, or Adobe Creative Cloud).
  • Solid foundation in adult learning theory, instructional design models, and assessment design (e.g., Bloom's Taxonomy, Kirkpatrick Evaluation Model).
  • Practical experience using generative AI tools to accelerate content ideation, drafting, and multimedia production while maintaining strict editorial and factual oversight.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Clear, effective verbal and written communication across remote, multidisciplinary teams.
  • Ability to work well both independently and as part of a collaborative, cross-functional team in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.
  • Interest or background in behavioral health is a plus.
  • Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic startup environment: we're looking for candidates who embrace change, thrive in ambiguity, and shift readily as priorities and team needs evolve.

A portfolio of past instructional design projects, storyboards, or interactive e-learning modules is required with your application.

Salary

The expected annual salary for this role is between $72,000–$80,000. Actual starting salary will be determined on an individualized basis and will be based on several factors including but not limited to specific skill set, work experience, etc.

Why Join Our Team

  • Generous benefits package (401k with match, Flexible PTO, paid holidays, paid service days, 4 week paid sabbatical, 12 week paid parental leave, health benefits starting on your first day, and more)
  • Opportunity to join a mission-driven company that is changing the landscape of pediatric mental health treatment
  • Chance to make a far-reaching impact by helping children and families access desperately-needed, evidence-based care
  • Opportunity to work with talented and experienced team members who have devoted their lives to solving this problem
  • Fully virtual: work from the comfort of your home with periodic in-person retreats

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging (DEIB)

We want to make our clinical services available for everyone, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or how you identify. To achieve this, we recognize we must continually make progress in building a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive team. Through these efforts, we support two primary objectives at InStride Health:

  1. Providing high quality patient care to families. We are in a privileged position to support families during a vulnerable time in their lives. We approach all families and each other with compassion and are most effective as a diverse team where all individuals feel valued, respected, and accepted.
  2. Building a mission-driven business that lasts. Specifically, we believe our commitment to a supportive culture improves innovation, decision-making, and efficiency.

We invite you to share any additional information about yourself or your experiences that may not be reflected in your CV. Inclusion of this information is completely voluntary.

Beware of fake job postings and offers. All official communications from InStride Health will come from email addresses ending in @instride.health. We will never ask for personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank details during the application process. If you receive a suspicious job offer or communication, please contact our recruitment team directly () to verify its authenticity.

Reporting to the President and CEO, the Vice President of Human Resources (Administrative Services Lead) serves as the College's chief human resources officer and provides strategic leadership and management across all aspects of the College's human resources function. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President serves as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to the President, executive leaders, and the Board of Trustees on workforce strategy, organizational effectiveness, labor relations, employment policy, and risk management, ensuring the College has the talent, leadership capacity, and organizational infrastructure needed to advance its mission and strategic priorities. Over time, this position may expand to provide executive oversight across areas such as Human Resources, Legal Affairs, and Finance as a part of an integrated administrative services strategy.

The Vice President of Human Resources (Administrative Services Lead) leads the development and implementation of a sustainable Human Resources strategy that supports the College's continued growth and evolution. This includes strengthening workforce planning, talent acquisition and retention, organizational development, compliance, and Human Resources operations while fostering a workplace culture grounded in equity, belonging, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement. The Vice President also leads the continued modernization of the College's Human Resources function by improving systems, technology, business processes, and the use of workforce data to enhance operational effectiveness, employee experience, and organizational capacity.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities

The duties below are representative of the role and are not intended to cover all of the duties performed within the scope of work.

I. Strategic Human Capital Leadership

  • Leads the development and implementation of a comprehensive Human Resources strategy aligned with the College’s mission, strategic plan, and long-term organizational priorities.
  • Provides executive leadership for strategic workforce planning to ensure the College has the talent and organizational capacity to meet current and future needs.
  • Serves as a strategic advisor to the President, Executive Team, and Board of Trustees on workforce strategy, organizational effectiveness, labor relations, and human capital risks.
  • Leads organizational development, leadership development, and succession planning initiatives to strengthen institutional capacity and leadership continuity.
  • Develops Human Resources policies and practices that advance equity, compliance, innovation, and continuous improvement.
  • Leads or supports organizational change initiatives that strengthen institutional effectiveness and workforce adaptability.

II. Talent Acquisition, Employee Experience & Workforce Development

  • Provides executive leadership for recruitment, hiring, and selection processes to ensure equitable, compliant, efficient, and workforce-aligned practices.
  • Partners with managers around team organization and talent strategy development and technical implementation, aligned with evolving operational needs, compliance requirements, and best practices.
  • Oversees employee orientation and onboarding, hiring committee training, faculty minimum qualifications, and equivalency processes to ensure consistent and compliant hiring practices.
  • Leads development and implementation of culture-building initiatives, including strategies to support change management to strengthen employee engagement, retention, and trust across the College.
  • Oversees employee performance management and supports professional development and training programs that enhance organizational effectiveness.
  • Leads leadership development initiatives that build current and future leadership capacity across the institution.
  • Reviews and approves Human Resources processes, materials, and related documentation to ensure compliance, consistency, and alignment with institutional policies.

III. Human Resources Operations, Systems & Modernization

  • Provides executive oversight of Human Resources operations to ensure efficient, consistent, and effective delivery of HR services.
  • Leads the modernization of Human Resources systems, policies and procedures, leveraging technology to streamline and continuously improve hiring, onboarding, performance management, and employee records and data management.
  • Develops strategies to streamline, standardize, and automate HR processes to improve efficiency, accuracy, and consistency.
  • Partners with Information Technology and College divisions to ensure HR systems are integrated and aligned with institutional systems and priorities.
  • Utilizes workforce analytics and HR metrics to support reporting, planning, and executive decision-making.
  • Oversees maintenance of employee records, employment documentation, and Human Resources files in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and institutional policies.

IV. Labor Relations, Compliance & Risk Management

  • Serves as the College’s chief labor negotiator and provides executive leadership for collective bargaining and labor relations.
  • Develops and executes a proactive labor relations strategy designed to build a more collaborative labor-management relationship over time.
  • Oversees complaints, grievance resolution, disciplinary matters, workplace investigations, and employee relations issues.
  • Serves as the College’s Equal Employment Opportunity Officer and Title IX Coordinator, ensuring compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and Board policies and coordinating with external agencies such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, California Civil Rights Department, and U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights as required.
  • Serves as the College’s primary representative in matters before the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) and other labor relations bodies and regulatory agencies, working closely with legal counsel on unfair labor practice charges, grievance arbitration, and contract interpretation disputes.
  • Provides executive oversight of employee benefits, leave administration, workers’ compensation, unemployment, and related risk management programs.
  • Ensures compliance with federal and state employment laws, California Education Code, Title 5 regulations, and collective bargaining agreements.
  • Oversees mandatory training, compliance reporting, and regulatory employment requirements.
  • Establishes documented, repeatable desktop procedures for core HR transactions to reduce risk and reliance on manual processes, institutional knowledge, and improve audit-readiness.

V. Executive Leadership & Institutional Partnership

  • Collaborates with executive leadership to advance institutional priorities and strengthen organizational effectiveness.
  • Prepares and presents Human Resources reports, agenda items, and recommendations to the Board of Trustees.
  • Supervises, develops, and evaluates Human Resources leadership and staff.
  • Develops and administers departmental goals, budgets, policies, and operational plans.
  • Promotes a workplace culture grounded in equity, belonging, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Oversees development, revision, and maintenance of Human Resources policies, procedures, forms, and related administrative documentation to ensure compliance and operational consistency.
  • Represents the College on internal and external committees, task forces, negotiations, and professional organizations as appropriate.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned in support of the College’s mission and strategic priorities.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of:

  • Principles and practices of public sector human resources administration.
  • Federal and state employment laws, including California Education Code, wage and hour laws, Title 5, ADA, Title IX, and related regulations.
  • Collective bargaining, labor relations, and grievance/disciplinary processes.
  • Employee relations, recruitment, selection, worker classification, and performance management practices.
  • Human Resources information systems and basic workforce reporting tools.

Skills in:

  • Developing and implementing HR policies, procedures, and compliance practices.
  • Communicating effectively with employees, managers, executives, governing boards, and external agencies.
  • Leading through organizational change, building trusted relationships, and guiding culture-building.

Ability to:

  • Plan, organize, and direct a comprehensive Human Resources operation in a public sector or higher education environment.
  • Analyze complex personnel issues and develop appropriate solutions.
  • Lead investigations and resolve employee relations matters in a fair and consistent manner.
  • Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment in sensitive matters.
  • Manage through both proactive labor management relations and adversarial labor relations environments.
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with diverse constituencies.
  • Lead cross-functionally within lean organizational structures.
  • Prepare and present reports and recommendations to executive leadership and governing boards.

    OR

Business Development Manager

Position summary

Solutions Metrix is hiring a Business Development Manager to build and run our account-based growth strategy in financial services. You will research priority banks and credit unions, reach the right decision-makers, and turn their needs and transformation plans into qualified opportunities for our CRM, integration, data, and business transformation services.

This is not a high-volume sales development role. Success means creating access, intelligence, engagement, and qualified pipeline in the accounts we most want to serve. You will work closely with Sales, Marketing, Client Partnerships, executive leadership, and our technology partners.

What you'll do

Research target accounts

  • Learn each assigned account's leadership, technology environment, priorities, and active initiatives.
  • Watch for engagement triggers: executive changes, mergers, technology conversions, modernization, and customer or member experience programs.

Map stakeholders and build relationships

  • Identify executives and influencers across technology, operations, digital, member experience, data, and marketing.
  • Use existing company, employee, advisor, client, and partner connections for introductions.

Prospect and develop accounts

  • Run personalized, sustained outreach by phone, email, LinkedIn, events, and referrals, tailored to each person's role and institution.

Work with technology partners

  • Work with Creatio, Boomi, and other partners to find shared target accounts, warm introductions, and joint pursuits, and track partner-supported activity.

Run discovery and hand off

  • Hold first conversations to understand challenges and current state, and spot needs in CRM, integration, data, workflow automation, member experience, and modernization.

How success is measured

We measure account development and pipeline, not activity alone:

  • Priority accounts engaged, new stakeholders identified, and multi-threaded relationships built
  • Qualified discovery conversations and conference meetings with priority accounts
  • Engaged accounts converted into qualified sales opportunities, and pipeline created
  • Partner-assisted introductions and opportunities
  • Quality and completeness of account intelligence in the CRM

What we're looking for

Required

  • 3 to 5+ years in business development, account development, enterprise sales, fintech, financial services, consulting, enterprise software, or a related field
  • Skill at researching organizations and finding the right decision-makers and influencers
  • Strong written and verbal communication, credible with senior business and technology leaders
  • Comfort starting relationships by phone, email, LinkedIn, events, and referrals
  • Experience with CRM and sales or business development tools

Nice to have

  • Experience with banks, credit unions, fintechs, or financial services technology providers
  • Familiarity with core banking, CRM, integration, data, digital banking, or workflow automation platforms
  • Account-based marketing, named-account sales, or strategic account development experience
  • Relationships with executive-level buyers

Who thrives here

You want to understand how organizations work and where their real problems are. You turn public information into useful intelligence and talk about business issues, not just products. You are persistent without being repetitive and credible with senior leaders at banks and credit unions.

You also work well with Sales, Marketing, consultants, leadership, and partners, stay organized across many accounts, and own outcomes. A growing company with an evolving go-to-market suits you.

Where the role fits

The role sits in Revenue Operations and connects market development to active sales. The goal is more than booking meetings. You help Solutions Metrix Identify → Understand → Surround → Engage → Convert → Expand priority accounts, so our sales and consulting teams start conversations with more context, more credibility, and a better chance of winning.

LifeMD is seeking a Medical Director to provide clinical leadership across our multi-vertical telehealth platform. This role holds physician-level accountability for the quality, safety, and compliance of clinical care delivered through our network of MD/DOs and nurse practitioners (NPs), and partners closely with product and clinical operations teams to shape how care is delivered at scale.

Key Responsibilities:

Physician Supervision & Accountability

  • Supervise, mentor, and evaluate MD/DO providers across the platform's clinical verticals
  • Establish and monitor performance metrics for physicians (e.g., quality of documentation, adherence to protocol, patient outcomes, escalation handling, complaint/incident rates)
  • Partner with the Clinical NP Manager to co-drive accountability for overall clinical performance across the combined physician and NP workforce
  • Conduct or oversee periodic chart audits and peer review

Collaborating Physician Duties

  • Serve as collaborating/supervising physician for NPs in states where state law requires a collaborative practice or supervision agreement
  • Maintain compliant, up-to-date collaborative practice agreements in each applicable state, including required chart review percentages, meeting cadence, and documentation standards
  • Monitor changes in state NP scope-of-practice law (full practice authority vs. reduced/restricted) and adjust collaboration structures accordingly, in coordination with legal/compliance
  • Administrative support in Full Practice Authority (FPA) states, NPs may practice independently without a collaborating physician; this role's supervisory obligations in those states are administrative/quality-based rather than a legal collaboration requirement

Clinical Protocol Development

  • Develop, review, and maintain evidence-based clinical protocols and treatment guidelines across the platform's service lines
  • Ensure protocols reflect current clinical guidelines, incorporate risk mitigation, and are updated as new evidence or regulatory guidance emerges
  • Standardize protocols across verticals where clinically appropriate while allowing for vertical-specific nuance

Product & New Vertical Review

  • Participate in clinical review of new products, service lines, and platform features prior to launch
  • Assess proposed new verticals for clinical appropriateness, regulatory risk, and staffing/scope-of-practice implications
  • Serve as clinical subject-matter expert in cross-functional product planning meetings
  • Partner closely with the SVP of Operations on the business and operational implications of new products, staffing models, and clinical capacity planning

Quality, Risk & Compliance

  • Identify and respond to clinical risk trends (e.g., adverse events, malpractice exposure, prescribing pattern outliers)
  • Partner with Legal/Compliance on licensing, credentialing, and multi-state regulatory requirements
  • Support incident investigations and corrective action plans
  • Serve as a voting member of the Quality & Patient Safety Committee (QPSC)
  • Lead or participate in root cause analyses (RCAs) for adverse events, near-misses, and clinical practice issues, and ensure corrective action plans are implemented and tracked to closure
  • Champion a culture of clinical quality and patient safety across all provider types and verticals, including trend monitoring, peer review findings, and safety event reporting

Physician Administration

  • As the direct manager of the physician staff, review and approve physician timecards and payroll submissions on a recurring basis
  • Manage physician payroll, including compensation calculation, bonus/incentive structures tied to clinical performance, and timely resolution of payroll discrepancies
  • Partner with Finance and Legal on physician compensation structure, contract terms, and payroll system administration

Requirements

  • MD or DO with active, unrestricted medical license (multi-state licensure or willingness to obtain additional state licenses preferred)
  • Board certification in a relevant specialty (e.g., Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Emergency Medicine)
  • 8+ years of clinical practice experience including experience in the telehealth space
  • Experience supervising or collaborating with NPs and/or PAs, ideally across multiple states
  • Familiarity with telehealth care delivery models and multi-state regulatory/licensing considerations
  • Demonstrated experience developing clinical protocols or guidelines

Preferred:

  • Prior experience in a Medical Director or similar clinical leadership role at a telehealth or multi-site healthcare company
  • Experience across multiple clinical verticals (e.g., primary care, weight management, mental health, urgent care, women’s health, men’s health)

  • Experience navigating state-by-state NP scope-of-practice variation

  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)

  • Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)

  • Malpractice insurance coverage

The Role

This role leads the EMEA Small to medium and MidMarket business team and is accountable for new logo acquisition and expansion revenue across the region. The expectations are high: a team that generates its own pipeline across multiple countries, deals that are qualified with discipline, forecasts that hold, and Account Executives who improve every quarter.

This is not an oversight role. The leader in this seat works deals alongside their team, sets the standard for outbound execution in each market, and uses data to drive performance. It is a first-line leader role who has already delivered results in EMEA and wants to operate at the pace and scale of a fast-growing company.

Responsibilities

Deal leadership

  • Engage directly in the team's most important opportunities: discovery, executive alignment, mutual close plans, commercial structure, procurement, legal, DPA, and security review.
  • Set the standard for value-based selling: quantifying the customer's business pain, building the business case, and tying Bitwarden to risk reduction and compliance outcomes that drive European buying decisions (GDPR, NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001).
  • Diagnose and unblock stalled deals, and use them to raise the skill level of the entire team. Coach disciplined excellence and field skills to find, transition and close deals efficiently.
  • Work tirelessly in the detail of each customer requirement, enabled by experience and strategic effort, placing Bitwarden in the best position possible to win deals and transfer this knowledge to the team.
  • Drive accountability through metrics, motivation, method and effective communication techniques. Be accountable, methodical, pragmatic and foster by example lead from the front.

Outbound pipeline generation

  • Build and mature a repeatable cold outbound motion with AEs and partnered SDRs, localized by market: territory and account prioritization, ICP and persona targeting, multi-threaded sequencing, and messaging adapted for country and language.
  • Set activity and pipeline-generation standards, inspect them weekly, and hold every AE accountable for self-sourced pipeline.
  • Align and drive our message with Marketing, Sales Development, and Channel on programs, including partner-sourced plays, that produce qualified pipeline at a predictable rate.

MEDDPICC and value-based execution

  • Run MEDDPICC as the team's operating system across qualification, deal reviews, forecast calls, and win/loss analysis, with value-based selling defining how the team earns and proves each element.
  • Inspect every material opportunity for quantified Metrics, a validated Economic Buyer, a tested Champion, clear Decision Criteria and Process, a mapped Paper Process (including works council, procurement, and data-protection steps), and an honest read on Competition.
  • Deliver an accurate weekly forecast built on deal evidence and maintain CRM data the business can rely on.

Data-driven coaching

  • Own the team's KPIs (pipeline generation, coverage, stage conversion, win rate, cycle length, average deal size, and activity-to-outcome ratios) by rep and by market, and act on what they show.
  • Identify where each AE is losing ground and build targeted coaching plans to close the gap.
  • Run a disciplined operating cadence across time zones: weekly 1:1s, pipeline and deal reviews, forecast calls, and call reviews.

Team building

  • Recruit, hire, onboard, and ramp high-caliber Account Executives across EMEA markets, and develop them toward promotion.
  • Build a culture of accountability, competitiveness, and continuous improvement across countries and cultures.
  • Work across Sales Operations, Sales Enablement, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Channel, and Marketing, to deliver revenue as one team.

Requirements

  • 3–5 years of first-line sales leadership in EMEA, ideally leading AEs selling security SaaS (identity, access, credential, endpoint, or adjacent categories).
  • A proven, documented track record of quota attainment as a leader, and as an individual contributor before that.
  • Deep working fluency in MEDDPICC and value-based selling, applied together to qualify, inspect, forecast, and coach.
  • A track record of building and maturing a cold outbound pipeline across more than one EMEA market, with the ability to explain exactly how it was done and what it produced.
  • Strong analytical skills, including fluency with Hubspot & industry tooling for reporting, dashboards, and spreadsheets, and a record of using KPIs to direct coaching and improve AE performance.
  • A hands-on approach to leadership, with direct, regular involvement in live deals.
  • Player-coach, building own pipeline coaching the team through example, including closing and processing, customer excellence.
  • Strong intellect, a fast learning curve, and the drive to perform in a high-growth environment with demanding targets.
  • Strong command of EMEA buying dynamics, procurement processes, regulatory drivers, and channel/partner models.
  • Fluent business English. (Additional languages are beneficial considering the role supports all of EMEA e.g., German, French, Dutch, etc.)

At Twin Health, we empower people to improve and prevent chronic metabolic diseases, like type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a new standard of care. Twin Health is the only company applying AI Digital Twin technology exclusively toward metabolic health.

We start by building a dynamic model of each person’s metabolism — drawing on thousands of data points from CGMs, smartwatches, and meal logs — that maps their personal path to better health. Working here

Our team at Twin Health is passionate, talented, and united by a shared purpose: to improve the metabolic health and happiness of our members. We believe in empowering every Twin to make a meaningful impact for our members, our clients, and each other, while enjoying a supportive, collaborative work environment.

Twin has been recognized not only for our innovation but also for our culture, including: Innovator of the Year by the Employer Health Innovation Roundtable (EHIR), selected to CB Insights’ Digital Health 150, and named one of Newsweek’s Top Most Loved Workplace® .

With more than $100 million raised in recent funding, including a $53 million Series E round in 2025 led by Maj Invest, and a $50 million investment in 2023 led by Temasek, Twin is scaling rapidly across the U.S. and globally. Backed by leading venture firms like ICONIQ Growth, Sequoia, Sofina, Temasek, and Peak XV, we are building the most impactful digital health company in the world.

We are looking for a Registered Nurse and Manager, Clinical Stewardship Operations who is a self-starter energized by working with clients and building strong relationships both externally and internally to drive exceptional outcomes for our clients and members. The ability to problem solve, analyze and troubleshoot, with strong verbal and written communication skills tailored to the situation and audience, will be key.

  • Manage project expectations through regular meetings, status reports and strong relationships
  • Build out standard implementation work plans, templates, playbooks and cross-functional SOPs to drive continuous improvement and best practices for stewardship
  • Prepare, execute and participate in special events held for or hosted by clients

Lead Cross-functionally

  • Manage client issues and escalations and mobilize internal teams such as Client Growth, Clinical Delivery, Product, Member Operations and Business Development to drive resolution
  • Partner with Business Development and Client Growth on stewardship scoping, solutioning and new client opportunities, providing clinical input during the sales process
  • Work cross-functionally with teams such as Clinical Delivery, Product, Marketing, Engineering, Billing Operations and Executive teams to ensure client and market feedback drives ongoing improvement

Preferred

In 2017, our founders started Sarwa due to a lack of financial services offered to most of the world, and out of a need to help empower people in the region to invest in their financial future. Sarwa is poised to continue growing into the go-to platform for people to grow their wealth.

We do this through expert, affordable and easy investing. We're a small team working on the region's first and fastest growing investment and personal finance platform, making investing easy, low-cost and transparent, with a human touch woven into every step of the process.

We are a remote-first team. Where you choose to work is up to you — we have an office in Abu Dhabi that you can utilise as often or little as you'd like.

We are looking for a Marketing Associate that keeps Sarwa's marketing on (or ahead of) schedule. You'll own the content calendar and publishing across our channels, and help get product launches, campaigns and partnerships out the door. The role also includes ideating and writing, with plenty of room to experiment with content.

What you'll do

  • Run the marketing board. Track social content and campaigns from brief to launch.

  • Support product launches end to end. Pull together the full set of launch comms (email, in-app pop-ups, push, social, help centre and FAQs), make sure every asset is ready, and line it all up for launch day.

  • Execute campaigns. Set up and QA campaign emails, in-app flows and landing pages, and keep teams across the company updated and aligned on what's going live and when.

  • Publish and schedule. Upload, format and schedule content across social, email, the app, and the newsletter. Check every detail before it goes live.

  • Manage the compliance workflow. Submit content and campaigns for review, track feedback and versions, and make sure nothing goes out without sign-off.

  • Support partnerships and events. Work with the team leads on creator and influencer collaborations, webinars and events. Help prepare briefs, track timelines.

  • Support shoots. Work with our content team to prepare scripts, get approvals and set schedules, so every shoot day runs smoothly.

  • Own the daily newsletter. Write and send the daily brief, along with the daily push notification.

  • Report on performance. Pull channel and campaign numbers into a regular snapshot, and analyse insights to support team strategy.

Requirements

  • A bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, English Literature or a related field. Fresh graduates and early-career applicants are welcome.

  • A track record of keeping many moving pieces on schedule.

  • Strong attention to detail.

  • Clear, natural writing in English.

  • An interest in investing and how people think about money.

  • Comfort with marketing tools, or the ability to pick them up quickly: email/CRM platforms, scheduling and analytics tools, a CMS and project boards (ActiveCampaign, Sprout Social, ClickUp, etc.).

  • Calm, direct communication with writers, designers, product, compliance and external partners.

  • Enthusiasm to learn and grow. You ask questions, take feedback well and want more responsibility over time.

Some of our benefits:

  • Remote and flexible work environment

  • Diverse, driven and supportive team with a positive work atmosphere (one of our core values)

  • A culture of growth - being mentored, coached and supported to grow in your career

  • Great company healthcare package with dental and optical coverage

  • Learning and development budget

  • Equity plan for all employees.

jobs.excerpt: Career OpportunityRole TitleSenior UnderwriterPurpose of roleThe Senior Underwriter is responsible for underwriting life insurance application using universally recognized underwriting principles by evaluating health, financial, lifestyle and other risk factors to determine the appropriate underwriting rate class, while managing and maintaining service levels and acceptable mortality results.
jobs.description:
Career Opportunity

Role Title

Senior Underwriter

Purpose of role

The Senior Underwriter is responsible for underwriting life insurance application using universally recognized underwriting principles by evaluating health, financial, lifestyle and other risk factors to determine the appropriate underwriting rate class, while managing and maintaining service levels and acceptable mortality results. The incumbent will work closely with and establish strong relationships with company stakeholders including New Business, Actuarial, Claims, and Distribution.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

  • Review insurance application files for new business, reinstatements and coverage change requests
  • Establish and maintain effective relationships with producers, including communicating the underwriting decision
  • Balance investigative costs for tests/assessments versus risk management requirements to make informed underwriting decisions and determine steps to be taken to fully evaluate the application, including identifying additional required information and/or professional resource assessment reports
  • Order required medical tests/assessments, as required. Arrange for any additional required assessments from professional resource contacts and contact the producer to obtain missing application information
  • Research, interpret and analyze information relevant to the application, including product details, legislation, rate manuals, medical/drug reference books, applicant insurance history, motor vehicle reports and other relevant sources. Access (decode) confidential medical information related to the applicant through the Medical Information Bureau (MIB)
  • Efficiently document the applicant file on the Underwriting systems as additional information is received. Code and enter data from received medical reports to the information system
  • Complete a full underwriting assessment of the application following the receipt and review of all required information, considering potentially competing factors such as new/increased business income to Foresters versus risk of significant financial loss. Consult with Chief Underwriter as required on complex underwriting issues
  • Finalize the underwriting decision within approval limits as assigned by the Chief Underwriter, carefully distinguishing standard from preferred and preferred plus risks, and authorize issues of the new or revised insurance certificate for approval applications
  • Initiate processes to refer application files for reinsurance as required
  • Compose related correspondence to members/producers related to the information required to assess the application with appropriate reconsiderations, where possible; advisory letters to the member and producer regarding the approval/decline of the application, letters containing confidential medical information to the applicant’s physician related to a decline decision
  • Participate in the research, review and analysis of underwriting related legislation and regulations, and current underwriting issues and trends, and participate in the review and development of new/revised underwriting policies, procedures, systems and standards as assigned by the Chief Underwriter
  • Work with the Medical Director on cases as required
  • Other projects and duties as assigned

Key Qualifications

  • A minimum of five (5) plus years of underwriting experience
  • Achieved AALU and working towards FALU/FLMI designations
  • Strong medical and financial underwriting knowledge
  • Experience with simplified issue and final expense type products
  • Strong knowledge of underwriting theory, principles, methods, systems, processes and standards attained from Part One of the Academy of Life Underwriting program and underwriting experience
  • Consultation skills to make consistent and appropriate underwriting decisions within Foresters policies and standards
  • Consultation and communication skills to request information from a broad range of resources/professionals as required
  • Knowledge of the interpretation and application of underwriting legislation and regulations across the US
  • Knowledge of the Foresters purpose, goals and objectives to ensure compliance of decisions with Foresters policies and standards
  • Ability to learn and understand in detail, Foresters insurance products and contact provisions to review and assess applications in order to make effective underwriting decisions
  • Travel to Head Office, Toronto, Ontario, Canada will be required.

The actual base salary for this position will depend on several factors, including job-related skills, experience, and education. In addition to base pay, eligible employees may participate in a discretionary variable incentive plan, results are subject to both individual and company performance.


Please note that this posting is intended to fill an existing vacancy; however, there may be instances where more than one vacancy is available for the same role.

The Role

Base salary range: $120K to $200K
OTE (On-Target Earnings) range: $240K to $400K

Reporting to Sales Leadership, our Client Partner is responsible for managing and growing a portfolio of client relationships for CCC Intelligent Solutions. This is a hands‑on, client‑facing sales role focused on deepening commercial partnerships, driving account growth, and expanding adoption of CCC’s strategic products.

The Client Partner operates as a trusted advisor to clients, balancing relationship management with disciplined sales execution. This role requires the ability to prioritize across a portfolio, identify whitespace, build pipeline, and execute structured sales plays while maintaining a consultative, value‑driven approach.

There is flexibility around location for this role. Considerable travel will be required to visit clients and to spend time with the senior leadership team at CCCIS headquarters in Chicago.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own and manage day‑to‑day commercial relationships for a portfolio of client accounts, serving as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor
  • Drive revenue growth by identifying and closing upsell and cross‑sell opportunities across the client portfolio, with a primary emphasis on strategic growth products
  • Develop and execute annual account plans to support consistent year‑over‑year growth, including whitespace analysis, pipeline development, and disciplined sales execution
  • Build and maintain a healthy, well‑qualified pipeline, advancing opportunities through a defined sales process and maintaining accurate forecasting and CRM hygiene
  • Partner closely with customer delivery teams to monitor client satisfaction, ensure retention, and drive measurable value realization
  • Represent the voice of the clients internally, sharing feedback to inform product innovation and go‑to‑market strategy
  • Collaborate with peers and sales leadership to share best practices and contribute to a high‑performing sales culture
  • Carry an annual ACV quota and hold accountability for revenue, pipeline, and forecast accuracy

5+ years of experience building and managing client relationships

Demonstrated success growing client accounts

The candidate must have proven experience accelerating growth within existing client accounts, including identifying expansion opportunities, deepening executive relationships, and delivering measurable results.

Demonstrated tech sales competency

The candidate should have experience operating within a defined sales methodology — building pipeline from whitespace, running structured sales plays, managing a forecast, and navigating complex, multi-stakeholder deals in a SaaS or technology environment. Candidates who have spent their careers in purely relationship or account management roles without these commercial mechanics will find this role challenging.

Experience calling on or working within the insurance industry

A strong understanding of the insurance industry is a significant plus — whether through direct domain expertise or a demonstrated track record successfully selling to or partnering with insurance clients. Familiarity with claims processes and insurance operations is particularly valuable.

Collaborative stakeholder leadership

The ideal candidate is a confident communicator who builds trust with clients, peer functions, and internal teams alike. They are skilled at navigating complex organizations and driving alignment across multiple stakeholders.

CRITICAL LEADERSHIP CAPABILITIES

Driving Results

  • Identifies new opportunities within client relationships to extend value and deepen commercial impact
  • Sets ambitious but achievable goals and holds themselves accountable to results

Acting Strategically

  • Develops and executes multi-year account plans aligned to client priorities and CCCIS growth objectives

Collaborating and Influencing

  • Serves as a credible, proactive voice for the client within the CCCIS organization

IMPORTANT PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS

jobs.excerpt: Company:Qualcomm Germany GmbHJob Area:Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Technical Standards EngineeringGeneral Summary: As a senior Technical Standards contributor and participant, you will work closely with internal and external partners to improve and evolve industry technical standards while representing Qualcomm as a delegate in standardization forums and industry organizations.
jobs.description:
Company:

General Summary:

As a senior Technical Standards contributor and participant, you will work closely with internal and external partners to improve and evolve industry technical standards while representing Qualcomm as a delegate in standardization forums and industry organizations. Your responsibility will include understanding data center industry landscapes and competitors' strength and weaknesses, collaborating with internal partners to identify existing and emerging standards for Qualcomm to focus on, help review and guide internal product requirements and specifications for conformance with the standards, and working with attorneys to file patents that protect the novel IP aspects of any inventions.

The primary focus for this role is wired connectivity infrastructure involving high-speed optical and electrical SerDes standards for core data center infrastructure. This includes the implications of solving problems across photonics, packaging, materials science, and system architecture.

Technical Focus Areas

  • Direct experience with IEEE 802.3 and OIF. Aware of related developments in other data center interconnect standards ecosystems including OCI MSA, OCP, UEC, and UALink.
  • Deep understanding of 200G, 400G and forward-looking 800G/1.6T Ethernet rate evolution, including PAM4/PAM6 modulation, FEC, equalization, channel loss, BER targets and link-budget tradeoffs.
  • Knowledge of scale-up, scale-out and scale-across data center fabrics, including electrical copper reach limits, active electrical cables, linear pluggable optics, co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and optical module architectures.
  • Strong ecosystem credibility with data center silicon, optics, connector, cable, module, switch, NIC and hyperscaler stakeholders.
  • Ability to assess competitive technology directions, identify standards gaps, and shape specifications to support Qualcomm product and IP roadmap objectives.
  • Ability to translate hyperscaler, AI accelerator, switch silicon, and optical module requirements into practical SerDes, PHY, controller and standards engagement priorities.
  • Ability to check posted technical material for accuracy and prepare internal technical material and analysis.
  • Ability to establish and play a leading role in a potential future “800G Interest Group” (or similar name) as a means to promote Qualcomm credibility and thought leadership in Data Center connectivity.

  • Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field

  • 5+ years in a technical leadership role
  • Deep understanding of data center ecosystems, including enterprise, HPC, and hyperscale environments

  • Has implemented or influenced deployable OCP-compliant platforms
  • Experience designing and developing SerDes across full lifecycle (architecture, design, implementation, verification, validation, through manufacturing and silicon qualification)
  • Knowledge of global data center market dynamics and competitive landscape

Our mission is to remove geographical borders as a barrier to equal opportunity and freedom for everyone. If we succeed, we believe this will be one of the most important tasks of our time.

Somewhere in the world right now, a SafetyWing member is messaging us. Maybe they're stuck abroad and need help fast, or they're trying to understand what their plan covers. Often the first one to answer is our AI agent, built on Intercom Fin.

We're looking for an AI Support Operations Specialist to fully own the AI agent: to make it sharper, more helpful, more human, and to keep us at the front as AI support keeps changing. You’ll own how the AI Agent performs: what it resolves, how well it resolves it, and when it hands off. You’ll also measure the difference it makes for members.

👩‍💻 What you’ll do:

Turn our AI agent into a top performer
  • Make sure our AI agent always has the most up to date information about our products, by checking with our internal policy experts
  • Look at where it succeeds, hands off or misses, find the root cause and add it to our roadmap
  • Test changes before and after launch, and keep record of what changed and what it achieved
  • Spot the next opportunities to expand the AI agent into new products and more complex support journeys
Shape how it behaves
  • Write and refine the AI agent's guidance, tone, and handoff behavior so every answer sounds like SafetyWing: warm, clear, and accurate
  • Build, test, and maintain procedures and Intercom workflows, and partner with Engineering when you need integrations or technical work
  • Make sure members reach a person smoothly whenever the AI agent isn't the right one to help
Stay ahead of AI support
  • Keep track of new Intercom capabilities and the wider AI support field
  • Separate real breakthroughs from hype, run small pilots, and recommend what we should adopt next
  • Share what you learn in a way the team can act on right away
Work with others
  • Turn your findings into clear, prioritized requests for knowledge owners, and coordinate the updates that improve the AI agent's answers
  • Work with Product, Engineering, and Compliance on bugs, data questions, and new capabilities.
  • Report on the AI agent's performance to Customer Care leadership
  • Build a feedback loop so anyone in Customer Care can flag an issue and see how it was resolved

  • Has configured and improved Intercom Fin, including Guidance, workflows, or Procedures, and can show the results
  • Writes responses that are clear, accurate, and human, and can tell when one isn't

  • Extra-shine if you have experience with data privacy, insurance or healthcare

  • Think for themselves instead of copying others
  • Are willing to try new things, even with the risk of failure
  • Are intellectually curious and open to new ideas
  • Are creative and bold in the face of any problems
  • Have strong integrity and do the right thing

  • Our own global safety net, giving you worldwide health, income, and travel coverage
  • A minimum of four weeks of vacation per year

With a growing portfolio of novel therapies, industry-leading R&D, and a goal of delivering eight breakthroughs by 2030 across major cancer types, we're translating cutting-edge science into market-shaping impact. Join us to make history — for patients, for their families, for the future.

What You Will Achieve

The US Hematology Thought Leader Engagement Lead (TLEL), will play a critical role on the growing US Hematology team by developing and executing an overarching Thought Leader engagement plan for key national and regional thought leaders in the field of Hematology. Pfizer’s Hematology portfolio spans multiple products in lymphoma, multiple myeloma and leukemia. This leader will create a first-class experience for external stakeholders in Hematology, coordinating relationships end-to-end (research to end-of-lifecycle) and working as part of a broader cross-functional Pfizer team. Focusing on National, Emerging, and certain Community Thought Leaders, this person will be responsible for establishing and maintaining relationships across a wide variety of key Hematology thought leaders.

The TLEL will be engaging Hematology Thought Leaders via 1:1 engagements at major congresses and national / regional product theaters to identify mutual points of interest between the TL and Pfizer Oncology Commercial, gathering insights on Hematology Thought Leader beliefs and preferences to inform development and execution of HCP commercial strategies / tactics, nominating TLs for Ad Boards, Speaker Programs, or other programming as requested by marketing teams, collaborating effectively with the HEME Global Thought Leader Strategy Lead, and advancing the capabilities of the Hematology franchise in the US.

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact supporting the Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program. The Senior Data Engineer will work as part of the CMM Data Modernization and Governance team responsible for delivering an integrated data governance, engineering, data platform, reporting, analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities that support operational decision-making and fulfill AO's data and analytics objectives in support of the CMM program.

The successful candidate is responsible for designing, building, testing, and maintaining scalable data engineering components and platform services that power the CMM Program. This role delivers high-quality, secure, and performant data pipelines, transformations, ETL/ELT delivery, data management solutions, and system integrations aligned with federal standards and CMM objectives for modernization, analytics, and operational excellence.
