jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive, North America
jobs.excerpt: Sonatype is the software supply chain security company.
jobs.description:
Sonatype is the software supply chain security company. Sonatype is accelerating the future of agentic software development. As developers and AI agents build faster than ever, enterprises need a new level of control, visibility, and confidence at the moment software is assembled. Our Nexus One platform helps development, security, and platform teams govern the components, dependencies, models, and artifacts that power modern applications without slowing innovation down.

We are uniquely positioned to lead this next era. Sonatype operates both Maven Central, one of the world’s largest public open source registries, and Nexus Repository, a top-ranked enterprise repository used by thousands of organizations and over 70% of the Fortune 100. With over 1 trillion downloads annually across our ecosystem, we have unmatched visibility into how software is published, consumed, and propagated. That insight helps our customers make smarter decisions earlier, reduce rework, avoid security surprises, and ship AI-powered software with greater speed and confidence.

We are seeking an exceptional Enterprise Account Executive — US to accelerate Sonatype's growth across one of the most commercially significant and competitive enterprise technology markets in North America.

This is a pure new-logo acquisition role for an accomplished enterprise hunter who thrives on creating opportunities, displacing established competitors and winning complex, high-value enterprise business.

As artificial intelligence transforms how software is developed, organisations are facing unprecedented challenges around open source security, software supply chain integrity, developer productivity and governance.

Sonatype operates at the intersection of these challenges, helping some of the world's largest organisations build and deploy software securely through industry-leading software supply chain intelligence and an integrated platform spanning repository management, application security and malware prevention.

The US West territory presents an opportunity for a commercially ambitious seller to develop strategic enterprise relationships, challenge established technology providers and build a significant new-business pipeline.

You will own a defined portfolio of enterprise prospects across the United States, with a clear mandate to identify, develop and close new-logo opportunities.

This is not an account management position, nor is it a role designed around managing an inherited customer portfolio.

Your success will be defined by the new customers you acquire, the competitive opportunities you create and the revenue you generate.

You will be expected to operate confidently against an annual quota, bringing the commercial discipline, enterprise sales experience and competitive intensity required to deliver sustained performance.

We're particularly interested in speaking with consistently high-performing enterprise sellers who have achieved President's Club, Pinnacle Club or equivalent recognition and can demonstrate repeated success in complex, competitive technology markets.

Our role in detail:

    Territory Development & Strategic New-Logo Acquisition:

    • Develop and execute a comprehensive enterprise territory strategy across an assigned portfolio of US accounts.

    • Take full accountability for new-logo acquisition, building and converting a sustainable pipeline of high-value enterprise opportunities.

    • Identify and prioritise strategic prospects based on enterprise size, software development complexity, security maturity, competitive landscape and commercial potential.

    • Build sophisticated account plans identifying organisational structures, executive stakeholders, buying committees, incumbent technology providers and potential entry points.

    • Generate significant self-sourced pipeline through proactive outbound prospecting, executive engagement, targeted account-based campaigns and strategic networking.

    • Establish relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, VP Engineering, DevSecOps, Platform Engineering and Application Security leadership.

    • Engage enterprise prospects before formal buying processes begin, helping customers recognise challenges and opportunities they may not yet be actively addressing.

    • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Engineering, Channel and executive leadership to develop coordinated account acquisition strategies.

    • Identify opportunities to position Sonatype's broader software supply chain platform through compelling customer-specific business cases.

    • Maintain strong commercial discipline around pipeline coverage, opportunity qualification, deal progression and forecasting.

      • Competitive Displacement & Enterprise Deal Execution:

      Competitive displacement will be a significant component of this role.

      We are looking for someone who understands the enterprise cybersecurity, DevSecOps and developer tooling landscape and is confident challenging established technology providers.

      You will be expected to:

      • Identify enterprise accounts using competing or incumbent software supply chain, repository management and application security technologies.

      • Develop account-specific competitive displacement strategies based on customer challenges, technical requirements and business outcomes.

      • Demonstrate a strong understanding of the competitive landscape, including organisations such as JFrog, Snyk, Black Duck, Mend, GitHub, GitLab, Checkmarx and Veracode.

      • Understand where Sonatype's intelligence, security capabilities, platform breadth and preventative approach provide meaningful customer differentiation.

      • Lead sophisticated enterprise sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders, technical evaluations, proofs of value, procurement and executive decision-making.

      • Develop strong economic buyer relationships and build compelling financial, operational and security business cases.

      • Apply structured enterprise sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC to establish clear qualification, decision criteria, competitive positioning and mutual action plans.

      • Navigate complex negotiations and commercial discussions while maintaining strong customer relationships.

      • Build internal and external champions capable of influencing enterprise purchasing decisions.

      • Demonstrate the judgement to qualify out opportunities where genuine customer value or a viable purchasing path cannot be established.

        • We want a seller who knows how to win when the customer already has a solution, not someone who only succeeds when there is no competition.

        Industry Knowledge & Technical Credibility:

        This role requires a strong understanding of the market in which Sonatype operates.

        You should be comfortable discussing how modern enterprise organisations develop, secure and deploy software, and how AI is changing the speed and complexity of those processes.

        You will:

        • Understand the commercial and technical challenges associated with open source software, software composition analysis, DevSecOps and application security.

        • Engage confidently with technical and executive buyers around software supply chain risk, developer productivity, governance and security.

        • Position Sonatype's platform capabilities across Nexus Repository, Firewall, Lifecycle and related solutions.

        • Understand how software supply chain intelligence can help organisations identify vulnerable components, prevent malicious packages entering development and make better risk decisions.

        • Translate technical capabilities into measurable business outcomes rather than relying on feature-led selling.

        • Recognise opportunities to position Sonatype as a strategic enterprise platform rather than a standalone point solution.

        • Stay informed about emerging technology, AI-assisted development, competitive market movements and evolving enterprise security requirements.

          • Channel & Cross-Functional Enterprise Selling:

          Enterprise sales success requires the ability to bring the right expertise together around the customer.

          You will:

          • Build productive relationships with regional channel partners, systems integrators and enterprise solution providers.

          • Identify partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities that support new-logo acquisition.

          • Collaborate with Sales Engineering to develop effective technical validation strategies and proofs of value.

          • Partner with Marketing on account-based campaigns, executive engagement and targeted enterprise outreach.

          • Engage executive sponsors where appropriate to support strategic opportunities.

          • Coordinate internal resources effectively while retaining clear ownership of the commercial outcome.

          • Share competitive intelligence, customer insights and market feedback to improve Sonatype's broader enterprise go-to-market execution.

            • Role Outcomes:

            Success in this role means establishing a high-performing, predictable new-logo acquisition engine across the assigned US West territory.

            You will be expected to:

            • Deliver against an annual new-business quota.

            • Consistently originate and close new enterprise customer opportunities.

            • Build a sustainable, self-generated enterprise pipeline.

            • Win strategically important competitive displacement opportunities.

            • Establish relationships with senior technology and security decision-makers across priority accounts.

            • Increase Sonatype's presence within major enterprise organisations.

            • Demonstrate strong enterprise deal qualification, commercial judgement and forecast accuracy.

            • Build effective relationships with Sales Engineering, Marketing and Channel partners.

            • Create repeatable territory development and enterprise acquisition practices that support long-term growth.

              • What Success Looks Like:

              First 30 Days — Understand, Assess & Prioritise

              You will develop a deep understanding of Sonatype's technology, competitive positioning, customer value proposition and enterprise go-to-market strategy.

              You will assess your assigned territory, identify priority accounts, evaluate competitive incumbents and develop relationships with the wider Sales, Sales Engineering, Marketing and Channel teams.

              You will begin building an evidence-based view of where the strongest new-logo opportunities exist.

              First 60 Days — Build the Acquisition Strategy

              You will have developed a prioritised territory plan, identifying target accounts, executive stakeholders, competitive displacement opportunities and clear outbound engagement strategies.

              You will be actively building relationships with prospective customers, generating qualified pipeline and coordinating account-based activity with the wider go-to-market organisation.

              Your opportunities will reflect clear customer challenges, credible buying processes and measurable business value.

              First 90 Days — Demonstrate Commercial Momentum

              You will be independently driving enterprise pursuits, demonstrating meaningful self-generated pipeline creation and establishing relationships with key decision-makers.

              You will be progressing opportunities through technical validation, commercial discovery and structured enterprise qualification.

              Your territory plan, pipeline coverage and forecasting will provide leadership with confidence in your approach to delivering against quota.

              First 12 Months — Deliver High Performance

              You will have established a sustainable enterprise acquisition engine and demonstrated the ability to deliver against a quota circa $1.5-2m.

              You will have acquired new enterprise customers, progressed competitive displacement opportunities and built a strong forward-looking pipeline.

              You will be recognised for your commercial judgement, proactive hunting mentality, enterprise customer credibility and ability to win complex opportunities.

              Who You Are:

              You are an accomplished enterprise technology sales professional with a demonstrable track record of acquiring new customers, exceeding ambitious revenue targets and winning in highly competitive markets.

              You are a hunter by nature, motivated by opening doors, creating opportunities and winning business that would otherwise remain with a competitor.

              Essential Experience & Capabilities

              Proven Enterprise New-Business Performance

              • Demonstrated success carrying and achieving substantial enterprise new-business quotas, ideally around $2 million annually or at a comparable level of commercial complexity.

              • A track record of consistent quota attainment and strong new-logo acquisition.

              • Evidence of personally originating, developing and closing complex enterprise opportunities.

              • Ability to quantify pipeline creation, average contract values, competitive wins and revenue performance.

                • Consistent High Performance

                • A history of operating among the strongest performers within your sales organisation.

                • President's Club, Pinnacle Club or equivalent recognition is particularly attractive.

                • Evidence of sustained performance across multiple sales periods, rather than reliance on one exceptional transaction or favourable territory.

                  • Competitive Enterprise Selling

                  • Proven experience winning business against established technology providers.

                  • Ability to develop differentiated competitive strategies and challenge incumbent solutions.

                  • Strong negotiation, executive engagement and commercial deal leadership skills.

                    • Enterprise Territory Development

                    • Experience developing a geographic or named-account territory through proactive outbound activity.

                    • Strong account prioritisation, stakeholder mapping and territory planning.

                    • Ability to generate your own pipeline rather than relying predominantly on inbound demand.

                      • Technical & Industry Understanding

                      • Strong familiarity with cybersecurity, DevSecOps, application security, developer tooling, cloud infrastructure or adjacent enterprise technology.

                      • Confidence engaging technical and executive stakeholders in complex buying environments.

                      • Ability to translate sophisticated technical capabilities into clear commercial value.

                        • Sales Methodology & Commercial Discipline

                        • Experience applying structured enterprise qualification methodologies such as MEDDPICC.

                        • Strong forecasting, opportunity management and pipeline discipline.

                        • Ability to manage complex enterprise opportunities involving multiple stakeholders, technical evaluations and procurement processes.

                          • Preferred Experience:

                          We would particularly welcome candidates with experience from:

                          • Software supply chain security and software composition analysis.

                          • Application security and DevSecOps platforms.

                          • Repository management and developer infrastructure.

                          • Enterprise cybersecurity and cloud-native security.

                          • Enterprise platform selling and competitive displacement.

                          • Global 2000, Fortune 500 or similarly complex enterprise customers.

                          • Working with channel partners and enterprise systems integrators.

                          • Selling across the US West technology and enterprise ecosystem.

                          • Consumption-based, platform-led or land-and-expand commercial models.

  • 2025 AI Compliance Solution of the Year - AI Breakthrough Awards

  • 2025 DEVIES Award to our SBOM Manager new product for its innovation and impact in developer technology

Company Overview
Our client is a fast-growing, venture-backed SaaS company helping frontline workers access life-changing benefits like childcare, elder care, and nutrition assistance. Their AI-powered platform connects employees to available government programs—cutting through complexity and delivering support where it matters most.

Used by major retailers, healthcare providers, and Fortune 500 companies, the product is trusted to handle sensitive workflows in regulated environments. The fully remote team is mission-driven, pragmatic, and growing quickly, with strong enterprise backing and a clear expansion path.

Your Role

This is not a “run the test plan someone else wrote” role. Until now, engineers have checked their own releases. The product has grown into a web app, connections to outside systems and AI chat features, so each release now needs someone who can say whether it’s ready, with evidence. New federal Medicaid rules start January 1, 2027, and the team is building tools that help states keep eligible people covered through them. You’ll start by building the automated tests and the ready-to-ship check for the releases closest to that date. It’s a hands-on, senior seat with no direct reports. You decide where the risk is, which team needs you most, and what “done” means.

You’ll:

  • Test strategy and automation

    • Decide where the product is most likely to break and what gets tested first

    • Build end-to-end journeys, a smoke suite on every build, and integration tests in code engineers review and keep

    • Pick the tools and run everything in GitHub Actions

  • Release verdicts

    • Give engineers a “ready / not ready” note before each release: what passed, what failed, what nobody checked

    • Write a plain-language summary for non-engineers of what’s verified, and push back on a risky date with evidence

  • Testing inside delivery teams

    • Sit with customer-facing teams and test features while they’re being built, moving between teams as workload shifts

    • Set a shared definition of “done” and coach engineers on testing their own work

  • Web app, services and outside systems

    • Run functional, regression and accessibility tests across browsers and devices, and check each customer’s configuration

    • Test APIs and asynchronous flows between services, and write contract tests for outside systems

    • Make sure the product behaves sensibly when a dependency is slow, down or returns wrong data

  • AI chat features

    • Build evaluation suites with golden datasets for chatbots and assistants, rerun them on every prompt or model change, and test guardrails

    • Use AI tools to write, maintain and triage tests

  • Test data and security

    • Seed realistic test data for a complex system, inside strict access and data-protection rules

    • Help find and fix security vulnerabilities in the app and its infrastructure

You Bring:

  • 5+ years in quality, test or software engineering, with automation you wrote yourself, running in CI and kept by other engineers

  • At least one test practice you built from a low baseline: you chose the tools, wrote the first suites, wired them into CI, and can explain what you left untested

  • Strong test code in Python or TypeScript across API, browser and pipeline, including headless browser runs and integration tests for failing dependencies

  • Experience testing business rules you had to learn first: you read the policy, found the gaps, and wrote tests from the answers

  • Experience as the only quality person across several teams, setting your own priorities with no backlog handed to you

  • Clear written updates for engineers and non-engineers alike, including the confidence to challenge a deadline with facts

What’s Offered

  • Fully remote across the U.S., with live collaboration during U.S. business hours

  • Full-time, permanent seat (about 40 hours a week)

  • Competitive USD compensation (bring your target to the first call)

  • Real authority: you define the testing strategy, the automation and what “good” looks like

  • An engineering buddy to help you get set up from day one

  • Direct impact: your work helps families get and keep the benefits they’re eligible for

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Engineer
jobs.excerpt: As a Revenue Operations Engineer at vCluster Labs, you aren't just keeping the CRM tidy; you are building the automated engine that tells our sellers which accounts matter and why.
jobs.description:
As a Revenue Operations Engineer at vCluster Labs, you aren't just keeping the CRM tidy; you are building the automated engine that tells our sellers which accounts matter and why. You will design Clay pipelines, enrichment workflows, and AI agents that surface the right accounts to sales and SDRs, and you will make sure they keep working long after launch. You own the GTM stack for our EMEA team, from Salesforce workflows to the integrations that tie HubSpot, Notion, and Slack together.

As a Revenue Operations Engineer, your role will include:

  • Account intelligence and enrichment: You will build and extend Clay tables, enrichment, and discovery pipelines that find new accounts and surface the right ones to sales and SDRs. You will push the tool well past its current setup and get the full value out of it.

  • AI agents and automation: You will turn manual GTM workflows into automated ones using agents in Clay, Salesforce, and Claude. You build them to run end to end and stay useful, not to demo once and break a month later.

  • Data quality that stays clean: You will design repeatable processes that keep account and contact data accurate over time. When a cleanup happens, it happens once, and the workflow behind it prevents the mess from coming back.

  • Scoring and top-of-funnel signals: You will own account and MQL funnel scoring and the signal workflows that route intent to the right seller at the right time.

  • Systems and integrations: You will build Salesforce workflows and maintain integrations across Salesforce, HubSpot, Momentum, Chili Piper, Notion, and Slack. When a new tool or feature beats what we built six months ago, you will make the call to replace it.

  • EMEA RevOps support: You will own the RevOps ticket queue during EMEA hours, partnering with our US-based RevOps teammate for follow-the-sun coverage. That includes helping reps with live opportunity questions, not only systems work.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Hands-on Clay experience: You have built Clay tables, enrichment waterfalls, and pipelines yourself, and can explain what you would build next.

  • Salesforce depth: You can build Salesforce flows and automation, not just run reports. HubSpot fluency is expected alongside it.

  • AI-forward building: You have built AI agents or automations that run in production, using tools like Claude, Clay agents, or Salesforce automation, and you can show what they do today.

  • Systems thinking for GTM: You understand how scoring, routing, enrichment, and CRM hygiene connect, and you design for the whole loop rather than one fix.

  • EMEA-based and self-directed: You are based in EMEA, comfortable owning a queue without a teammate in your time zone, and you decide what to fix next without waiting to be told.

Bonus points for:

  • Salesforce Admin certification: Or equivalent admin-level experience owning an org.

  • Code and CLI comfort: Experience with scripting, APIs, the Claude CLI, or MCP integrations.

  • Startup scaling experience: You have helped a company grow from Series A toward later stage and built the systems that growth needed.

  • Advanced Clay or Anthropic tooling: You are the person others ask when they want to know what Clay or Claude can actually do.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

Compensation Range: £75K - £95K

Who We Are Seeking

This person will be expected to own the success of their region from both a revenue and go-to-market perspective. The ideal candidate understands modern infrastructure and can sell across multiple lines of business—not simply into one technical team.   • Identify strategic regional events, partners, communities, and customer relationships that can help accelerate Spectro Cloud's market presence.

  • Serve as the voice of the region back to Sales, Marketing, Product, and executive leadership.

What You Will Sell

You will position Spectro Cloud's portfolio across a broad set of enterprise infrastructure and AI initiatives, including:

  • Enterprise Kubernetes management

  • Hybrid and multi-cloud infrastructure

  • Virtualization modernization

  • VMware alternatives and modernization initiatives

  • Data center modernization

  • Edge and distributed computing

  • Platform engineering

  • GPU infrastructure

  • AI infrastructure

  • AI workload orchestration

  • Infrastructure efficiency and economics

  • Tokenomics and AI inference economics

You will be expected to uncover opportunities across multiple lines of business and connect Spectro Cloud capabilities to broader enterprise transformation initiatives.

Strategic Selling

This is not a role where pipeline is simply handed to you.

Successful candidates know how to create a market within their territory and build opportunities from the ground up.

You will be expected to:

  • Proactively create pipeline within strategic enterprise accounts.

  • Identify and develop multiple strong internal champions.

  • Drive late-stage opportunities with urgency, accountability, and clear next steps.

  • Maintain disciplined forecasting and demonstrate complete command of your business.

Channel & Partner Leadership

Channel success is an important component of this role.

You will:

  • Build strong relationships with strategic channel partners throughout the region.

  • Identify partners that can open doors into targeted enterprise accounts.

  • Develop joint GTM strategies and account plans with key partners.

  • Create and manage partner-generated pipeline.

  • Work with VARs, systems integrators, cloud providers, OEMs, and technology partners.

  • Help partners understand how Spectro Cloud fits into infrastructure modernization, Kubernetes, virtualization, GPU, and AI initiatives.

  • Coordinate partner, customer, and Spectro Cloud resources to accelerate strategic opportunities.

  • Hold partners accountable while making Spectro Cloud a company they want to bring into their most important accounts.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of successful enterprise technology sales experience.

  • Proven success selling complex infrastructure technology into large enterprise organizations.

  • Consistent history of meeting or exceeding quota.

  • Strong new-logo acquisition experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to build a territory rather than simply manage an existing book of business.

Why Spectro Cloud

Enterprise infrastructure is undergoing one of its largest transformations in decades.

Kubernetes, virtualization modernization, distributed infrastructure, GPU computing, and AI are converging and changing how organizations design, deploy, and operate technology.

Spectro Cloud sits at the center of that transformation.

ABOUT KLED

Kled is building the largest opt-in human data network in the world.

We are not a labeling firm. We are not a task marketplace.

We are a consumer application where people upload their real photos, videos, and documents and get paid continuously.

We then filter, standardize, and license that data to frontier AI labs and enterprises that need fresh, rights-aware training data.

Since launching our mobile app in 2026, we have:

• Reached #1 on the App Store (Finance) with 0 paid marketing
• Scaled to 600,000+ active data contributors

• Processed 5M uploads per day

• Raised $15M+ from investors behind SpaceX, Airbnb, Coinbase, xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Spotify, Lyft, Uber, and more

Our mission is to let anyone download the app and earn a real living wage from uploading their data.

This listing is for one paid task in the Kled app: "Narrate What You Are Doing While You Do It". There is no interview and no minimum hours: download the app, open the task, and you are paid per accepted submission.

What you will do

Film any everyday task with your hands in shot, and say out loud what you're doing as you do it.

Steps

  1. Prop your phone or hang it round your neck so your hands are in shot

  2. Start recording in Kled and begin the task

  3. Say what you are doing as you do it, 'now I'm loosening this screw', 'this bit always sticks'

  4. Keep going to the end without stopping the recording

  5. Upload

What gets rejected

  • Do not narrate afterwards, talk while you work

  • Do not stop and restart the recording

  • Do not film with your hands out of shot

  • Do not read from a script

Accepted: One unbroken take, hands visible throughout, continuous speech describing the action as it happens.

Pay

$2.60 per accepted clip. At a typical pace of about 7 minutes per clip, that is about $22 per hour. A 20-minute session of about 3 clips pays about $7.80. One clip of 3 to 5 minutes per submission. You are paid per accepted submission (piecework, independent contractor); submissions that break the rules are not paid. Payouts are made in the app (PayPal, Venmo or a Solana wallet).

Where and when

Open worldwide: the task runs in 100+ countries. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

What you need

  • An iPhone running iOS 18.6 or later (the Kled app is iPhone-only right now)

  • 18 or older

  • Somewhere to prop your phone so it sees your hands and the work

How to start

  1. Download Kled from the App Store: (also at kled.ai/app).

  2. Create your account and open Tasks.

  3. Search "Narrate What You Are Doing While You Do It", read the brief and follow the on-screen steps.

  4. Submit. Accepted submissions are paid in the app.

Every submission is reviewed, and you opt in to a commercial training license on each upload; accepted submissions are licensed to AI labs. Questions: .

jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Endpoint Engineer to develop, maintain, deploy, and support standardized endpoint capabilities for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This position supports endpoint images, application packaging, device provisioning, software deployment, patching, configuration baselines, and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure.

The Endpoint Engineer supports physical and virtual endpoints throughout their lifecycle, including testing, deployment, configuration, patching, troubleshooting, refresh, recovery, and retirement. The engineer works with the Senior Endpoint Engineer and other technical teams to deliver secure, consistent, and supportable endpoint services across USMEPCOM Headquarters, MEPS, Remote Processing Substations, COOP locations, and remote-user environments.

This role maintains a clear division of responsibility with Task 6 cybersecurity personnel. Task 6 identifies, prioritizes, and validates security findings. The Endpoint Engineer evaluates assigned findings, tests the approved correction, implements the operational change through established change-control procedures, and provides deployment evidence for cybersecurity validation.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Occasional after-hours maintenance, incident response, on-site support, or travel may be required.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Endpoint Engineer will:

  • Develop, test, maintain, and document standardized endpoint images.
  • Maintain image components, operating-system settings, drivers, firmware dependencies, security baselines, required software, and deployment configurations.
  • Support image versioning, testing, approval, release, rollback, and retirement processes.
  • Validate endpoint images for functionality, compatibility, security, performance, and operational readiness.
  • Develop and maintain automated device-deployment task sequences, provisioning workflows, enrollment processes, and configuration profiles.
  • Support endpoint deployment using approved Microsoft and Government management platforms.
  • Administer approved endpoint-management capabilities involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Configuration Manager, Windows Autopilot, or comparable technologies.
  • Develop, test, maintain, and deploy application packages.
  • Package commercial, Government, and internally developed software using approved formats and standards.
  • Develop installation, detection, dependency, requirement, upgrade, repair, and removal logic.
  • Test application packages for silent installation, accurate detection, compatibility, security, and clean removal.
  • Troubleshoot package failures, dependency problems, application conflicts, detection errors, and deployment issues.
  • Develop approved scripts and automation for provisioning, packaging, configuration, deployment, validation, and remediation.
  • Maintain endpoint-management scripts and configurations in approved documentation and version-control repositories.
  • Support patching of endpoint operating systems, applications, drivers, firmware, and management components.
  • Configure and maintain pilot groups, deployment rings, production waves, maintenance windows, deadlines, and exception processes.
  • Test operating-system updates, security patches, vendor patches, and application updates before production deployment.
  • Monitor patch and deployment progress, failure rates, compliance status, endpoint health, and approved exceptions.
  • Investigate failed patches and coordinate corrective actions, redeployment, rollback, or exception documentation.
  • Engineer and support Virtual Desktop Infrastructure capabilities.
  • Develop and maintain VDI base images, desktop pools, application delivery, user-profile configurations, and endpoint-access policies.
  • Troubleshoot VDI login, profile, application, display, performance, peripheral, and connectivity problems.
  • Support VDI refreshes, upgrades, capacity activities, deployment, testing, and optimization.
  • Coordinate VDI dependencies with virtualization, storage, network, identity, application, and cybersecurity teams.
  • Support endpoint deployment and refresh projects across geographically dispersed USMEPCOM locations.
  • Assist with device provisioning, enrollment, configuration, testing, deployment, replacement, recovery, and retirement.
  • Support operating-system upgrades, application migrations, technology refreshes, and endpoint-management transitions.
  • Provide advanced engineering support for complex endpoint, image, application-packaging, deployment, patching, and VDI incidents.
  • Analyze endpoint logs, deployment status, policy results, management-platform data, and other technical evidence.
  • Support root-cause analysis and implement approved corrective actions for recurring endpoint incidents.
  • Assist with major incidents and outages involving endpoint management, software deployments, VDI, or widespread device failures.
  • Implement approved workarounds and restoration actions during endpoint-related incidents.
  • Coordinate with the Service Desk and field-support teams to improve troubleshooting, escalation, and knowledge content.
  • Develop technical guidance for common endpoint, packaging, deployment, patching, and VDI problems.
  • Review cybersecurity findings assigned to endpoint operations by Task 6.
  • Assess operational impact, dependencies, testing requirements, deployment approach, and rollback requirements.
  • Test and implement approved endpoint security changes through established change and release procedures.
  • Execute assigned remediation involving endpoint images, software versions, patches, configurations, policies, or management settings.
  • Track the affected endpoint population, deployment status, failures, exceptions, and completion results.
  • Provide remediation and completion evidence to Task 6 for validation.
  • Coordinate unresolved remediation issues with cybersecurity personnel, vendors, system owners, and Government stakeholders.
  • Apply approved endpoint-security baselines and DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides.
  • Support endpoint compliance reporting, configuration validation, vulnerability remediation, and audit-evidence collection.
  • Maintain endpoint inventories, deployment records, image documentation, software-package records, patch status, VDI records, and configuration baselines.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, packaging instructions, test plans, deployment plans, rollback procedures, and recovery documentation.
  • Follow approved incident, problem, change, release, configuration, asset, security, and quality-management processes.
  • Provide endpoint health, deployment, patching, compliance, risk, and issue information for program reporting.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience where permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • Minimum of six years of relevant experience in endpoint engineering, systems engineering, device management, desktop engineering, VDI engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Experience developing or maintaining enterprise endpoint images.
  • Experience developing, testing, and deploying application packages.
  • Experience supporting endpoint provisioning, deployment, patching, configuration, and lifecycle management.
  • Experience engineering or supporting Virtual Desktop Infrastructure.
  • Experience implementing assigned endpoint-security or vulnerability-remediation changes.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex endpoint, packaging, deployment, patching, or VDI issues.
  • Knowledge of controlled testing, pilot deployment, phased implementation, validation, rollback, and change-management practices.
  • Ability to maintain image documentation, software-package records, test plans, deployment plans, rollback procedures, and completion evidence.
  • Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate certification when relevant to the assigned Microsoft 365 or Intune environment.
  • Ability to support after-hours maintenance, deployment windows, critical incidents, and endpoint recovery when required.
  • Strong written, verbal, analytical, and technical problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • Experience with Microsoft Intune or Microsoft Endpoint Manager.
  • Experience with Microsoft Configuration Manager or System Center Configuration Manager.
  • Experience with Windows Autopilot and modern device provisioning.
  • Experience with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
  • Experience with Microsoft Entra ID and hybrid endpoint management.
  • Experience with PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or comparable endpoint-automation technologies.
  • Experience packaging applications using MSI, MSIX, Win32, App-V, or comparable formats.
  • Experience with VMware Horizon, Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, Citrix, or another enterprise VDI platform.
  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense endpoint environments.
  • Experience applying DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides to Windows endpoints.
  • Experience supporting Risk Management Framework controls, vulnerability remediation, or authorization evidence.
  • Experience with endpoint analytics, compliance, configuration-management, or digital employee-experience tools.
  • Experience supporting large-scale operating-system migrations, device refreshes, or endpoint-management modernization.
  • CompTIA Security+ or another relevant security certification.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification.
  • Relevant Microsoft, VMware, Citrix, cloud, automation, or endpoint-management certification.

Skills and Competencies

  • Enterprise endpoint engineering and support.
  • Image development and automated deployment.
  • Application packaging and software distribution.
  • Operating-system and application patch management.
  • Endpoint security-baseline implementation.
  • VDI configuration, deployment, and troubleshooting.
  • PowerShell and endpoint-management automation.
  • Complex troubleshooting and root-cause analysis.
  • Controlled testing, phased deployment, and rollback execution.
  • Cybersecurity remediation and evidence development.
  • Technical documentation and configuration management.
  • Cross-functional engineering coordination.
  • Strong attention to detail and change discipline.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

jobs.description:
About the role

We are seeking a proactive, technically strong Backend Developer to keep a live, business-critical microservices platform healthy while delivering meaningful improvements on top of it.

This is a hands-on role with a high degree of autonomy: you’ll take a bug report or change request, investigate it across the codebase, and see it through to production. You’ll balance production support with feature engineering, backed by a supportive team, and we’re embracing agentic development with AI coding agents to ship efficiently without compromising quality.

Key responsibilities

  • Resolve production issues: Triage, diagnose, and resolve issues across distributed microservices, tracing a request from the user-facing API down to the services that talk to external systems.
  • Support incident response: Investigate root causes, apply fixes, add regression tests, and document findings so issues don’t recur
  • Deliver enhancements: Build improvements to existing services, including new versions of certification programs, scorecard and scoring changes, payment adjustments, and integration updates
  • Work within the architecture: Follow established patterns and shared internal libraries in a layered service architecture, from the API gateway through the business logic services down to the adapters that integrate with external systems
  • Maintain integrations: Maintain and extend integrations with external platforms for performance data, CRM, enterprise resource planning (ERP), payment processing, email, and cloud file storage
  • Manage data changes: Write and update database migration scripts and investigate data-related production issues carefully against live data
  • Partner with QA and product: Answer testers’ questions, clarify expected behavior, help reproduce issues, and support verification so fixes and features can be signed off smoothly. Ask product clarifying questions early and confirm intent and edge cases
  • Improve observability and documentation: Contribute structured logging, masking of sensitive data, and clearer production visibility, and take part in code review while keeping documentation current as the platform grows

Required qualifications

  • Proven ability to take ownership of a problem from start to finish, from initial bug report or change request through to a tested, deployed solution
  • Production experience building and maintaining backend services with Node.js and TypeScript
  • Strong experience with NestJS (or a comparable structured backend framework), including modules, controllers, services, dependency injection, and middleware
  • Solid REST/HTTP fundamentals, including service-to-service communication, API contracts, versioning, and error handling
  • Comfortable with relational databases, writing and reviewing PostgreSQL queries, and safe migration practices
  • Experience debugging distributed systems where a single feature spans several services, reading logs and metrics to find root causes rather than symptoms
  • Sound judgment about risk, including the difference between a safe local fix and a change that calls for a rollout plan, particularly for payments, authentication, and live data
  • Experience integrating third-party systems (payment providers, CRMs, ERPs, identity providers) behind a clean internal interface
  • Understanding of authentication patterns: OAuth 2.0, JWT verification, single sign-on (SSO), and service-to-service (machine-to-machine) authentication
  • Comfortable with agentic development, using AI coding agents and tooling to investigate, build, and ship work efficiently while keeping a careful eye on quality
  • Ability to write tests that confirm fixes and prevent regressions
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including clear status updates, incident notes, pull request descriptions, and documentation others can act on

Nice to have

  • Experience supporting a platform through the transition from active build to maintenance-and-enhancement mode
  • Familiarity with adapter patterns that isolate external systems from core business logic
  • Experience with webhook-driven integrations, including verifying signatures, scoped service-to-service authorization, and safely handling repeated inbound events
  • Familiarity with containers and orchestration (Docker and Kubernetes) and services deployed on a major cloud provider such as AWS
  • Experience with observability practices such as structured logging and masking of sensitive data

jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD101464

Senior Finance Business Partner, AOS Finance

L'affichage de poste en français suivra / The French job posting follows


Position Overview

One of the adjacencies that Autodesk is expanding into is Operations, by extending our AI-powered clouds into the entire lifecycle of buildings, factories and infrastructure. Autodesk Operations Solutions (AOS) is the group building that business, and it will grow through both organic investment and acquisition.

We're hiring a Senior Finance Business Partner to join the AOS finance team to help build and grow this business into a significant part of Autodesk’s portfolio. You'll report to the Director of AOS Finance and work with the AOS leadership team. You'll partner with AOS leaders on planning, forecasting, and financial insights, and you'll support the financial modeling for M&A opportunities and the integration of acquired companies into Autodesk.

You'll influence senior leaders on strategic, investment, and operational decisions through financial analysis. You're comfortable with ambiguity, you adapt quickly, and you solve problems across cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

  • Business partnering. Advise the AOS leadership team on investment trade-offs, resource prioritization, and ROI. Prepare quarterly business reviews and executive and Board materials that turn the numbers into a clear message.
  • Financial analysis and modeling. Develop financial analyses and models to influence business decisions (pricing & packaging for subscription and consumption models, business cases, etc.)
  • Planning and forecasting. Run annual plan, quarterly and monthly forecasts, and long-range model for ARR, ACV, revenue, headcount, and expense.
  • M&A financial modeling. Build and own financial models for acquisition, partnership, and build-versus-buy opportunities, including scenario and sensitivity analysis. Support projections for acquisition targets, including expansion, retention, pricing, and synergies. Partner with Corporate Development, and AOS leadership on the business case and financial due diligence.
  • Post-close integration. Lead the FP&A workstream for newly acquired companies: align financial structure, ARR and other metric definitions, and reporting; bring the acquired team into Autodesk's planning and forecast cadence; and report integration progress and deal performance against the original thesis to leadership.
  • Topline reporting and analysis. Develop and report on topline financial metrics to measure financial performance. Analyze financial results, distilling/synthesizing key trends
  • Spend management. Track AOS spend and headcount against plan, explain variances, and support the business on budget management.
  • Process and tooling. Improve the models, reporting, and automation that AOS finance relies on, and make acquired-company data easier to onboard each time. Look for practical ways to use AI to speed up analysis, reporting, and forecasting

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in financial planning & analysis, strategic finance, investment banking, or management consulting, ideally including time at a software company
  • Proven ability to influence and collaborate with cross functional leaders, including senior executives
  • Advanced financial modeling skills including experience building M&A financial models
  • Strong experience with SaaS metrics and revenue modeling (ARR, retention, bookings and billings, pricing and packaging); consumption-based model experience a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with a knack for distilling complexity into executive ready insights
  • Experience working in a global, matrixed environment
  • Solution-driven, innovative, and creative mindset
  • Proven track record of financial systems, process & tools improvement/automation
  • Curiosity about AI and an interest in using it to improve how finance works
  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, accounting, economics; MBA preferred

Partenaire d’affaires principal en finance, AOS Finance


Aperçu du poste

L’un des secteurs connexes dans lesquels Autodesk se développe est celui des opérations, en étendant nos solutions cloud basées sur l’IA à l’ensemble du cycle de vie des bâtiments, des usines et des infrastructures. Autodesk Operations Solutions (AOS) est le groupe chargé de développer cette activité, qui se renforcera à la fois par des investissements organiques et par des acquisitions.

Nous recherchons un partenaire d’affaires principal en finances pour rejoindre l’équipe financière d’AOS afin de contribuer à l’établissement et à la croissance de cette activité, qui deviendra un élément important du portefeuille d’Autodesk. Vous relèverez du directeur des finances d’AOS et travaillerez avec l’équipe de direction d’AOS. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants d’AOS en matière de planification, de prévisions et d’analyses financières, et vous contribuerez à l’élaboration de modèles financiers pour les occasions de fusion et d’acquisition ainsi qu’à l’intégration des entreprises acquises au sein d’Autodesk.

Vous influencerez les hauts dirigeants dans leurs décisions stratégiques, d’investissement et opérationnelles grâce à vos analyses financières. Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’ambiguïté, vous vous adaptez rapidement et vous résolvez des problèmes au sein d’équipes interfonctionnelles.


Responsabilités

  • Partenariat d’affaires. Conseiller l’équipe de direction d’AOS sur les compromis en matière d’investissement, la hiérarchisation des ressources et le rendement du capital investi (RCI). Préparer des revues d’affaires trimestrielles ainsi que des documents destinés à la haute direction et au conseil d’administration qui transforment les chiffres en un message clair.
  • Analyse et modélisation financières. Élaborer des analyses et des modèles financiers pour orienter les décisions d’affaires (tarification et offres pour les modèles d’abonnement et de consommation, analyses de rentabilité, etc.)
  • Planification et prévisions. Établir le plan annuel, les prévisions trimestrielles et mensuelles, ainsi qu’un modèle à long terme pour le chiffre d’affaires récurrent annuel (ARR), la valeur contractuelle annuelle (ACV), les revenus, l’effectif et les dépenses.
  • Modélisation financière des fusions et acquisitions. Élaborer et gérer des modèles financiers pour les acquisitions, les partenariats et les opportunités « faire soi-même ou acheter », y compris des analyses de scénarios et de sensibilité. Appuyer les projections relatives aux cibles d’acquisition, notamment en matière d’expansion, de fidélisation, de tarification et de synergies. Collaborer avec le service de développement d’entreprise et la direction d’AOS sur l’analyse de rentabilité et la vérification financière préalable.
  • Intégration post-clôture. Diriger le volet FP&A pour les entreprises nouvellement acquises : harmoniser la structure financière, les définitions de l’ARR et d’autres indicateurs, ainsi que le reporting; intégrer l’équipe acquise au rythme de planification et de prévision d’Autodesk; et rendre compte à la direction des progrès de l’intégration et de la performance de la transaction par rapport à l’hypothèse initiale.
  • Rapports et analyses des résultats financiers globaux. Élaborer et présenter des rapports sur les indicateurs financiers globaux afin de mesurer la performance financière. Analyser les résultats financiers, en identifiant et en synthétisant les tendances clés
  • Gestion des dépenses. Suivre les dépenses et l’effectif d’AOS par rapport au plan, expliquer les écarts et soutenir l’entreprise dans la gestion budgétaire.
  • Processus et outils. Améliorer les modèles, les rapports et l’automatisation sur lesquels s’appuie le service des finances d’AOS, et faciliter l’intégration des données des entreprises acquises à chaque fois. Rechercher des moyens pratiques d’utiliser l’IA pour accélérer l’analyse, la production de rapports et les prévisions

Qualifications Minimales

  • Au moins 8 ans d’expérience en planification et analyse financières, en finance stratégique, en services bancaires d’investissement ou en conseil en gestion, idéalement avec une expérience au sein d’une entreprise de logiciels
  • Capacité avérée à influencer et à collaborer avec des dirigeants de divers secteurs fonctionnels, y compris des cadres supérieurs
  • Compétences avancées en modélisation financière, y compris une expérience dans l’élaboration de modèles financiers liés aux fusions et acquisitions
  • Solide expérience des indicateurs SaaS et de la modélisation des revenus (ARR, fidélisation, prises de commandes et facturation, tarification et offres); une expérience des modèles basés sur la consommation constitue un atout
  • Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et verbale, avec un talent particulier pour transformer des informations complexes en aperçus clairs et prêts à être présentés à la haute direction
  • Expérience de travail dans un environnement international et matriciel
  • Esprit axé sur les solutions, innovant et créatif
  • Expérience avérée en matière d’amélioration et d’automatisation des systèmes, des processus et des outils financiers
  • Curiosité à l’égard de l’IA et intérêt pour son utilisation afin d’améliorer le fonctionnement des services financiers
  • Baccalauréat en finance, en administration des affaires, en comptabilité ou en économie; un MBA est un atout

Learn More

About Autodesk

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Salary transparency

Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For Canada based roles, we expect a starting base salary between $116,000 and $169,400. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Belonging

We are not a labeling firm. We are not a task marketplace.

What you will do

Paste in something you wrote badly first, then your improved version, an email, a message, a caption, an application. Then say what you changed.

Steps

  1. Paste an early draft of something you wrote

  2. Paste your improved version

  3. Explain what you changed and why it is better

  4. Submit

  • Do not submit pairs that differ only by a typo

  • Do not skip the explanation

Accepted: A before version, an after version, and a written reason for the changes.

Pay

You are paid per accepted submission (piecework, independent contractor); submissions that break the rules are not paid. Payouts are made in the app (PayPal, Venmo or a Solana wallet).

Where and when

Open worldwide: the task runs in 100+ countries. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

What you need

  • An iPhone running iOS 18.6 or later (the Kled app is iPhone-only right now)

  • 18 or older

  • Your own writing, typed in the app

How to start

  1. Download Kled from the App Store: (also at kled.ai/app).

  4. Submit. Accepted submissions are paid in the app.

jobs.description:
About ShareGate

ShareGate is the leading Microsoft 365 migration and governance platform, trusted by over 100,000 IT pros for its unmatched simplicity.

It offers the simplest, most reliable, and most affordable way to move business data to Microsoft 365.

Whether migrating from Google Workspace, file shares, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, or tenant-to-tenant, ShareGate gets the job done, without surprises. From cloud transformation to M&A integration, it keeps things just damn simple.

ShareGate also helps organizations stay in control once their data is migrated. Its powerful governance features let users assess environments, uncover issues, and apply fixes on the spot, so everything stays clean, secure, and optimized. It lays the groundwork for safe Microsoft Copilot deployment within organizations.

ShareGate is developed by Workleap Technologies, a Montréal‑based software company.

Your role

You will own how Workleap detects, investigates and responds to threats across Workleap and ShareGate, and you will build the AI layer that runs it. Our security tooling generates more noise than a small team can work, and too many findings are ambiguous or wrong. This role exists now to turn detection and response into a system where agents triage, enrich and investigate, and people make the calls that genuinely need judgment. It is a hands on Staff individual contributor role with no direct reports.

Your impact:

  • Build the pipeline that runs security operations end to end: integrations that pull alerts and findings out of every source tool, an agentic system that triages, enriches, correlates and drafts the investigation, and a connection into Jira that routes each result to the owning team with evidence and a fix path, so no finding is ever copied by hand.
  • Define the trust model for those agents, deciding what they close alone, what they recommend and what always goes to a human, backed by evals and secured against prompt injection and permission abuse.
  • Drive false positives and misrated findings out of our security tooling, so every finding that reaches a person is real and correctly prioritized.
  • Own detection engineering end to end, written as code and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, so coverage survives any change of platform.
  • Lead security incident response from triage to postmortem, with agents gathering the evidence, and hold our managed detection partner to a measurable standard.
  • Make security a partner developers want to work with, delivering findings in their workflow with clear evidence and a fix path.

Your team

Over the next 12 months, LeapSec is delivering two strategic bets: putting security inside product squads, with agents carrying vulnerability and detection work, and automating SOC 2 evidence so nobody gathers it by hand. You will own the detection and response side of that work: cleaning up the tooling, building the agents, and proving how much they can be trusted to do alone.

LeapSec covers Security Operations and Compliance across Workleap and ShareGate. You will report to the Director of Infrastructure and Security and work daily with our Staff Application Security Specialist and security tooling team, and as needed with Infrastructure, ITX and product engineering. We are a small team with a wide mandate: we track work honestly in Jira, deliver on fixed dates, and expect people to own outcomes end to end.

Our environment is Azure first, with a cloud native SIEM and XDR stack, Zscaler, Cloudflare and a managed detection partner today. We choose tools on merit and expect to keep choosing.

What you'll bring

  • 7+ years in security operations, incident response or detection engineering, with recent hands on time in a cloud SaaS environment;
  • Deep experience working findings that are not clean: validating what tooling flags, tuning false positives out at the source, and deciding with incomplete evidence whether something is real;
  • Years of working directly with developers, getting fixes shipped without authority and keeping the relationship intact when the answer is no;
  • Built and shipped agent systems for security work that others depend on, such as MCP servers, Claude skills, subagents or custom tools, with evals that decide when the output is trusted;
  • A working model of how agentic systems fail and get attacked, including prompt injection, tool permission scoping and credential handling;
  • Detection engineering as a discipline: detections as code, a SIEM query language you write fluently, and false positive rates you actually measure;
  • Strong grasp of identity and cloud attack paths, ideally in Azure and Entra ID;
  • Bonus: experience directing a managed detection partner, threat hunting or forensics, and working proficiency in French.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $125 000 - $160 000.This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale.Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
  • Annual bonus program.
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gatherings twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

What drives us

We build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

Hi! We'reMercuryo, and we’re on a mission to redefine finance by blending the best of traditional banking with the power of decentralized finance (DeFi). We believe everyone deserves seamless access to Web3 and traditional financial services, so we're building the platform that makes it real: one that simplifies crypto and integrates it into the broader financial ecosystem.

We've partnered with leading brands including Visa, Mastercard, MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Ledger, and Jupiter, powering over 200 products and collaborating directly with major ecosystems like Solana, Consensys, and BNB Chain.

Why Mercuryo?

Industry Impact

Join us in helping world-class Web3 projects onboard millions of new users into the next generation of finance.

Innovative Environment

Collaborate with more than 300 talented professionals from diverse backgrounds — including banking, SaaS, and Web3 — all united in delivering outstanding user experiences.

AI-First Culture

We actively integrate AI across the company, from operations and analytics to marketing and product workflows. It helps teams move faster, improve productivity, and focus on high-impact work - while maintaining human oversight and accountability at every step. We see AI as a core part of how our teams innovate, collaborate, and scale.

Growth and Learning

Our expanding network of 200+ B2B partnerships and a user base of over 7 million means there’s always room to grow your skills, tackle new challenges, and push boundaries.

Flexible Culture

We’re remote-first, celebrating diversity across 30 countries. At Mercuryo, you’ll be empowered to take ownership of your work, spark creativity, and shape how we move forward together.

About the role

The Head of Anti-Fraud runs Mercuryo's fraud prevention function and reports directly to the Head of AML Operations. The role owns fraud risk across the on/off-ramp widget, wallet, swaps and card acquiring pay-ins and pay-outs: detection rules, investigations, chargeback and card scheme exposure, and checking that partners and merchants use our products only where we approved them.

We need an experienced, hands-on leader who has run large-scale fraud investigations, can find weaknesses in controls, and can redesign the procedures, rules and tooling to close them. Detailed knowledge of Visa and Mastercard rules is essential, in particular the programmes covering merchant integrity, fraud and dispute ratios, and transaction laundering.

Your Role:

Investigations

  • Lead complex and large-scale fraud investigations: linked-account networks, card testing, mule activity, account takeover, scams, and merchant or partner collusion.
  • Set the investigation standard: one case record per subject with linked history, closure deadlines, root-cause analysis, and evidence that stands up to an acquirer, a card scheme or an auditor.
  • Act on findings by changing rules, restricting or offboarding merchants and partners, and escalating suspicion to Transaction Monitoring and the MLRO.

Rules, controls and procedures

  • Own the anti-fraud rule set: design, impact testing before release, documented approval, a rule register, and regular effectiveness and false-positive reviews.
  • Find where controls fail or can be bypassed, and redesign them.
  • Write and maintain the anti-fraud procedures and the fraud risk assessment, and be able to show that each control works as written.
  • Build and run the AML alert and block rules that Transaction Monitoring and Compliance request on the anti-fraud platform, including for card acquiring, with fraud and AML rules kept separate in the register and each assigned an owner.

Card schemes, acquirers and chargebacks

  • Keep every acquirer relationship and MID within Visa and Mastercard fraud and dispute thresholds, with early warning before a limit is reached.
  • Lead the anti-fraud response to Visa and Mastercard notices and programme identifications within scheme deadlines.
  • Act as the anti-fraud lead with our acquiring partners: respond to RFIs with evidence, agree remediation plans, and complete due diligence questionnaires.
  • Own chargebacks and disputes: representment, pre-arbitration, deadlines and win rates, supported by tooling and pre-dispute alerts.

Merchant and partner integrity

  • Build and run the programme that detects and stops partners and merchants offering our widget or payment links on websites we have not approved, including through resellers, aggregators, iframes and redirects.
  • Select and manage a merchant monitoring and transaction laundering detection provider, and set how its alerts are triaged, actioned and evidenced.
  • Agree with KYB, Integrations, Legal and Acquiring what follows confirmed misuse (blocking, takedown, contractual remedies, offboarding and reporting), and check that each action has taken effect.

Leadership and reporting

  • Lead and develop the Anti-Fraud team of specialists, analysts, chargeback and fraud operations staff, based in several countries.
  • Report fraud losses, chargeback and fraud ratios, scheme exposure, incidents and control status to the Head of AML Operations, senior management and the Board.
  • Keep the incident register, and close audit, QA and compliance monitoring findings with evidence.
  • Work with Product and Engineering so new products, markets and merchants have fraud controls in place before launch.

What We're Looking For:

  • At least 8 years in fraud prevention in payments, card acquiring, a PSP or EMI, or crypto, including at least 3 years leading a fraud team or function, preferably one spread across several countries.
  • Has personally led large-scale fraud investigations from detection to resolution, such as card-testing attacks, mule networks, account takeover rings or merchant collusion, and produced evidence for acquirers, card schemes or law enforcement.
  • Has redesigned fraud controls and procedures after an audit, a scheme notice or a major incident, and can show the effect on losses and ratios.
  • Has handled acquirer RFIs, remediation plans and scheme programme cases directly.

Visa and Mastercard programmes

  • Visa: VAMP, VIRP, TC40 fraud reporting, dispute rules including Compelling Evidence 3.0, and the pre-dispute tools Order Insight and RDR.
  • Mastercard: ECP, EFM, the Global Merchant Audit Program (GMAP) due in April 2027, BRAM, GRIP, the Scam Merchant Monitoring Program, the Merchant Monitoring Program and its registered providers, Fraud and Loss Database (SAFE) reporting, MATCH and Ethoca alerts.
  • How these rules apply to a crypto merchant of record (MCC 6051) whose payments are offered through partners and resellers, including exposure from transaction laundering.
  • 3-D Secure and Strong Customer Authentication, including exemptions and liability shift.

Fraud controls, data and detection

  • Has owned a rules-based fraud engine: rules, lists, velocity limits, device fingerprinting, BIN and geo controls, with back-testing or shadow mode before release.
  • Writes SQL, builds dashboards in Metabase or a similar tool, and analyses large transaction datasets personally.
  • Has designed detection for transaction laundering and unauthorised website use, including test purchases through multi-step checkouts, redirect and referrer analysis, and measurement of a monitoring provider's detection rate and false positives.
  • Has run a fraud risk assessment covering external and internal fraud, using COSO or ACFE fraud risk guidance.

Governance and AML

  • Writes clear procedures that pass internal audit and regulator review, and keeps evidence that controls operate as written.
  • Understands where fraud meets AML, including mule networks, SAR escalation and sanctions screening, and has built AML controls on a fraud platform.
  • Gets engineering priority for control work by presenting clear data on losses and scheme exposure.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.

Nice-to-have:

  • Crypto on/off-ramp, exchange or wallet experience, including blockchain analytics such as Chainalysis in fraud and scam investigations.
  • Merchant risk experience at an acquirer or payment facilitator: underwriting, ongoing merchant monitoring and terminations.
  • Chargeback management platforms and automated dispute evidence.
  • Website takedowns through hosting providers and registrars.
  • Scam victim handling, including authorised push payment fraud.
  • CFE, CAMS or an equivalent qualification.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive market rate salary and performance-based incentives.
  • 22 days annual leave with an additional 6 company days, plus bank holidays.
  • Comprehensive health insurance plans.
  • Maternity & Paternity leave support.
  • Extensive benefits program.
  • Flexible work schedule and remote work options.
  • Modern offices and co-working spaces across 6 countries.
  • Working equipment.
  • Professional development and training opportunities.
  • Opportunity to shape the initiatives you’re working on.
  • Diverse and friendly team.
  • We are open-minded to new ideas.

If you're driven to be a part of the Web3 forefront and are keen to leave your mark on this rapidly evolving field, Mercuryo is an excellent choice. Discover our open positions and see how you can contribute to shaping the future!
