jobs.description:
About the COOL company

The COOL company is a global leader in AI-powered advertising technology, helping brands, agencies, and publishers simplify advertising and amplify performance.

Powered by COOL AI, our intelligent platform unifies creative generation, media activation, optimization, and attribution into one continuously learning system. Instead of relying on fragmented tools and manual campaign management, COOL AI executes thousands of real-time micro-optimizations across search, social, display, video, and connected TV—helping customers launch faster, optimize continuously, and achieve stronger business outcomes.

Our innovation and growth have earned industry-wide recognition, including being named a 7-time recipient of the Inc. 5000 list of America's Fastest-Growing Private Companies, a 2-time Deloitte Technology Fast 500 honoree, recognized on Crain's New York Fast 50, honored by the Digiday Media Awards for helping modernize digital media, and named one of Adweek's Top 10 Fastest Growing Solution Providers globally.

We're building the future of advertising, where every signal becomes intelligence and every optimization drives performance. As we continue to grow globally, we're looking for curious, ambitious people who want to work with cutting-edge AI technology, solve complex challenges, and help redefine what's possible in modern advertising.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Senior Ad Operations professional to manage, optimize, and troubleshoot programmatic advertising campaigns.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience working with platforms such as Google Display & Video 360 (DV360), The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, or similar DSPs and understands the full campaign lifecycle from campaign setup and targeting to pacing, optimization, reporting, and troubleshooting.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable managing multiple campaigns, analyzing performance data, identifying delivery issues, and making optimization decisions that improve campaign results and profitability.

Responsibilities

  • Set up, launch, manage, and optimize programmatic advertising campaigns across DSPs such as DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, and similar platforms.

  • Manage campaign structure including advertisers, insertion orders, line items, creatives, budgets, bids, targeting, frequency caps, and flight dates.

  • Monitor daily campaign delivery, pacing, spend, performance, and KPIs.

  • Optimize campaigns toward objectives including CPM, CPC, CPA, CTR, viewability, completion rate, conversions, and ROAS.

  • Manage audience, contextual, geographic, device, inventory, placement, and supply-source targeting.

  • Troubleshoot campaign underdelivery, overspend, low win rates, creative issues, tracking discrepancies, and inventory limitations.

  • Analyze DSP reporting and identify opportunities to improve campaign performance and media efficiency.

  • Manage and validate pixels, conversion tracking, click trackers, impression trackers, and third-party measurement.

  • Work with programmatic inventory across display, video, mobile app, CTV, and other digital formats.

  • Understand and troubleshoot the programmatic buying flow between DSPs, SSPs, exchanges, publishers, and measurement vendors.

  • Work with internal commercial and technical teams on campaign requirements, inventory availability, targeting, and performance.

  • Prepare campaign reports and clearly communicate performance, issues, and optimization actions to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Maintain accurate campaign documentation and ensure campaigns are launched and managed according to agreed requirements and deadlines.

Qualifications

Required

  • 3+ years of hands-on programmatic campaign management / Ad Operations experience.

  • Strong practical experience with at least one major DSP, preferably Google DV360.

  • Experience creating and managing campaigns directly inside a DSP rather than only reviewing reports.

  • Strong understanding of programmatic advertising, including RTB, DSPs, SSPs, exchanges, auctions, CPMs, bid floors, and targeting.

  • Experience with campaign pacing, budget management, bidding, optimization, and troubleshooting.

  • Understanding of display and video advertising formats and creative specifications.

  • Strong analytical skills and ability to make optimization decisions based on campaign data.

  • Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills.

  • High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple campaigns simultaneously.

  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

Preferred

  • Experience with DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, Xandr, Yahoo DSP, or similar platforms.

  • Experience with CTV, video, and mobile app campaigns.

  • Understanding of OpenRTB, VAST, Prebid, ads.txt/app-ads.txt, sellers.json, and supply-chain concepts.

  • Experience with third-party verification and measurement platforms such as DoubleVerify, IAS, or similar solutions.

  • Experience working with both buy-side and sell-side programmatic teams.

Cultural Competencies

  • Must be able to work primarily between the hours of 9:30 AM - 6:30 PM ET

  • Must have a player/coach mentality, willing to both execute and lead

  • Ability to juggle multiple projects concurrently and set and meet deadlines

  • Skilled at receiving and providing direct feedback

  • Collaborative mindset and great teamwork skills

  • Entrepreneurial & adaptable; great learning skills

  • Curious, research-minded, data-informed

  • Able to search for possible solutions and apply them

  • Creative confidence

  • Proactive communicator

  • A sense of humor and a love of online culture

  • Thrives in a start-up culture

Our Authorization team develops highly scalable, high-performance systems that manage access and establish trust across services, applications, and complex enterprise environments. As a Software Engineer on the Splunk Platform Authorization team, you’ll build and maintain backend services that power secure, reliable access across complex enterprise environments. You’ll work with experienced engineers to implement technical solutions, solve challenging problems, and improve the performance and reliability of our core platform. You’ll have the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful engineering work while expanding your expertise in distributed systems and cloud-native technologies.

What you will do

Talk the way you normally do, mixing two languages as you go.

Steps

  1. Declare which two languages you mix

  2. Tap record and talk as you would with a friend who speaks both

  3. Switch naturally, mid-sentence

  4. Submit

Open in 11 Southeast Asian countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

Go through a website step by step and screenshot each screen as you go. Stop before you pay for anything.

Steps

  1. Pick a flow: sign-up, search-to-basket, booking, account settings

What gets rejected

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years and we do not screen on your CV, because we decide on what you do in the trial.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application with a short Loom video.
  2. A short written step: your internet speed, your computer, and a few questions in your own words.
  3. Aptitude tests, with a published floor.
  4. A recorded video interview. One take, no re-records. We verify the work history you've told us about.
  5. A short call with the founder.
  6. A paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

    1. Full time once hired, and this is your only job. During the paid trial you work 4 hours a day with us, 2 of them at a fixed time inside our working day, and you can keep your current job. If you pass, you give notice and join us full time within 30 days.
    2. Reliable internet, at least 30 Mbps down and 5 Mbps up, tested live with us.
    3. Strong written English.
    4. Based in South Africa.
    5. You track your working time with our time tracking tool from day one.

Benefits

1300 USD per month on hire, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

Pass your 90-day review and your pay goes up by 50 percent. The 90 days count from the day you start full time.

On top of that:

  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.
  3. Paid sick leave.
  4. A health allowance.
  5. A coworking allowance.

Responsibility and pay move quickly here for people who earn them. Authority over decisions that reach a client moves slowly and deliberately, and it is earned on a track record rather than on a good first month. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

jobs.excerpt: What We’re BuildingHoneycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do!
jobs.description:
What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!
If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb.io press releases.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

Little more about the team:

Product marketing at Honeycomb is a small team with a wide surface area. We decide how Honeycomb is positioned, what we say at launch, what the sales team brings into a deal, and how an engineer who has never heard of us understands the product in the first two minutes. Because the team is small, the work is broad: in one week you might rewrite a product page, build a competitive one-pager, interview a customer, and run the launch checklist for a new feature.

This role is built for someone early in a product marketing career who wants to systematically improve the customer buying journey. As a product and messaging expert, you will partner with go-to-market teams to drive business impact through sales and marketing campaigns. You will get real ownership of real launches, and you will have senior product marketers, a technical field team, and engineers who like explaining their work close at hand. Our audience is engineers and platform teams, so the bar is accuracy first: we would rather be precise and useful than clever.

What you’ll do in the role:

You will support and execute product marketing across Honeycomb's core products, with a generalist mix of messaging, launches, content, enablement, and competitive work. Expect to start by contributing to pieces of each and to own more of them over your first year.

Responsibilities

  • Messaging and positioning: Write and maintain messaging for features and product areas, from the one-sentence version an engineer reads on a web page to the slide a sales engineer uses in a technical conversation. Keep it accurate and grounded in what the product actually does.
  • Launches: Run launch execution for small and mid-sized releases and support the larger ones. Build the plan, write the assets, coordinate Product, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success, and report on how the launch performed.
  • Content: Produce the practical material that helps people evaluate and adopt Honeycomb: blog posts, solution briefs, web copy, demo scripts, FAQs, and customer-facing one-pagers.
  • Sales enablement: Equip the field with what they need to run a good conversation, including pitch narratives, objection handling, battlecards, and release updates. Join customer calls, listen to recorded ones, and fix the material that isn't landing.
  • Competitive and market intelligence: Track the observability market and competitor moves. Maintain competitive assets and keep them current and honest, so the field trusts them.
  • Voice of customer and proof points: Talk to customers and prospects, turn what you hear into case studies, quotes, and proof points, and bring the patterns back to Product and Marketing.
  • Measurement: Help define what success looks like for your work, pull the data, and share what you learn, including the things that didn't work.

What you’ll bring to the role:

  • 2 to 5 years of experience in product marketing, or in a closely adjacent go-to-market role such as content marketing, sales engineering, technical writing, developer relations, or product management, with at least some of it in B2B SaaS.
  • Strong writing. You can take a dense technical explanation and turn it into something short, accurate, and useful, and you can tell the difference between the two yourself.
  • Curiosity about technical products and the patience to learn how they work. You ask engineers questions until you actually understand the answer, and you are comfortable in a product that assumes a technical user.
  • Passion about the team winning: Sales, marketing, and product teams will depend on you to succeed. Their success is your success, but you’re not simply an order taker: you look for the smart solutions and don’t wait to be asked.
  • The ability to run a project across teams without formal authority: setting a timeline, chasing the open items, and telling people clearly when something has slipped.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward shipping. Our priorities move, the team is small, and the best work here comes from people who start rather than wait for a brief.
  • Willingness to use data to decide and to evaluate your own work honestly.
  • Demonstrated experience applying AI tooling in your work.

Nice to have

  • Exposure to observability, developer tools, distributed tracing, OpenTelemetry, platform engineering, or reliability and SLO practices. We will teach this, but a head start helps.
  • Experience marketing to engineers as the primary audience.
  • Hands-on familiarity with AI and LLM tooling, including coding agents and MCP-based workflows.
  • Experience with webinars, conference talks, or community programs.
  • Experience working in a fully distributed company.
Base Salary based on level of experience
$125,000—$190,000 USD

What you'll get when you join the Hive:

  • A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program
  • It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience
  • Time to recharge with unlimited PTO
  • A distributed-first mindset and culture (really!)
  • Home office, co-working, and internet stipend
  • Full benefits coverage for employees, with additional coverage available for dependents
  • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, regardless of path to parenthood
  • Annual development allowance
  • And much more...
Please note we cannot currently sponsor or support visa transfers at this time. Additionally, in compliance with applicable law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work.

Phishing and Recruitment Scam Warning:

We take your security seriously. Please be aware that recruitment scams are increasingly common and scammers may create email addresses or websites to impersonate Honeycomb employees. To help protect you:
  • All communications will come from an @honeycomb.io email address
    • We occasionally work with external recruiting agencies. These partners will use legitimate business email addresses—never personal accounts like Gmail or Yahoo.
  • Our recruiting process will never ask you to provide financial or sensitive personal information, including but not limited to:
    • Social security or tax identification numbers
    • Credit card numbers
    • Bank account information

Diversity & Accommodations:

We're committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace—where people of all backgrounds, identities, experiences, and abilities are welcomed, valued, and supported. We recognize that there is no single path to success and embrace nontraditional career journeys and diverse perspectives as key to building stronger, more innovative teams.
We strive to ensure an inclusive experience throughout every stage of our hiring process and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations as needed. If you require accommodations or accessible formats at any point during our hiring process, please let your recruiter know.
As an equal opportunity employer our hiring process is designed to put you at ease and help you show your best work. If there’s anything we can do to improve your experience, we’re always open to feedback.

Privacy Notice:

If you apply for a job at Honeycomb and your application is unsuccessful (or you withdraw from the process or decline our offer), Honeycomb will retain your information after your application for a period of time in accordance with local laws. We retain this information for various reasons, including in case we face a legal challenge in respect of a recruitment decision, to consider you for other current or future jobs at Honeycomb, and to help us better understand, analyze and improve our recruitment processes.
For more information regarding our privacy practices please see the Honeycomb Privacy Notice.
If you do not want us to retain your information, or want us to update it, please contact . Please note, however, that we may retain some information if required by law or as necessary to protect ourselves from legal claims.

jobs.description:
Mission

EdReports.org is at the forefront of the curriculum reform movement. By increasing the capacity of educators to identify and demand the highest quality curriculum, EdReports.org is both disrupting a multibillion-dollar market and transforming the way students are taught and ultimately perform. With the firm belief that what is taught matters and that all students deserve high quality materials, EdReports.org publishes free, online, evidence-rich reviews of instructional materials. Explore our organization's core competencies in greater detail here.

Planning to use Artificial Intelligence (AI) for your application, interview prep, or for other means of assistance throughout the hiring process? Click here to review our AI guidance before proceeding.

Purpose of Position

The Lead, Reviews will oversee and support the review of instructional materials within their designated content area, ensuring that reviews are evidence-rich, aligned to EdReports criteria, and meet the needs of educators and curriculum decision makers. The Lead, Reviews will collaborate with content teams and stakeholders to enhance review processes, provide expert guidance, and drive improvements in instruction across the nation.

This specific role will bring deep expertise in K–12 mathematics education to EdReports’ work, with a focus on how students develop mathematical understanding, procedural skills, and the ability to apply mathematics. The Lead will apply expertise in college- and career-ready mathematics standards, instructional shifts, learning progressions, and current research-supported practices to the review of instructional materials and related organizational initiatives. This role is well suited for someone energized by instructional materials and the review process itself, including working with educator-reviewers to examine curriculum closely, collect and analyze evidence, identify patterns, and translate findings into clear, accurate, evidence-rich written reviews. The Lead will balance this detailed individual contributor work with broader content leadership, serving as a cross-functional mathematics expert who strengthens review tools and processes and informs strategic projects and initiatives.

Key Responsibilities & Outcomes

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and support reviews of mathematics instructional materials, ensuring alignment to relevant standards, current research, and EdReports’ high-quality, evidence-based criteria. This role requires flexibility to support reviewer meetings and review activities, including late afternoon and evening availability when scheduled.
  • Apply deep expertise in K–12 mathematics, college- and career-ready standards, instructional shifts, learning progressions, and research-supported instructional practices to accurately analyze instructional materials.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to examine emerging research, trends, and best practices in mathematics education and translate findings into actionable recommendations that support the continuous improvement of instructional materials review practices.
  • Train and support educator-reviewers, ensuring consistent calibration across teams to produce reliable, evidence-rich reviews that meet EdReports’ quality benchmarks.
  • Collaborate across content teams to update and refine mathematics review tools and processes based on research, feedback, and evolving educational trends.
  • Provide expert guidance and coaching to review teams, helping them navigate the review process and build consensus on educational criteria.
  • Exercise independent judgment on complex content and review questions, resolving issues within established review standards and elevating decisions with broader strategic or organizational implications as appropriate.
  • Engage with external stakeholders, including publishers, to communicate the review process.
  • Serve as a thought leader explaining EdReports mathematics review findings to educators, districts, states, partner nonprofits, and other audiences using our resources to select curriculum.
  • Serve as a mathematics subject matter expert across EdReports, partnering cross-functionally to inform organizational projects, strategies, resources, and initiatives.
  • Other relevant duties as assigned to support the organization's strategic goals, with the expectation that all EdReports employees remain flexible and adaptable to evolving responsibilities.

Outcomes:

  • Contribute to the completion of mathematics reviews in line with [current-year] goals and KPIs.
  • Achieve 100% alignment in calibration checks across review teams by the end of each review cycle, ensuring evidence and criteria are consistently applied.
  • Implement three process improvements annually with a goal of reducing review cycle times while maintaining or improving quality.
  • Ensure 100% of reviewers complete required training and demonstrate proficiency through calibration activities and post-training assessments.
  • Spend roughly 10% of time engaging with the Brand Office on thought leadership, events, and external stakeholder education about review processes and outcomes.
  • Collaborate with colleagues on cross-functional strategic and operational initiatives.

Travel

National travel will occur related to organizational needs and for professional learning, as needed. The amount of travel will be monitored to ensure it is appropriate for both the organization and this position.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Passion for EdReports’ mission and vision, our core values, and our commitment to Diversity, Belonging, Inclusion, and Equity;
  • At least seven years of relevant professional experience in mathematics curriculum design, instruction, coaching, research, assessment, program leadership, or a related field, demonstrating deep expertise in college- and career-ready mathematics standards and instructional shifts.
  • Understanding of the K–12 mathematics education political and policy landscape.
  • Ability to analyze complex instructional materials and synthesize evidence into clear, actionable recommendations for diverse stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex initiatives and influence cross-functional stakeholders toward shared outcomes without relying on formal authority.
  • Demonstrated skill facilitating adult learning, coaching educators or colleagues, and building alignment across groups with differing perspectives or interpretations of evidence.
  • Exceptional written and spoken communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Fluency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office (including Excel and PowerPoint).
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • Residency in and authorization to work in the United States.

Preferred:

  • Additional expertise supporting Multilingual Learners or Special Populations.
  • K–12 mathematics classroom and coaching experience.
  • Experience with thought leadership, public speaking, and external engagement, including presenting complex ideas to partner organizations, funders, and stakeholders.
  • Experience with Adobe Creative Suite, Salesforce, Canvas, and online learning management platforms.
  • Master’s degree.

Salary

The salary for this position is $102,824 - $139,114 annually. At EdReports, we determine final salaries based on the role's requirements and the candidate's experience and skills, while maintaining equity within our compensation bands. To support fairness and provide opportunities for growth, we typically offer salaries at or below the midpoint of the range. All salary offers are non-negotiable to ensure consistency and equity across the organization.

Benefits

We know the importance of living a fulfilling, healthy life–both professionally and personally. That’s why some of the benefits we offer include:

  • Unlimited Discretionary Time Off (DTO) and Sick Time,
  • 21 days of paid holidays and office closure days in 2026,
  • Monthly Communications Reimbursement,
  • Initial home office and technology setup stipend,
  • EdReports pays for 90% of health care for both the employee and their immediate family, and
  • 401k that new hires become eligible for after six months of employment (includes safe harbor, employer match, etc.).

Work Authorization Requirements

All EdReports employees must reside in and be authorized to work in the United States. EdReports does not sponsor employment visas, and we are unable to consider candidates residing outside the U.S.

Physical Requirements

Work is normally performed in a remote office environment including, but not limited to standing and sitting for long periods of time; and fine-finger and hand manipulation to operate a computer and keyboard. Employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing electronic information, transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, and extensive reading. This person will travel by car, air, or other transportation (as indicated in the Travel section) and should be able to physically withstand the demands of such travel. Core Competencies

  • CORE EXPERTISE: Possess skills, knowledge, and abilities to perform essential duties; keeps knowledge current; utilize multiple points of view to achieve goals and is a subject matter resource for others.
  • ORGANIZATIONAL STEWARDSHIP: Cultivate external relationships, uphold policies, leverage historical insights, actively participate in organizational improvement, and adapt to align with the needs of the organization.

We Value All Voices

EdReports is committed to equal-employment principles and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop, and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live, work, and serve. jobs.description:
We’re Sharp Performance

Sharp Performance exists so that everyone who answers the call has someone in their corner who has walked in their shoes.

We help first responders and their spouses thrive through confidential coaching from people with similar lived experience. Our coaches have carried the badge, worn the gear, or stood beside someone who did. Through our mobile platform, we connect law enforcement, firefighters, and other frontline professionals with coaches who understand the job because they have lived it.

We’re early-stage and backed by amazing investors. The team is small enough that your work shows up in the rollout, the product, and the customer’s experience within weeks. If building something that matters alongside people who hold a high standard sounds better than a safe seat somewhere else, come build it with us.

The Opportunity

We’re hiring a Head of Marketplace to run the system that connects first responders with the coaches who have walked in their shoes. This role reports directly to the CEO.

Sharp is a two-sided marketplace. On one side are departments and the first responders inside them. On the other are coaches who have lived the job. The Head of Marketplace owns how those two sides come together: the supply forecast that tells us how many coaches to hire and where, the matching process that takes a member from intake to first session, and the numbers that show whether the marketplace is working. Implementations get Sharp in the door and Customer Success keeps departments engaged. You make sure a coach is ready the moment a first responder reaches out.

This is a cross-functional role. You will work closely with Coaching, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success, and you will lead our Operations function: the Lead Product Analyst, all of our data efforts, and BizOps. You set the operating rhythm for the company and bring the numbers to every leadership conversation.

This role is remote within the US, with travel to Carlsbad, CA and to customer departments as the work requires.

What You’ll Own

  • Marketplace Planning: Own supply and demand forecasting. Turn the rollout calendar and department demand into coach capacity targets by discipline (law enforcement, fire, EMS, spouses) and region. Give the Head of Coaching a clear plan to hire against, so no department waits for a coach and no coach sits idle.
  • Matching Process: Own the process that connects first responders with coaches, from intake to first session to rematch. The Head of Coaching owns the coaches, the Head of Product owns the coaching product, and you own how the whole system runs and whether it works. Set the rules, find the bottlenecks, and bring clear requirements to Product.
  • Marketplace Efficiency: Own the metrics that show whether the marketplace works: time to first session, match rate, coach utilization, active coaches, and rematch rate. Report them by department every month, with a plan for every account below target.
  • Data: Own the single source of truth. Metric definitions, dashboards, and board reporting live with you. Lead the Lead Product Analyst and our data efforts so leadership trusts the numbers because you stand behind them.
  • Operations: Lead BizOps and set the company’s operating rhythm, so everyone knows what matters this quarter and why. Set priorities, hire, and hold the standard.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Give GTM the supply and cost inputs it needs to set pricing. Give Marketing readiness inputs for launches. Give Customer Success the engagement data it needs to drive renewals.

The Numbers

Two numbers define success in this role. You will set the targets with the CEO in your first 90 days and own them after that:

  • Marketplace liquidity. Time from rollout to first session, match rate (the share of members matched within a set number of days), coach utilization, and active coaches by discipline and region. Reported by department, monthly, with a plan for every account below target.
  • Marketplace quality. Rematch rate, member satisfaction after sessions, and how accurate the supply forecast is against actual demand.

Who Thrives Here

This role is not for everyone. You will thrive if you:

  • Have scaled the provider network or marketplace operations at a telehealth or care marketplace, working with independent (1099) providers, employed (W-2) providers, or both, and can show how you improved time to first appointment, match rate, and provider utilization.
  • Are comfortable with data models but can explain them in simple terms.
  • Make decisions with incomplete information and adjust fast when the data says you were wrong.
  • Prefer ownership over supervision.
  • Care deeply about serving those who serve others.

Why you’ll love working here

Sharp is a small, fast-growing team, and our success starts with the people doing the work. The package is built to support your health, your finances, and your growth:

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance for you and your family.
  • Flexible PTO to recharge and perform at your best.
  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity that reflect the seniority of the role.
  • 401(k) with company match.
  • Unlimited access to the Sharp Performance platform and our coaches.

American Families for Vaccines (AFV) is a national organization leading the pro-vaccine grassroots movement across the country. About the Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance

The Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance (PVLA) is a legal strategy and litigation initiative supporting evidence-based vaccine policy across the United States. Working as a project under American Families for Vaccines (AFV), PVLA provides legal analysis, litigation support, and strategic guidance to state advocates, policymakers, and public health leaders.

PVLA aims for high-impact legal infrastructure, not a volume-driven litigation shop. Our work focuses on strengthening public health authority, countering the expansion of non-medical exemptions, and shaping the legal and constitutional framework surrounding vaccine policy.

The Pro-Vaccine Legal Alliance Associate Director will serve as a core member of PVLA, supporting state-level vaccine policy through legal research, analysis, and strategic advising. This position sits at the center of a rapidly evolving legal landscape. The PVLA Associate Director will work closely with the Director to develop litigation memos, provide real-time legal guidance during legislative sessions, support amicus and litigation strategy, and contribute to PVLA’s growing national legal infrastructure. jobs.description:
Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We make eco-friendly products and donate 50% of our profits to provide clean water and help build toilets for the billions of people who lack proper access. So far, we’ve contributed over $18 million AUD (roughly $12.5 million USD) to fund sanitation projects around the globe. Basically, we’re really good at doing good.

With hubs in Australia, the Philippines, China, the US, UK and Europe, our amazing team of 200+ work to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next couple of years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our Digital Experience Lead, you’ll own how our Customer Experience team’s technology actually works. You’ll hold the roadmap for a stack of CX tools — think Zendesk, Zapier, Sprout and a handful of others — and make the call on what stays, what goes, and what gets replaced. You’ll lead the build-out of automations and AI-powered workflows that take the busywork off our CX team’s plate, partner closely with IT and Digital Product to land new tools properly, and lead and grow one direct report along the way. We’re moving into a new phase of scaling up our internal processes to match our growth, and this role is central to making that happen — think less “maintain what exists” and more “figure out how we do this better.”

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

  • Reviewed our CX tech stack and made the case for consolidating two overlapping tools into one
  • Worked with the Analytics & Insights team to redesign our Zendesk issue-type taxonomy
  • Sketched out a 12-month roadmap of automation and AI experiments with Digital Product
  • Pushed back on a vendor renewal that didn’t stack up on cost, and proposed an alternative
  • Coached your direct report through a cross-functional roadblock with IT

Let’s talk about you

You lead without needing to be told howYou’ve led a team before and you’re used to making the call yourself, not waiting to be pushed into it. When something needs a recommendation, you bring one — with the reasoning attached.

You speak fluent tech, without needing to write the codeYou don’t need to be an engineer, but you understand technology well enough to pull apart a tool, weigh it against alternatives, and make a confident call on what we should actually be using. Hands-on time with tools like Zendesk, Sprout, Zapier, Kodif or similar CX platforms will help you hit the ground running.

You use AI as a toolkit, not a talking pointYou’re comfortable and confident using AI tools day to day, and you can see the practical ways they fit into automations and customer-facing workflows — not just the hype.

You give a crapDo you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off,as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the highest standards of social and environmental impact. With our most recent score of 125.5 we’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world,generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (95%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

Position Description

Position:Senior Director, Strategic Philanthropy

Employer:Vitamin Angels Alliance, Inc. (VA)

Department:Development

Location:Remote in the US – Eastern or Central Time Zone Preferred

Salary:$170,000-$190,000

About Vitamin Angels

Vitamin Angels (VA) is a 501(c)3 non-profit, global public health organization working towards ending malnutrition worldwide by distributing life-changing vitamins and minerals to at-risk mothers and children under five throughout the U.S., and around the world.

Vitamin Angels is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We are a dedicated group of individuals who aim to foster a supportive environment where everyone can contribute, thrive, and grow.

Role or Purpose of Position

The Senior Director, Strategic Philanthropy will lead Vitamin Angels’ fundraising from public foundations; global philanthropic alliances; and other institutional funders working in malnutrition; maternal, newborn, and child health; global public health; and adjacent areas aligned with Vitamin Angels 2030.

Reporting to the Chief Development Officer (CDO) and working in close partnership with the Programs Team, the Senior Director will serve as a player-manager with initial responsibility for building the Strategic Philanthropy function. They will personally lead the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-value, high-potential, and strategically important funder relationships while establishing the strategies, systems, and internal partnerships necessary for long-term revenue growth.

The Senior Director will initially hire and manage one direct report and will build additional capacity as revenue and organizational needs warrant. They will work closely with the CDO to develop long-term fundraising and partnership strategies that maximize revenue, diversify Vitamin Angels’ funding base, and position the organization’s programs, evidence, and impact effectively within the philanthropic marketplace.

Major Duties and Responsibilities

Pipeline Development and Resource Generation

  • Build and manage a portfolio of high-value prospects and funders, including foundations, global philanthropic alliances, and other institutional partners focused on malnutrition; maternal, newborn, and child health; global public health; and adjacent areas.

  • Lead the full fundraising cycle, including prospect identification, research, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, negotiation, award management, stewardship, and renewal.
  • Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward high-priority funders, developing sophisticated, long-term partnerships that advance Vitamin Angels’ strategic and programmatic objectives.

  • Oversee funder stewardship, reporting, and renewal strategies, ensuring that commitments are fulfilled and opportunities to renew, expand, and deepen support are identified.
  • Provide the CDO with regular revenue forecasts, pipeline analysis, and assessments of emerging funding opportunities and potential risks.

Strategy and Organizational Leadership

  • Serve as Vitamin Angels’ internal expert on foundation and institutional philanthropy, advising leadership on funder priorities, philanthropic trends, and emerging opportunities.
  • Translate Vitamin Angels’ programmatic strategy, scientific evidence, and impact into compelling philanthropic investment opportunities.
  • Monitor trends in global health and philanthropy and identify innovative opportunities for engagement both within and beyond the sector.
  • Partner with the broader Development team to identify cross-functional funding opportunities while ensuring clear coordination with Corporate Partnerships and other revenue-generating functions.
  • Share programmatic knowledge, funder intelligence, and positioning strategies that help the broader Development team identify and pursue new revenue opportunities.
  • Build alignment and foster collaboration across Programs, Finance, Marketing, the Executive Office, and Development around priority funder relationships and funding opportunities.
  • Represent Vitamin Angels in funder meetings, conferences, philanthropic networks, and relevant global health forums.
  • Contribute to the strategic direction, revenue planning, and overall performance of the Development department.
  • Represent Development in management team meetings (as needed) and collaborate with the CDO and departmental leadership to advance organizational priorities and ensure the team’s overall success.

Team Development and Management

  • Build the Strategic Philanthropy function, initially hiring and managing one direct report and expanding the team as revenue and organizational needs warrant.
  • Establish clear roles, goals, processes, performance measures, and standards of accountability for the Strategic Philanthropy team.
  • Recruit, onboard, coach, and manage staff to achieve individual and collective fundraising goals.
  • Create a collaborative, high-performing team culture focused on proactive fundraising, continuous improvement, shared accountability, and measurable results.
  • Develop the systems, tools, resources, and internal partnerships necessary to support sustainable growth in institutional philanthropic revenue.

Level of Decision-Making

Within the bounds of VA’s mission, values and policies, and sound professional practices,the Senior Directorhasthe broad discretion to use independent judgement to manage their activities in whatever way will best serve VA clients, partners, employees, and mission.Specific authorities associated with this position and their implementation procedures will be determined in conjunction with Chief Development Officer.

Organizational Relationships

VA operates under a collaborative, matrix management model. The Senior Director of Strategic Philanthropyis supervised by the Chief Development Officer with respect to overall assignments and performance. S/he connects regularly and collaborates with the VA Programs team, Director of Business Development, the Director of Grants Management and the VA Finance Team, VP of Marketing, Senior Managers, the CEO, the CFO, and Chief Development Officer, and interacts daily with all members of the VA team.The Senior Director of Strategic Philanthropy establishes their own daily work priorities and ensures that all responsibilities are conducted with the accepted best practices, sound professional judgment, and within established schedules and budgets.

Travel required

Qualifications and Skills (Required and Preferred)

  • At least 12 years of progressively responsible fundraising or related experience, including at least five years leading and managing high-performing teams.
  • Significant experience in foundation and institutional fundraising, with a proven record of personally cultivating, soliciting, negotiating, and securing significant grants and philanthropic commitments.

  • Demonstrated critical thinking, sound judgment, and the ability to manage complex projects and competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Description

Quantum Sky is hiring a Senior Cloud Security Engineer (AWS & GCP) to join our team of cloud, security, and compliance experts. This role is primarily focused on day‑to‑day security engineering, including system hardening, vulnerability remediation, cloud operations, and security tool management across AWS & GCP environments.

In addition to regular business‑hours responsibilities, engineers participate in a structured after‑hours 24×7 on‑call rotation (primary or backup) to support response to incidents, alerts, and escalations for customers operating under FedRAMP, FISMA, and NIST 800‑53 frameworks.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform systems administration and maintenance including patching, vulnerability scanning, compliance scanning and remediation, backups, and recovery for cloud workloads.
  • Support AWS & GCP environments, including Windows and Linux virtual machines, container workloads, and cloud services such as EC2, EBS, S3, RDS, WorkSpaces (AWS), Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL (GCP), and Active Directory or equivalent identity services.
  • Configure, update, and maintain security tools for endpoint protection, log collection, vulnerability scanning, and compliance monitoring.
  • Troubleshoot issues across network, compute, application, and identity layers by reviewing logs, collecting data, and analyzing system behavior.
  • Implement hardening and compliance controls using CIS Benchmarks, DISA STIGs, and FedRAMP requirements.
  • Remediate vulnerabilities identified by tools such as Tenable, Trivy, OpenSCAP, Anchore, Twistlock, and others.
  • Provide quality assurance feedback during system deployments to ensure architecture meets compliance and operational requirements.
  • Collaborate with Security Analysts to ensure uninterrupted delivery of security services to customers.
  • Create and maintain documentation including network diagrams, dataflow diagrams, SOPs, and security tool configuration guides.
  • Support client communications, deliverables, and issue resolution with strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Support and mentor junior engineers as and when required.
  • After‑Hours 24×7 On‑Call Rotation:
    • Serve as primary or backup on‑call engineer during assigned rotation.
    • Respond to after‑hours security alerts, infrastructure incidents, outages, and ConMon events.
    • Perform initial triage, containment, and stabilization using established runbooks.
    • Investigate and respond to alerts generated.
    • Escalate complex issues to senior engineers, architects, or compliance teams.
    • Document incidents, actions taken, and recommended improvements.
    • Contribute to automation improvements and runbook enhancements.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Six (6) or more years of IT engineering and/or cybersecurity experience, with at least three (4) years working in a dedicated cloud security engineering or similar position.
  • Hands‑on experience with both AWS and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
  • Ability to diagnose and resolve issues across Linux and Windows systems, network infrastructure, and cloud services.
  • General systems administration and vulnerability management experience, including system patching and hardening, identity and access management (IAM), and related tasks.
  • Experience working in a DevSecOps environment, integrating security practices into cloud and infrastructure workflows.
  • Familiarity with ITSM ticketing systems such as Gitlab (preferred), Jira, ServiceNow, etc.
  • Ability to work independently during both business hours and on‑call periods.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for customer interaction and incident documentation.
  • Hands‑on experience with one or more of the following tools:
    • Splunk Enterprise
    • Tenable Security Center/Nessus
    • Invicti/Acunetix
    • Appgate
    • Okta
    • GitLab
    • Palo Alto Networks Firewalls
    • TrendMicro Deep Security
    • Trivy
    • Anchore
    • Terraform
    • CloudFormation
    • Ansible

Desired:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or other relevant field.
  • Experience supporting federal/government-facing customers or consulting engagements, ensuring compliance and operational requirements.
  • Experience with FedRAMP, FISMA, or NIST 800‑53 compliance frameworks.
  • Prior on‑call, SRE, SOC, or incident response experience.
  • Relevant AWS or Google Cloud Platform certifications.
  • Security+ or other relevant industry security certification.
  • Experience with infrastructure‑as‑code or automation tooling.
  • Experience with Kubernetes is highly desirable.

Location:

  • Remote (US)

Clearance:

  • Must be a US Citizen with the ability to obtain a security clearance

About Quantum Sky

Compensation:

  • Compensation is unique to each candidate and relative to the skills and experience they bring to the position. The salary range for this position is typically between $135,000-$160,000 This does not guarantee a specific salary as compensation is based upon multiple factors such as education, experience, certifications, and other requirements, and may fall outside of the above-stated range.

Benefits:

  • Highlights of our benefits include Health/Dental/Vision, 401(k) match, Paid Time Off, STD/LTD/Life Insurance, Referral Bonuses, professional development reimbursement, and parental leave.

About the Hiring Group

RTI Health Solutions (RTI-HS), a wholly owned subsidiary of RTI International, is an independent and internationally recognized research organization. With offices in the US, UK, Spain, France, and Sweden, we provide healthcare consulting and research expertise to optimize decision making for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device products across the development and marketing lifecycle. Clients rely on our expertise, quality standards, and integrity to guide their product development and regulatory and market access strategies.

Our various practice areas include Value, Access, and HEOR; Patient-Centered and Outcomes Research; Epidemiology and Biostatistics; Medical Communications; Global Business Operations; and Strategic Consulting and Growth.

We are currently seeking a Senior Psychometrician to join our Patient-Centered Outcomes Assessment (PCOA) team.

This role can be office-based, hybrid, or remote in the UK or one of our European office locations, including Spain, France, and Sweden.

What You'll Do

RTI-HS psychometricians serve both a strategic and technical role within interdisciplinary research teams. They provide scientific leadership on the development, evaluation and application of clinical outcome assessments; guide psychometric and outcomes research strategies for clients, including participating in regulatory interactions; and are responsible designing, implementing and interpreting a variety of technical analyses.

You will be expected to:

  • Provide strategic scientific leadership on psychometric and outcomes research programs, including study design, endpoint selection, regulatory strategy, interpretation of evidence, and client decision-making.
  • Design, oversee, and conduct classical and modern psychometric analyses, interpretation of meaningful within-patient change, and advanced statistical analyses to support the development, evaluation, and regulatory acceptance of clinical outcome assessments
  • Accurately analyse, interpret, and clearly communicate psychometric results to clients within specified deadlines
  • Produce high-quality psychometric analysis plans, technical reports, and manuscripts
  • Lead and contribute to proposals, thought leadership initiatives, methodological innovation, and business development activities that support growth of the PCOA practice.
  • Communicate effectively (via email, telephone, and in-person) with clients and team members

What You'll Need

  • Master’s degree in quantitative psychology, statistics, biostatistics, or related field with at least 10 years of directly related experience, or a PhD and a minimum of 5 years of directly related experience
  • Extensive experience independently preparing psychometric analysis plans and reports of clinical outcome assessments for regulatory review
  • Demonstrated proficiency in SAS and/or R programming (expertise in both strongly preferred), along with experience using latent variable and psychometric modeling software packages.
  • Significant experience related to the psychometric evaluation of outcome measures, including classical psychometric methods (e.g., evaluations of test-retest reliability and internal consistency), exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and Rasch Measurement and/or Item Response Theory
  • Experience implementing hierarchical linear modeling, repeated measures models, mixture models
  • Demonstrated ability to work well independently and as team leader
  • Excellent analytical and communication skills (both written and oral)
  • Experience supporting regulatory submissions and interactions with health authorities related to clinical outcome assessments, endpoint strategies, psychometric evidence, or patient-focused drug development initiatives.

jobs.description:
Join Team CARFAX as a Sales Enablement Program Manager

Isn't it time you bragged about where you work? At CARFAX, we do, every day. We pride ourselves on being mission-focused on helping to grow a brand built on accuracy and integrity. We care deeply about our products and our customers. We’re more than just a company: We help millions of consumers make more-informed decisions every day. We know that our teammates are our most valuable asset, and we value a balanced life while tackling challenging projects in a fast-paced environment.

About the Role

CARFAX is investing in its Revenue Enablement function, and the Sales Enablement Program Manager is central to that effort. This is a hands-on, high-impact role focused on sharpening the skills, process discipline, and execution of our DBU sales teams — Field Sales, Hybrid Field Sales, Strategic Sales, and Inside Sales.

You’ll spend the majority of your time embedded in the flow of the sales org: coaching reps and frontline managers, reinforcing our sales process and methodology, and building the programs, content, and tools that help sellers win. You’ll also serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership — bringing field insight and enablement expertise into decisions about process, change, and go-to-market execution. This is a builder’s role on a growing team, so you’ll help shape how enablement operates at CARFAX while delivering results from day one.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Enable all DBU sales roles.Serve as the dedicated enablement partner to Field Sales, Strategic Sales, and Inside Sales — tailoring programs, coaching, and content to the distinct motions, customer profiles, and performance goals of each team. One size doesn’t fit all; what works for a field rep calling on independent dealers is different from what an inside seller needs to convert on the phone.
  • Build and lead training and coaching.Own the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of sales training on core selling fundamentals — discovery, value articulation, objection handling, negotiation, and pipeline management. Provide hands-on coaching to reps and managers through field ride-alongs, call reviews, and deal reviews. Equip frontline managers to reinforce these skills with their own teams so your impact scales across the org. Best-in-class enablement functions treat training as a continuous discipline, not a one-time event — this mindset is the foundation of the role.
  • Reinforce process, methodology, and tools.Drive consistent adoption of CARFAX’s sales process and methodology through sustained, ongoing reinforcement. Champion adoption of the supporting tech stack — CRM, conversation intelligence, enablement platforms — so reps work smarter and sales leaders have the visibility they need to coach effectively.
  • Build assets and codify best practices.Create and maintain polished, field-ready sales assets — playbooks, battle cards, talk tracks, pitch decks, and process guides. Surface what top performers do differently through field observation, call reviews, and win/loss patterns, and systematically distribute those insights across the sales org. Ensuring reps have access to the right content at the right moment in the sales cycle is a core enablement discipline.
  • Partner on the onboarding handoff.Work closely with the Onboarding Lead to ensure a seamless transition from new hire onboarding into ongoing, role-based enablement. This role does not own onboarding, but its success depends on a tight partnership with the person who does.
  • Serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership.Act as a trusted advisor to DBU sales leadership on how to raise seller performance and execution quality. Bring the field’s perspective into internal decisions on process roll-outs, change management, and product launches — ensuring the field is ready to execute before go-to-market, not after.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally.Partner with Revenue Operations to define and track the KPIs that demonstrate enablement’s impact on pipeline health, conversion rates, and revenue performance. Partner with Marketing on sales assets, messaging, and go-to-market motions — so programs are data-informed and what reps carry into the field is aligned, current, and on-brand.

What we’re looking for:

Required

  • 3+ years of sales enablement experience, ideally supporting multiple, distinct sales motions simultaneously.
  • Experience carrying a sales quota — you’ve sold, and you understand the seller’s world firsthand.
  • A demonstrated track record of designing and delivering training and coaching programs that measurably change rep behavior and drive revenue outcomes.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, and coaching skills — both in-person and virtually — including the ability to create compelling, polished presentations in PowerPoint (or equivalent tools).
  • The ability to build trust and influence without authority across reps, managers, senior leadership, and cross-functional partners.
  • Comfort operating in a build-from-scratch environment where structure, programs, and processes don’t fully exist yet — and you’ll help create them.
  • Experience with a formal sales methodology (e.g., MEDDIC/MEDDPICC, Integrity Selling, Challenger, SPIN, or similar) and a track record of reinforcing it in the field over time.
  • Ability to travel up to 10% of the time to coach reps in the field and support team events.

Preferred

  • Automotive industry or automotive technology experience — familiarity with how dealerships operate, how they buy, and what they value is a meaningful advantage in this role.
  • Experience supporting a blend of field, strategic/enterprise, and inside sales teams within a single organization.
  • Hands-on experience with conversation intelligence tools (e.g., Gong, Chorus), Salesforce, learning management systems (LMS), and content management systems (CMS).

What’s in it for you:

  • Competitive compensation, benefits and generous time-off policies
  • 4-Day summer work weeks and a winter holiday break
  • 401(k) / DCPP matching
  • Annual bonus program
  • Casual, dog-friendly, and innovative office spaces.

Don’t just take our word for it:

  • 13x VA Best Places to Work
  • 12x Top Workplaces in Washington (Presented by The Washington Post and WTOP)
  • 9x Washingtonian Great Place to Work
  • 5x USA Today Top Workplaces
  • 5x St. Louis Post-Dispatch Best Places to Work

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $110,000 - $150,000. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on a variety of factors, including geographic location, relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

jobs.title: Senior Level Designer
jobs.excerpt: Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love.
jobs.description:
Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line.

With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built-in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years.

This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles.

What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world’s best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor.

Since the start, we’ve raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who’ve built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones.

At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

The opportunity

You’ll be the keeper of the player experience on our hybrid casual RPG. Combat, heroes, art, and features all come together in the levels you build, and you decide whether that adds up to something players want to come back to.

You’ll join a small, AI-native game team on its way to launch. You’ll own the level design area completely: you set the roadmap, make the calls, and ship. A dedicated level editor and an AI-powered level generation pipeline will be ready on day one, so you spend your time on what matters: making every level fun.

What you’ll do

  • Build. Design, build, and tune levels directly in Unity, covering layouts, encounters, pacing and difficulty.
  • Scale. Triple our level content by combining our AI pipeline with your own design judgment.
  • Balance. Model how health, damage, and stat changes affect the numbers before anything ships.
  • Polish. Bring existing levels to final quality and give them the feel and juice that make players stay.
  • Own. Set the level design roadmap, make design calls, and question whether each choice fits the game.
  • Specify. Write clear, detailed specs that developers can implement as written.
  • Learn from players. Use playtests and player data to see what works and iterate quickly.
  • AI. Use AI every day to generate layouts, prototype encounters, simulate balancing, and automate level work.

Requirements

  • Years of level design experience, with shipped levels on a hybrid casual, RPG or combat-based game.
  • Hands-on balancing skills: you’re comfortable with stats, health and damage maths, and spreadsheets.
  • Fluency in Unity: you build and iterate levels in the engine yourself.
  • A strong sense of game feel: you know when a level is fun, and you can explain why.
  • AI is already part of how you work every day. You've used it to automate, speed up, or rethink.
  • The autonomy to build your own roadmap and make design decisions.
  • A data-driven approach to level tuning.
  • Feature design experience alongside level design.

For this role, you’ll also bring

  • Extreme ownership. You drive outcomes. When something breaks, you fix it instead of explaining why it broke.
  • Proactive. You don’t wait for instructions or perfect conditions. You spot what needs doing and do it.
  • Pragmatism and simplicity. You look for the simplest solution that works, use whatever tools are available, and ship.
  • Sharp thinking. You learn fast, reason from facts, and structure your ideas clearly.
  • Hungry and motivated. You’re ambitious, high-energy, and grounded.

Even if you don’t check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we’re more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Why Homa

  • Exceptional growth. We hire people of outstanding potential, then put them where they can grow fastest.
  • Real ownership. You own the player experience of a game, and you’ll see your levels move the metrics.
  • The right tools from day one. A dedicated level editor and an AI level pipeline, so you focus on design.
  • A high talent bar. Our teams are small and ambiti us, and the people around you will push you to grow.
  • AI at the core. You’ll have access to the best AI tools, and you’ll help shape how level design works in an AI-first company.

Benefits

At Homa, we prioritize talent, energy, and determination over traditional credentials. We’re building a global community of brilliant, driven people who think boldly, act with pragmatism, move fast, and push boundaries. We believe true innovation comes from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and curiosity without limits. Our culture is grounded in four core values:

  • Humility: We recognise that we are always learning, we can always improve and grow.
  • Curiosity: We continuously seek the “why” behind the “what” - we explore with purpose and practicality.
  • Focus: Our curiosity takes us deeper, not wider - we obsess over the details and let pragmatism guide our attention.
  • Ambition: We strive for the best - we don’t settle for “good enough,” - we use common sense to reach higher.

Benefits

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here’s what you can expect:

  • 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you’ll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.
  • 🏢 Paris HQ Access: Enjoy a desk at our private office in a well-located WeWork building that will give you access to WeWork perks like rooftop view and designed coworking spaces.
  • 🌍 Coworking Access: You will have access to WeWork spaces throughout Europe, along with all their perks and professional office environments.
  • 🌐 Global Team: Collaborate in English with top-tier talent from 35+ countries, spanning Europe, the UK, the US, and more. Diversity fuels our creativity and innovation.
  • ✈️ Team Gatherings: We value time together beyond the screen. Join us for occasional team gatherings, off-site retreats (Workations as we name them) to connect, recharge, and celebrate.
  • 📈 Performance Reviews: We’re committed to your growth. Every six months, we reflect on your progress, recognize your achievements, and align on clear development goals.
  • 💻 Equipment Support: From day one, we’ll provide everything you need to do your best work, including a home office setup allowance if you're working remotely.

Where We Hire

Our HQ in Paris is a vibrant hub of creativity, collaboration, and connection. From rooftop lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, we’ve designed a space people genuinely enjoy - all within a cozy WeWork filled with good energy (and snacks).

We also have incredible team members across Europe - from Spain and Turkey to Germany, North Macedonia, Poland, the UK, and more. Whether you’re working from a sunny WeWork in Barcelona or your home setup in Warsaw, you’re fully part of our culture. To keep collaboration smooth, we primarily hire within European time zones (UTC to UTC+3). If you're based there - or planning to be - we’d love to hear from you!

Please note: this is one remote position open to multiple countries, not multiple openings.

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

We are seeking a Principal Modem PHY IP Design Verification Engineer to lead and execute verification of advanced modem PHY IP for the Terawave program. This role is responsible for developing robust verification strategies, building scalable verification environments, and ensuring high-quality modem PHY IP delivery for next-generation wireless ASIC platforms.

The ideal candidate combines strong digital design verification skills with a solid understanding of modem PHY and DSP systems. This engineer will work closely with PHY architects, RTL designers, systems engineers, firmware, FPGA, and validation teams to verify functionality, performance, and integration of modem PHY IP across simulation, emulation, prototyping, and silicon bring-up phases.

omodulation and demodulation

otiming and frequency synchronization

ochannel estimation and equalization

oMIMO / beamforming support

oFEC integration

ocontrol, configuration, and status interfaces

oimpairment handling and recovery behavior

· Identify, debug, and root-cause design and integration issues in collaboration with RTL and architecture teams.

· Support verification of performance-sensitive designs with attention to throughput, latency, buffering, and protocol timing behavior.

· Contribute to regression automation, CI flows, and verification infrastructure improvements.

oOFDM and/or single-carrier systems

osynchronization

ochannel estimation and equalization

oFEC such as LDPC, Polar, Turbo, or BCH

oMIMO / beamforming

ofixed-point and quantized signal processing

ommWave / sub-THz / Terahertz systems

osatellite or space communications

The barrier between imagination and reality has dissolved. As our AI Content Creator, you are the pioneer of our "Synthetic Production" arm. You aren't just writing prompts; you are integrating generative video, image, and audio tools into professional commercial workflows.

You will help us scale content production by generating hyper-realistic B-roll, impossible environments, and rapid-fire concepts that speed up our entire creative engine. If you spend your nights on Discord testing new models and your days dreaming of ComfyUI workflows, this is your launchpad.

What You’ll Do

  1. Generate High-Fidelity Assets

    • Create stunning, photo-real images and video clips using Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Runway (Gen-2/Gen-3), Pika, and Sora (as available).

    • Generate specific creative assets: product backgrounds, atmospheric B-roll, and surreal visual effects that blend seamlessly with live-action footage.

    • Utilize AI audio tools (ElevenLabs, Suno) to generate realistic voice-overs and custom background tracks for testing and final delivery.

  2. Hybrid Editing & Compositing

    • Take AI-generated assets and integrate them into video timelines.

    • Use After Effects and Photoshop to "fix" AI artifacts (glitchy hands, text errors) and composite products into AI-generated environments.

    • Upscale and interpolate footage (Topaz Video AI) to ensure all AI output meets broadcast 4K standards.

  3. Rapid Concepting & Storyboarding

    • Replace traditional stick-figure storyboards with fully rendered AI animatics, allowing clients to visualize the final commercial before we even turn on a camera.

    • Speed up the pre-production process by visualizing lighting setups and set designs virtually.

  4. Stay on the Bleeding Edge

    • Constantly test new models, LoRAs, and control nets. You are the agency's R&D department for creativity.

    • Build efficient workflows (e.g., ComfyUI pipelines) that allow other editors to utilize AI tools easily.

Who You Are

  1. A "Prompt Engineer" & Artist

    • You have a deep understanding of prompt syntax, negative prompting, seeds, and weights. You know how to get exactly what you want from the AI.

    • You have a strong foundation in traditional art/photography principles (composition, lighting, color theory)—AI is just your brush.

    • Proficiency in Midjourney, Runway, and ElevenLabs is required.

    • Strong working knowledge of Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects. You need to be able to use what you generate.

    • Experience with Stable Diffusion (Automatic1111 or ComfyUI) is a massive plus.

  3. Problem Solver

    • AI is unpredictable. You have the patience to iterate 50 times to get the perfect 3-second clip.

    • You know how to troubleshoot consistency issues (keeping a character's face the same across multiple shots).

  4. Ethically Aware

    • You understand the legal landscape of AI. You know how to create commercially safe content (avoiding copyright infringement or deepfaking real celebrities without permission).

  • Tool Access: We provide enterprise access to the top AI tools and unlimited compute credits.

  • Relentless Innovation Culture: Move fast, test constantly, and collaborate with some of the most creative minds in social media and video production.
