We attract, develop, and retain a high-performance workforce, comprised of people with diverse backgrounds and a shared drive for excellence. We strive to foster a positive and inclusive work environment that helps employees, and communities, thrive.


Our Purpose

TERADYNE, where experience meets innovation and driving excellence in every connection. We are fueled by creativity and diversity of thought and in our workforce. Our employees are supported to innovate and learn something new every day.

We cultivate a culture of inclusion for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better business results.


Opportunity Overview

As a Senior ML / AI Engineer at Teradyne, you will design, build, and operationalize the machine learning and AI solutions that power our IT organization, and you will prepare the team—technically and operationally—to own the AI solutions Teradyne develops internally. Reporting to the Enterprise AI/Data Product Manager within the Enterprise Architecture and Data organization, you will bridge solution development and production ownership, ensuring our AI solutions are reliable, governed, and sustainable long after they are first built.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role spanning classical machine learning and modern generative and agentic AI. You will develop ML/AI solutions requested by the IT organization—predictive and classification models, GenAI assistants, RAG workflows, and intelligent automation—and engineer the MLOps/LLMOps practices, pipelines, and playbooks that allow the team to operate and continuously improve them. You will work across our enterprise AI stack—primarily Microsoft Azure (Azure AI Foundry and Microsoft Copilot Studio), Anthropic Claude, and Google Vertex AI and Snowflake Cortex AI—grounding solutions in trusted enterprise data and integrating with enterprise systems through MCP servers and secure APIs. Your work ensures Teradyne’s AI investments move from experimentation to durable, production-grade capabilities.


ML/AI Solution Development for IT

  • Partner with the AI Enablement Team and the IT organization to translate business problems into ML/AI solutions—predictive and classification models, GenAI assistants, RAG workflows, and intelligent process automation.
  • Design, develop, train, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end ML and generative AI solutions using Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex AI.
  • Build and integrate AI agents with enterprise data sources, APIs, and MCP servers, grounding models in proprietary Teradyne data through embedding and retrieval pipelines.
  • Apply rigorous experimentation, model selection, and evaluation to deliver solutions that are accurate, performant, and fit for purpose.

Business Outcome: Deliver high-value, production-ready ML/AI solutions that solve real IT and business problems and demonstrate measurable impact.


Operationalizing & Owning Internally Developed AI Solutions

  • Own the transition of internally developed AI solutions from build to production, defining and certifying the release-readiness in accordance to standard set by the AI Platform Operations Team.
  • Implement full model lifecycle management—versioning, model registry, retraining, promotion, and deprecation—so solutions remain accurate and maintainable over time.
  • Define drift, degradation, and retraining criteria for deployed models and agents, and drive tuning and remediation of the underlying solution for the AI Platform Operations Team to execute scheduled retraining and registry operations against these criteria.
  • Partner with the AI Platform Operations Engineer, providing the technical input—model and agent behavior, dependencies, failure modes—needed for the run-books, on-call processes, and handoff standards they own and author.

Business Outcome: Ensure internally developed AI solutions are durable, well-owned, and continuously improved rather than one-off builds.


MLOps / LLMOps Engineering & Automation

  • Engineer reusable, multi-environment MLOps/LLMOps pipelines using Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions to automate the full lifecycle from training and evaluation to deployment.
  • Build CI/CD, testing, and infrastructure-/configuration-as-code for models, prompts, and agents to make releases repeatable, testable, and auditable.
  • Leverage tooling such as Azure Machine Learning, MLflow, and model/feature registries to standardize experimentation, tracking, and deployment.
  • Establish automated evaluation and regression testing (including offline and online evaluation) for both predictive and generative solutions.
  • Design MLOps/LLMOps pipelines for the AI Platform Operations Team to operate in production once deployed, ensuring pipelines are supportable, observable, and handoff-ready.

Business Outcome: Provide standardized, automated delivery pipelines that increase speed, quality, and reliability of AI solution releases.


Team Technical & Process Readiness

  • Establish the technical standards, reference patterns, and reusable frameworks the team needs to build and operate AI solutions consistently.
  • Define and document the processes and playbooks—development, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and support—that prepare the team to own AI solutions end-to-end.
  • Mentor and upskill engineers on ML/AI, MLOps/LLMOps, and agentic AI practices, raising the overall capability and readiness of the team.
  • Champion adoption of best practices and lessons learned across projects to mature the team’s AI operating model.

Business Outcome: Ensure the team is technically and process-ready to own and scale AI solutions with confidence and consistency.


Responsible AI, Governance & Reliability

  • Implement responsible AI practices and technical guardrails for data handling, model usage, and safe, compliant AI behavior.
  • Apply AI security controls to models, agents, and RAG workflows, mitigating risks such as prompt injection and unauthorized data access.
  • Build observability, logging, and audit trails for AI solutions to support explainability, compliance, and troubleshooting.
  • Monitor solution performance, quality, reliability, and cost, and drive continuous improvement against defined metrics.

Business Outcome: Reduce AI risk and improve trust, compliance, and reliability across Teradyne’s deployed AI solutions.


All About You

We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position.

  • 8–10 years of experience in ML/AI or software engineering, including at least 3 years building and operating production ML/AI systems and recent hands-on experience with generative and agentic AI.
  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience with ML frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.
  • Hands-on experience building and deploying ML and generative AI solutions with one or more enterprise AI platforms: Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Anthorpic Claude, Cursor, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex AI.
  • Proven MLOps/LLMOps experience—multi-environment pipelines, CI/CD (Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions), Azure Machine Learning, MLflow, and model lifecycle management.
  • Experience with agentic AI orchestration frameworks, RAG, vector databases and embeddings, prompt engineering, and integration via MCP servers and APIs.
  • Experience transitioning AI solutions from development into production ownership, including monitoring, drift detection, retraining, and support.
  • Strong knowledge of model evaluation and testing, AI observability, responsible AI, AI security, and governance frameworks.
  • Multicloud experience with Microsoft Azure as primary and Google Cloud as secondary, integrating with enterprise data on Snowflake and Microsoft Fabric.
  • Poven ability to mentor and upskill teams, fostering a culture of innovation and learning.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across technical and business teams.
  • Analytical mindset with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.

Software Engineer, External Integrations & Data

Location: Remote Canada

Employment Type: Full-time

Level: Senior Software Engineer

About the company

Our Series A client is transforming the building supply industry through innovative technology. Their integrated commerce platform enables independent building suppliers to streamline operations, enhance customer service, and deliver exceptional digital buying experiences. By connecting sales, accounts receivable, operations, and customer engagement into one seamless solution, they help their customers operate more efficiently and drive growth.

Their team is made up of curious, entrepreneurial problem-solvers who thrive in a fast-paced environment. They value innovation, collaboration, and ownership, with a shared focus on building practical solutions that create meaningful impact for their customers and the industry as a whole.

About the Role

We’re looking for a resourceful Software Engineer who thrives on solving problems where the path forward isn’t always obvious. You’ll work on building systems that interact with external platforms, services, and data sources — particularly in situations where official APIs are limited, unavailable, or insufficient for the job.

This role is ideal for an engineer with experience in web scraping, reverse engineering, or building integrations with third-party systems that weren’t necessarily designed to be integrated with.

You’ll help us connect to external sources, extract and normalize messy or unstructured data, and turn it into reliable, structured information that can power modern AI-driven applications. We’re looking for someone who enjoys figuring out how things work under the hood, navigating undocumented systems, and building robust solutions to complex technical challenges.

What You’ll Do

  • Build integrations without traditional APIs: Develop systems that interact with external websites, platforms, and services when official APIs are unavailable, incomplete, or too restrictive.

  • Develop data acquisition pipelines: Collect, extract, and transform data from diverse external sources, including HTML pages, dynamic web applications, documents, and unstructured content.

  • Reverse engineer external systems: Analyze network requests, browser behavior, page structures, and undocumented interfaces to understand how external systems operate.

  • Build scraping and automation tools: Use technologies such as browser automation, HTTP clients, headless browsers, and custom extraction logic to retrieve data reliably.

  • Clean and normalize messy data: Transform inconsistent, duplicated, incomplete, or poorly structured data into clean, standardized formats suitable for downstream applications and AI workflows.

  • Build resilient systems: Design integrations that can handle changing page layouts, evolving external systems, rate limits, authentication flows, and unexpected failures.

  • Leverage AI for data processing: Explore ways to use LLMs and other AI techniques to extract, classify, enrich, validate, and structure data from unstructured sources.

  • Improve reliability and scalability: Implement monitoring, retries, validation, error handling, and automated testing to ensure integrations remain dependable over time.

  • Collaborate across engineering and product: Work with other engineers to turn ambiguous requirements and unfamiliar external systems into practical, maintainable solutions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Professional software engineering experience building production-quality applications, integrations, or data pipelines.

  • Experience with at least one of the following:

    • Web scraping or large-scale data extraction.

    • Reverse engineering or working with undocumented interfaces.

    • Building integrations with third-party platforms that lack robust APIs.

    • Extracting, transforming, and cleaning data from inconsistent external sources.

  • Strong proficiency in a language such as Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript.

  • Experience working with HTTP, REST concepts, HTML, DOM structures, JSON, .Net C# and network requests.

  • An understanding of authentication, cookies, sessions, pagination, rate limiting, and other challenges associated with external integrations.

  • Experience designing maintainable software that can adapt when external systems change.

  • Strong debugging and analytical skills, with the ability to investigate unfamiliar systems and work through ambiguous technical problems.

  • A pragmatic, resourceful mindset and a willingness to experiment, prototype, and find creative solutions.

What Success Looks Like

  • You can take an unfamiliar external platform and figure out how to retrieve the information we need, even when there isn't a straightforward API.

  • You can turn inconsistent, dirty, or unstructured external data into clean, usable, structured datasets.

  • You build integrations that remain reliable even as external systems evolve.

  • You can move from investigation and proof of concept to production-ready software without sacrificing maintainability.

  • You consistently find practical solutions to problems that don't have an obvious playbook.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a software engineer who enjoys the investigative side of engineering. They might have built scrapers, reverse-engineered web applications, developed browser automation, or created integrations with platforms that weren't designed to expose their data.

They don't necessarily need experience in every area listed above. We're more interested in someone who has demonstrated the ability to figure out how external systems work, access and interpret data, and build reliable software around systems they don't control.

This is not simply a traditional API integration role. It's an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of external systems, data acquisition, data quality, and AI

ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

This team covers our customers in PST therefore must be based in one of the following states: California, Washington, Oregon, or Nevada.

As a Project Manager, you will be the operational backbone of our enterprise sales process. You will partner directly with Account Executives to manage the complete order-to-delivery lifecycle for clients, ensuring flawless execution and exceptional customer experience. Working alongside the West Coast-based sales team, you will leverage deep product knowledge and operational excellence to support deal closure and drive client satisfaction. Your role is critical to scaling our enterprise business while maintaining the quality and attention to detail that defines Quince.

Responsibilities

  • Assume deal ownership post-sale, from logo approval through invoicing, delivery and issue resolution

Qualifications

  • Experience managing internal and external stakeholders with distinct approaches
  • Self-starter comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
  • Extremely detail-oriented with ability to operate with a sense of urgency

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

jobs.excerpt: Bausch + Lomb (NYSE/TSX: BLCO) is a leading global eye health company dedicated to protecting and enhancing the gift of sight for millions of people around the world—from the moment of birth through every phase of life.
jobs.description:
Bausch + Lomb (NYSE/TSX: BLCO) is a leading global eye health company dedicated to protecting and enhancing the gift of sight for millions of people around the world—from the moment of birth through every phase of life. Our mission is simple, yet powerful: helping you see better, to live better.

Our comprehensive portfolio of over 400 products is fully integrated and built to serve our customers across the full spectrum of their eye health needs throughout their lives. Our iconic brand is built on the deep trust and loyalty of our customers established over our 170-year history. We have a significant global research, development, manufacturing and commercial footprint of approximately 13,000 employees and a presence in approximately 100 countries, extending our reach to billions of potential customers across the globe. We have long been associated with many of the most significant advances in eye health, and we believe we are well positioned to continue leading the advancement of eye health in the future.

Objectives:

To provide scientific and strategic leadership for all bioanalysis supporting Bausch + Lomb ocular therapeutic programs, from discovery through registration and lifecycle management, across small molecule and large molecule modalities.

Bioanalytical work is currently fully outsourced. The position owns that externalized model end to end — strategy, contract research organization (CRO) selection and governance, and accountability for data quality and regulatory defensibility. Should capital investment be approved, the position is expected to lead the establishment of an internal non-GLP bioanalytical laboratory within approximately the next two years, without interrupting program support.

Responsibilities:

Bioanalytical strategy and program support

  • Define and own integrated bioanalytical strategies across small and large molecules, oligonucleotides, biomarkers and anti-drug antibody (ADA) / neutralizing antibody assessment, selecting platforms appropriate to each modality and matrix (LC-MS/MS, ligand-binding assays, hybrid LC-MS, qPCR/ddPCR).
  • Represent bioanalysis on cross-functional program teams, translating program questions (dose selection, ocular and systemic exposure, PK/PD, target engagement) into fit-for-purpose analytical plans.
  • Establish the tiered assay approach across the portfolio — discovery/exploratory, GLP-validated and GCP-compliant clinical bioanalysis — with clear criteria for the level of validation rigor applied at each stage.
  • Author the bioanalytical sections of INDs, IMPDs and NDAs/BLAs, respond to health authority questions, and represent bioanalysis in regulatory interactions and inspections.

Biomarkers and translational analytics

  • Lead biomarker assay strategy from exploratory through validated — target engagement, pharmacodynamics, disease progression and patient selection — partnering with Clinical Evidence, Translational Development and Research on fit-for-purpose validation and context of use.

External partner (CRO) governance

  • Own the bioanalytical CRO landscape: identify, technically qualify, select and manage vendors across modalities and geographies, and negotiate scope, timelines and budgets with Procurement.
  • Provide scientific oversight of outsourced method development, validation and sample analysis — reviewing protocols, reports and data and approving deviations and investigations — and monitor partner performance against quality, turnaround and incurred sample reanalysis metrics consistent with GLP and GCP expectations.

Internal non-GLP laboratory build (anticipated)

  • With management, develop the business case, capability roadmap and phased investment plan for the internal laboratory, including make-versus-buy analysis and modality prioritization.
  • If approved, lead design and execution: facility fit-out, instrument selection, LIMS and chromatography data system architecture with data integrity and access controls appropriate to a non-GLP research environment, and sample management.
  • Recruit, onboard and develop the internal scientific team, and define the enduring hybrid model of internal capability combined with strategic outsourcing.

Leadership, compliance and budget

  • Build, lead and mentor a team of scientists; set objectives, manage performance and foster a culture of scientific rigor and data integrity.
  • Ensure externally conducted regulated bioanalysis complies with GLP, GCP, ICH M10 and Bausch + Lomb quality, data governance and EHS policies, and that internal non-GLP work operates to documented data-quality standards with non-GLP data clearly identified wherever reported.
  • Manage departmental operating and capital budgets and resource planning; maintain awareness of emerging bioanalytical technologies and ocular-specific methodologies.

Requirements:

Education

  • Ph.D. in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, pharmacology, immunology or a related discipline with 10+ years of industry experience; or M.S. with 14+; or B.S. with 16+.

Required experience

  • Demonstrated bioanalytical leadership in pharmaceutical or biotechnology development spanning both small and large molecules / biologics, with hands-on or oversight expertise across LC-MS/MS and ligand-binding platforms.
  • Track record in regulated bioanalysis (GLP) supporting IND, NDA and/or BLA submissions, including authorship of regulatory content.
  • Substantial experience managing bioanalytical CROs as sponsor-side lead, accountable for outsourced data quality and defensibility.
  • People leadership experience hiring and developing scientific staff; deep knowledge of ICH M10, FDA immunogenicity guidance and 21 CFR Part 11.

Strongly preferred

  • Demonstrated competence in implementing artificial intelligence (AI) into bioanalytical workflows — for example AI-assisted method development, peak detection and integration,
    or automated data review — with an understanding of the traceability and data integrity obligations that apply when such tools influence reportable results.
  • Ocular drug development experience, including familiarity with ocular tissue and fluid matrices and low-volume assay design.
  • Experience establishing or expanding a bioanalytical laboratory, including facility design, instrument qualification and laboratory automation.

Competencies

  • Strategic, build-oriented mindset comfortable establishing a function with no existing internal infrastructure; comfort with ambiguity, capital planning and matrixed decision-making; strong scientific judgment distinguishing fit-for-purpose from over-engineered approaches.
  • Scientific skepticism about where new tools, including AI, add genuine value versus unacceptable risk.
  • Excellent influencing and communication skills with non-bioanalytical stakeholders across Clinical, Regulatory, CMC and Quality.

This position may be available in the following location(s): US - Remote

Location: Remote- Eligible US Locations

About the role and about You:

Great support starts with great training. When our members hit a snag, our Community Support team gets them back into Watopia and helps them make the most of their Zwift experience. To help support our frontline agents, we’re hiring a hands-on Training Specialist to build and maintain the training they rely on.

Our training program already has a strong foundation: a structured new hire curriculum, an established design framework, and experienced subject matter expert trainers who facilitate instructor-led training. In this role, you’ll keep that program accurate and effective as Zwift evolves. When products, processes, or policies change, you’ll revise new hire training and build and deploy update training to match. When the team identifies a need for refresh training, you’ll build it. When something new and complex launches, you’ll be a crucial part of supporting it.

You’ll be a part of our Content & Learning team, who own training, user-facing self-service content, and the internal knowledge enabling Zwift’s support team. In this role, you’ll also be the subject-matter expert in Seismic, our learning management system, ensuring we’re maximizing the benefits of the tool, keeping groups and enrollments clean, tracking completion and assessment results, and partnering with our BPO partners to close gaps.

You’re organized, dependable, and easy to work with. You take direction well, own your work from start to finish, and partner effectively with your teammates. You know when to hold firm on accuracy and when to flex on format or timing. You’re comfortable working outside a defined box: you pick up new tools, figure things out on your own, take on new work as the team’s needs change, and handle shifting priorities with ease. You use AI thoughtfully, knowing where it speeds up work and where human validation is essential.

What you’ll do:

  • Develop new eLearning and instructor-led training (including exams and certifications) to support product launches and updated policies and procedures, while keeping existing training current.
  • Build and deploy refresh training when the team identifies a need, indicated by QA results, Customer Effort Scores, or related performance data.
  • Host train-the-trainer sessions to prepare subject matter expert (SME) trainers for seasonal new hire classes and update training rollouts.
  • Run regular audits of training materials with SMEs to catch inaccurate, outdated, or missing information.
  • Build and sustain strong working relationships with SME trainers, partner teams, and BPO leaders, rooting feedback in curiosity and respect while openly receiving it in return.
  • Own Seismic (our LMS): managing distribution groups, reporting on completion and assessment results, and working with BPO leaders to close gaps. Explore unused and emerging features, while recommending ones worth adopting.

  • 2+ years of instructional design, training, or learning and development experience.
  • Experience building eLearning, instructor-led training, and assessments using ADDIE or a similar model, with tools such as Articulate or Camtasia.
  • Familiar with Kirkpatrick or a similar model for measuring training effectiveness.
  • Experience as an LMS administrator using tools like Seismic (formerly Lessonly), Docebo, or equivalent, including user groups, enrollments, and reporting.
  • Experience facilitating virtual training, including train-the-trainer sessions, ideally with globally distributed or BPO teams.
  • Flexibility with an eagerness to support your team beyond training when priorities shift, whether for a short-term need or a longer-term change in focus.

Bonus points:

  • A passion for cycling, running, or fitness.
  • Experience supporting both internal and BPO (outsourced) contact center teams.
  • Familiarity with Zwift, gaming, the software industry, or fitness technology.

Your resume/CV is enough to show off your skills, accomplishments, and experience. However, if you choose to include a cover letter introducing us to your awesome personality, we will read that too.

About Us:

Zeitview is the leading intelligent aerial imaging company for high-value infrastructure, providing businesses with actionable, real-time insights to recover revenue, reduce risk and improve build quality. Trusted by the largest enterprises in the world, Zeitview is active in over 70 countries. Our mission is to accelerate the global transition to renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure through advanced inspection solutions. Take a look at our latest achievements here!

This role in one paragraph:

Be the voice of the customer for an entire industry at Zeitview. You will be Zeitview's resident expert for our Oil & Gas vertical. You own problem definition: understanding what enterprise customers in your vertical actually need, why they need it, and what it's worth. You run discovery, build client relationships alongside sales, synthesize market signals, and translate all of that into clear, prioritized requirements that our platform product managers and engineering teams can execute against. You are responsible for competitive intel and defining metrics to demonstrate the success of the product and strategies. You should be growth focused. You will not just iterate on our existing product/service offerings but propose business cases and GTM for expanding our offerings. You do not own the product backlog or ship software directly, you own the "what" and "why," then work with solutions-side PMs to negotiate the "how" and "when."

What you'll actually do in the first 6 months:

  • Define what "success" looks like for the Oil & Gas vertical in terms that connect to revenue, retention, and customer outcomes, not just feature delivery
  • Embed with 3–5 strategic accounts within our Oil & Gas portfolio. Not to sell, but to understand their inspection workflows, pain points, and decision-making structures deeply enough to write requirements they'd recognize as their own
  • Run structured discovery across a mix of methods (customer interviews, operational ride-alongs, competitive analysis, usage data) and synthesize findings into a prioritized problem set for your vertical
  • Negotiate with platform PMs over engineering capacity, making the case for your vertical's priorities with data and customer evidence, not volume
  • Write requirements that hold up under engineering scrutiny: specific enough to build from, flexible enough to serve platform-wide
  • Build internal credibility as the person who knows your industry better than anyone else in the building

This role is NOT:

  • A platform-building role. You will not own a product backlog, write technical specs, or ship software with engineers day-to-day. If that's what you're looking for, see our Senior Product Manager - Asset Insights posting.
  • A pure strategy role, with no customer contact. You will be on calls with enterprise clients regularly. You will travel to sites. You will see the physical infrastructure your product serves.
  • A people management role. You will coordinate across functions and informally guide others, but you will not have direct reports.

  • Bachelor's degree (or higher) in a science, technology, or related field, or equivalent work experience
  • 8+ years of professional experience, with 5+ years in product management, solutions consulting, technical sales, or a comparable customer-facing role in enterprise software
  • Deep domain expertise in Oil & Gas. "Deep" means you can walk onto a customer site and understand what you're looking at: the assets, the inspection workflows, the regulatory context, and the business model.
  • You have a track record of building trusted relationships with enterprise customers and converting those relationships into product insight, not just feature requests, but an understanding of underlying needs
  • You can run structured discovery and synthesize qualitative and quantitative inputs into a prioritized problem set that other teams can act on
  • You have commercial acumen: you understand how product decisions connect to pipeline, deal size, retention, and competitive positioning in your vertical
  • Exceptional communication skills. You can present to a customer's VP of Asset Management on Monday and translate that conversation into a product brief for solutions PMs and Engineering on Tuesday
  • Willingness to travel to customer sites and inspection locations

Strongly preferred: These will move you to the top:

  • Experience working with operational or service delivery teams (field inspection, drone operations, or similar)
  • Experience with geospatial data, remote sensing, or asset management platforms
  • Familiarity with AI/ML-powered products, enough to assess where these capabilities address real vertical problems vs. where they're a distraction
  • Experience with go-to-market strategy: product launches, positioning, pricing, or vertical-specific marketing
  • Experience in mobile application development

What’s Included:

  • Feel great about your work as you join a leading mission-driven intelligent aerial imaging company - our goal is to accelerate the global transition to renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure, and you personally will play a large part in making this happen!
  • Competitive base salary, annual bonus and stock options
  • Your choice of multiple medical insurance plans, including options with an HSA and 100% coverage of the premium for yourself and your dependents
  • Unlimited PTO: We mean it when we say we prioritize work-life balance and mental health
  • Autonomy and upward mobility
  • Diverse, equitable, and inclusive culture: a place where your voice matters

This role has a base salary range of $160,000 - $180,000 USD, plus a target annual bonus and eligibility for stock options. Actual compensation may vary based on experience, skills, and location within USA.

Make an Impact

Trillium Health Resources is a Tailored Plan and Managed Care Organization (MCO) serving 46 counties across North Carolina. We manage services for individuals with serious mental health needs, substance use disorders, traumatic brain injuries, and intellectual/development (IDD) disabilities. Our mission is to help individuals and families build strong foundations for healthy, fulfilling lives.

Why Work for Us?

Trillium believes that empowering others begins with supporting our team. We offer our employees:

  • A collaborative, mission-driven work environment
  • Competitive benefits and work-from-home options for most positions
  • Opportunities for professional growth in a diverse inclusive culture

Every day, our work changes lives – from children thriving through early intervention and school-based therapies, to adults with severe mental illness living independently and contributing to their communities.

If you are looking for a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact on the lives of others, apply today!

What We’re Looking For

Trillium Health Resources has a career opening for a Care Manager - Innovations Waiver (IW) to join our Care Management Team! The Care Manager – IW is responsible for providing complex care coordination and monitoring to members having a primary Intellectual or Developmental Disability, which may include secondary mental health or substance abuse, and/or complex medical/physical health needs. This position requires a dynamic, proactive approach to assessment, monitoring, and complex coordination of care, to ensure quality support and consistent adherence to waiver requirements. The Care Manager – IW assists with integrated care management through multi-disciplinary collaboration and referrals. This position has a primary focus on members who have Intellectual Developmental Disability, serving both children, adolescents, and adults. The individual must be dependable, organized, able to multitask, and communicate effectively, with strong reasoning and problem‑solving skills, including in crisis situations.

On a typical day, you might:

  • Utilize person centered planning methods/strategies to gather information, to get to know the members supported and to adequately address specific needs of the individual.
  • Provide education and support to members in learning about and exercising rights and responsibilities.
  • Consistently complete Discovery activities (information gathering and assessment) as a component of the planning process.
  • Ensure that members/legally responsible people are informed of services available (all types of Medicaid and state-funded services), service options available (e.g. Individual/Family Direction for Innovations participants), processes (e.g. requirements for specific service), Natural and community services, and so forth.
  • Assist members/legally responsible people in choosing service providers, ensuring objectivity in the process.

Employee Benefits:

Trillium knows that work/life balance is essential. That’s why we offer:

  • Typical working hours: 8:30 am – 5:00 pm; flexible work schedules with some roles with management approval.
  • Work-from-home options available for most positions
  • Health Insurance with no premium for employee coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 24 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) plus 12 paid holidays in your first year
  • NC Local Government Retirement Pension (defined-benefit plan)
  • 401k with 5% employer match and immediate vesting
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) qualifying employer
  • Quarterly stipend for remote work supplies

Qualifications

Required:

  • Must meet QP status.
  1. Fully licensed by the NC governing board regulating Human Services professions; OR Fully licensed RN who is licensed to practice in the state of NC by the NC Board of Nursing who also has four (4) years of full-time experience with the MH/DD/SA population served. OR
  2. A graduate of a college or university with a Master’s degree in a human service field and has one year of full-time, pre or post-graduate degree accumulated MH/DD/SA experience with the MH/DD/SA population, or a substance abuse professional who has one year of full-time, pre or postgraduate degree accumulated supervised experience in alcoholism and drug abuse counseling; OR
  3. A graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree in a human service field and has two years of full-time, pre or post-bachelor's degree accumulated MH/DD/SA experience with the MH/DD/SA population, or a substance abuse professional who has two years of full-time, pre or post bachelor's degree accumulated supervised experience in alcoholism and drug abuse counseling; OR
  4. A graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree in a field other than human services and has four years of full-time, pre or post-bachelor's degree accumulated MH/DD/SA experience with the MH/DD/SA population, or a substance abuse professional who has four years of full-time, pre or post-bachelor's degree accumulated supervised experience in alcoholism and drug abuse counseling.
  • Additionally, If serving members with LTSS needs, the care manager, must meet the minimum QP requirements defined above (A-D) and shall additionally have at a minimum two (2) years of prior LTSS and/or HCBS coordination, care delivery monitoring and care management experience. This experience may be concurrent with the years of experience required to become a Qualified Professional.
  • License and/or certification may be accepted as noted above.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license.
  • Must reside in Trillium’s North Central Region, which includes the following counties: Beaufort, Dare, Edgecombe, Greene, Hyde, Nash, Pamlico, Pitt, Tyrrell, Washington and Wilson.

  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship for employment now or in the future (ex: OPT F-1, J-1).

Preferred:

  • Experience with the Innovation Waiver or IDD population.
  • Care management experience.

Join our Talent Community through ADP to stay informed about future opportunities. Be sure to keep your resume updated in your profile.

jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Applied Scientist (Pricing) to design and evolve dynamic pricing systems for our marketplace. You will develop pricing as a feedback-driven decision system, balancing supply, demand, and business outcomes under uncertainty and delayed signals. Unlike traditional surge-based pricing, our marketplace operates on a unique bid-based pricing model, where prices are shaped through direct negotiation between riders and drivers. This creates a fundamentally different optimization problem, requiring advanced approaches to modeling user behavior, incentives, and marketplace dynamics.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and improve dynamic pricing policies, including elasticity and supply/demand response modeling
  • Frame pricing as a decision system under uncertainty and delayed feedback
  • Develop, test, and deploy real-time pricing algorithms
  • Design and analyze A/B experiments to evaluate pricing impact
  • Productionize models in collaboration with engineering, ensuring scalability and robustness
  • Monitor system performance, including stability, feedback effects, and long-term behavior
  • Contribute to methodological choices (e.g., optimization, control, RL-inspired approaches)

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

  • 3+ years of experience in Data Science, Applied Research, or algorithmic product optimization, preferably in marketplaces or pricing systems
  • Strong background in statistics, optimization, and causal inference
  • Proven ability to move from problem formulation to production-grade solutions
  • Proficiency in Python, SQL, and experience with production ML systems

Nice to Have
  • Experience with economic modeling (elasticity, auctions, policy design)
  • Familiarity with control systems, RL, or online optimization
  • Experience working with real-time, high-load systems

Why join us

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a Core AE, you will be helping our largest and most strategic enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US in the following states: Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, and Wisconsin.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close

  • 5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $100k+ ARR transactions
  • Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships
  • Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting

Annual OTE Salary
$222,400—$278,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. Belonging at Samsara

Accommodations

Our Commitment to Authenticity

Company Overview

Our client is a focused, growing SaaS company building the all-in-one booking and park-management platform for outdoor hospitality. Its software helps campground, RV park, and glamping operators manage reservations, availability, rates, payments, guest messaging, and reporting from one place. It also runs a traveler-facing marketplace that brings operators more bookings. Many customers are small and mid-sized businesses moving away from scattered tools, and they value one thing above all: practical, patient help getting it right.

Your Role

This is not a "read the script and close the ticket" role.

  • You'll own the customer experience from kickoff to launch. That means learning the product inside and out, understanding how each park actually operates, and setting customers up so the platform fits their real-world workflows.

  • Every campground is different: unique rate rules, site layouts, seasonal patterns, and different levels of comfort with technology. Your job is to simplify that complexity. You'll anticipate where customers get stuck and guide them before it becomes a blocker.

  • Success looks like smooth launches, confident customers, and product and engineering teams hearing clearly what customers need.

You’ll:

  • Guide new customers through onboarding end to end, from kickoff calls to go-live

  • Become a true expert on the platform, including availability, rates, payments, site maps, reporting, and guest communication

  • Deliver tailored demos that turn complex features into simple, practical examples

  • Build onboarding plans, setup checklists, and clear follow-up emails after every call

  • Spot common points of confusion early and address them proactively

  • Share specific customer insights, recurring questions, and pain points with product and engineering

  • Keep notes, next steps, and setup details organized in CRM and tracking tools

  • Stay calm, responsive, and organized during peak-season urgency

You Bring:

  • 2+ years of customer-facing experience, ideally in SaaS onboarding, implementation, customer success, support, or product training

  • Experience onboarding or training customers on a software product

  • The ability to explain complex software in plain language to non-technical users

  • Real curiosity about product details, and enjoyment of becoming the go-to expert

  • Strong organization and follow-through across calls, notes, and next steps

  • Comfort with CRM, helpdesk, or project-tracking tools

  • Excellent written and spoken English

  • Patience and empathy with users who feel overwhelmed by new tools, including when you're explaining the same concept for the third time

Bonus Points:

  • Experience in hospitality, reservations, booking, or payments software

  • Background in implementation work with complex, configurable setups

  • Experience turning customer feedback into clear, actionable notes for product teams

What’s Offered:

  • Remote setup with schedule overlap for customer calls and team collaboration

  • Compensation of $1,500–2,000 USD, based on experience

  • Growth paths into customer success ownership, implementation leadership, product education, or customer operations

  • A lean, hands-on team where your work is visible and valued

  • The chance to help small businesses in outdoor hospitality modernize and grow

  • Direct influence on the product through the customer insights you bring back

Interview Process

1️⃣ Application review and screening call with Atomic HR
2️⃣ Customer-facing interview, walking through your onboarding or implementation experience
3️⃣ Hiring team conversation on product curiosity, ownership, and handling customer complexity
4️⃣ Practical exercise, such as explaining a feature, running an onboarding scenario, or writing a customer follow-up

5️⃣ Final conversation and offer

The ISSE will engineer secure solutions across development, deployment, and operations.

This hands-on role focuses on security architecture, hardening, AWS cloud and container security, automation, vulnerability remediation, and technical testing. The ISSE will work with engineers, the Information System Security Manager (ISSM), and the Information System Security Officer (ISSO) to implement controls and provide evidence supporting authorization and continuous monitoring.

This remote position requires an active Secret security clearance. Periodic travel may be required for integration, assessments, customer meetings, and access to approved facilities. All classified work must be performed in approved facilities.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors, helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

  • Translate mission needs and security requirements into system architectures, control implementations, secure configurations, and testable acceptance criteria.
  • Perform threat modeling and security design reviews; identify trust boundaries, attack surfaces, data flows, dependencies, and technical risks before deployment.
  • Engineer and implement security controls for AWS infrastructure, Linux systems, containers, Kubernetes, application interfaces, and supporting services in coordination with system owners.
  • Configure and validate identity and access controls, least-privilege permissions, network segmentation, encryption, certificates, secrets management, audit logging, and security monitoring.
  • Apply Defense Information Systems Agency Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and approved hardening baselines; test changes for security effectiveness and mission impact.
  • Integrate security scanning and checks into continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, including code, dependency, container-image, secrets, and infrastructure-configuration checks.
  • Use scripting, infrastructure as code, and configuration automation to deploy repeatable security controls, detect configuration drift, and collect technical evidence.
  • Analyze vulnerability findings, validate applicability, implement fixes, and retest remediation; propose compensating controls for authorized review when immediate correction is not feasible.
  • Develop and execute security verification tests, support authorized assessments, and troubleshoot issues involving application, network, cloud, identity, and container security controls.
  • Produce security diagrams, configuration baselines, control implementation details, and test evidence supporting Risk Management Framework (RMF) activities and Authority to Operate (ATO) packages.
  • Coordinate technical remediation and closure evidence with the ISSO and ISSM; document residual risks and recommendations for government risk decisions without independently accepting risk.
  • Assess proposed system changes, maintain engineering documentation and runbooks, and support incident investigation, recovery, and corrective actions with responsible operations teams.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Active Secret security clearance, with the ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret if required by the assignment.
  • Minimum of five years of relevant experience in systems security engineering, cybersecurity engineering, cloud security, secure platform engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Hands-on experience implementing, troubleshooting, and validating security controls. Policy review or compliance documentation experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
  • Experience engineering or securing Department of Defense (DoD) information systems, including systems operating on or connected to the Department of Defense Information Network (DODIN).
  • Demonstrated hands-on professional experience implementing, securing, operating, and troubleshooting AWS workloads. Candidates must be able to describe AWS environments they supported, security controls they personally implemented, and remediation they validated. AWS certification or coursework alone, or experience limited to other cloud providers, does not satisfy this requirement.
  • Practical experience with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), security groups, compute and storage security, encryption, and AWS logging and monitoring, including AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch.
  • Experience hardening and troubleshooting Linux systems and containerized workloads, with working knowledge of Kubernetes security controls.
  • Experience using scripting, infrastructure as code, or configuration-management tools to automate security tasks, and working with source control and software delivery pipelines.
  • Working knowledge of TCP/IP networking, routing, firewalls, network segmentation, secure application connectivity, certificates, encryption, and identity and access management.
  • Experience applying RMF requirements, NIST SP 800-53 controls, STIGs, vulnerability scanning, and remediation practices to technical implementations and authorization evidence.
  • Current relevant cybersecurity certification and ability to meet applicable contractual workforce qualifications, including DoD 8140 work-role requirements where applicable.
  • Strong technical writing, troubleshooting, and coordination skills; ability to work independently with distributed engineering teams and support periodic travel. A college degree is not required.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience securing AWS GovCloud environments or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), including workloads supporting DoD Impact Level 4, 5, or 6.
  • Experience with Terraform, Ansible, GitLab, Helm, policy as code, hardened container images, software bills of materials, artifact signing, or automated security evidence collection.
  • Experience engineering Zero Trust controls, Common Access Card authentication, DoD public key infrastructure integration, or secure interfaces between approved mission environments.
  • Experience supporting eMASS or another government authorization system through engineering artifacts, control implementation details, assessment responses, and remediation evidence.
  • Experience supporting Special Operations Forces, combatant commands, mission software, AI-enabled platforms, or robotics and autonomous-system programs.
  • CISSP, ISSEP, CCSP, Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist, cloud security, or another relevant advanced technical certification.
  • Bachelor's or master's degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, engineering, or a related discipline.

The target salary range for this position is $92,075 - $158,138.

The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is not a guarantee of compensation. Individual salaries are determined by various factors including, but not limited to location, internal equity, business considerations, client contract requirements, and candidate qualifications, such as education, experience, skills, and security clearances.  

Applicants must meet eligibility requirements for a U.S. Government security clearance. Only US Citizens are eligible for a security clearance. Everyday Speech is a no-prep digital curriculum that makes teaching social, behavioral, and communication skills easy and effective. The MTSS-aligned curriculum combines evidence-based video modeling, interactive web games, and worksheets to provide educators everything they need to support both neurodiverse and neurotypical PK-12 students. Everyday Speech is trusted by 50,000+ special educators, speech-language pathologists, counselors, and other specialists for targeted interventions and whole-class lessons that help students build the skills they need to thrive.

Everyday Speech is right for you if:

You care about making a positive impact.

End each day knowing your work directly impacted educators across North America in our mission to build the most impactful PreK-12 social skills curriculum and make teaching it effortless. Success goes beyond shipping features here; we’re improving the lives of educators and their students. To achieve this, we create meaningful content, stay closely connected to our users, and maintain consistently high NPS scores as a fully bootstrapped company growing organically and sustainably.

You value being a part of a company that takes care of its team.

Not only do we have extremely happy team members, we also have incredible perks. Participate in our health/wellness and retirement benefit offerings, and between having every other Friday off (3-day weekends!) and our flexible PTO plan, that elusive work-life balance is an actual thing here. We’ve also never had an office and never will. We take remote work seriously and know how to support a distributed team. We give you the flexibility to work in a way that’s best for you, but still have high standards and accountability. These are just some of the reasons why our eNPS score from 2025 was 78.

You want to be at a company whose values are more than just words on a wall.

Our values are at the forefront of our decisions, how we recognize each other, how we challenge ourselves—everything we do. Our values mean something, and with that guiding light, we are able to land with clarity, create alignment, identify our strengths, and move with purpose. Hear it directly from a team member: “I love the values. I never imagined I could end up in a position that was so connected to the things that mattered to me most”.

As a member of the Growth team, the Demand Generation Manager will own how educators discover and choose to try Everyday Speech, through product-led content drawn from our product and the clinical expertise behind it. This is an individual contributor role for a strategic marketer and strong writer who can set the demand strategy and also do the work: create, publish, promote, measure, and iterate.

You will own net-new demand across webinars, community and creators, partnerships, email, paid social, website content and search, including AI answers. You'll partner closely with our clinical team, who bring the expertise that makes our content credible, and with the rest of the marketing team and Sales to make sure content reaches the right people and moves them forward.

The ideal candidate is extremely values aligned:

● We start with empathy— in the work we do and the people we do it with. Our strength comes from a culture that values candidness, trust, and valuing our teammates as whole human beings. We care, challenge, and communicate. We are serious about our responsibility to educators, who rely on us every day.

● We ruthlessly prioritize. We don ’t just say no to the obvious stuff, we say no to the things that feel important in the moment because we understand anything we say yes to is inherently saying no to something else.

● We create momentum. We don’t let the small stuff hold us back. We learn by shipping. We know most actions are reversible and that action always wins in the long run. If all else fails, bias towards action.

● We are fearlessly objective. We don't do things just because we're "supposed to." We constantly ask "why" and don’t let conventional norms define our efforts. We're not afraid to seek answers, even if that means discovering we were wrong. We focus on what delivers results, regardless of the source.

● We exercise agency. We have the ability to create systems that don’t yet exist to get what we need or to solve problems no one has identified. If something isn’t working, it’s within our control to fix it.

● We’re driven to grow. We set ambitious goals because we want to maximize our impact. We embrace challenges and take risks, seeing failures as opportunities to learn and improve. We seek out feedback and coaching and thrive in environments that push us.

Your work will have a significant impact on how we drive new contacts, product signups, and pipeline, and will shape how educators and district leaders come to know and trust Everyday Speech.

In this role, you will:

  • Own Everyday Speech's demand generation strategy and product-led content calendar, planned around the school year, choosing the topics and formats that drive new contacts, form submissions, and product sign-ups.
  • Decide which channels we invest in, including new ones, how we show up on each, and how each moves educators into and through the funnel.
  • Lead with product-led content: our free resources, lead magnets, and SEO pages come from the product itself, so educators experience Everyday Speech through the content they find.
  • Own all website content, including resources, blog posts, landing pages and lead magnets, and the path from content to signup: CTAs, gated and ungated offers, and conversion testing.
  • Own our webinar program end to end: topics, speakers, CEU partnerships, promotion, and follow-up.
  • Partner with our clinical team to turn their expertise into content, including organic social, and to put their credibility in front of the educators who trust it.
  • Grow co-marketing partnerships with associations, CEU providers, and aligned organizations, from co-hosted webinars to guest content.
  • Own and produce our monthly content email calendar, grow our email audience, and build campaigns that distribute content.
  • Own paid promotion as a core lever, building on our Meta ads strategy and testing other paid channels.
  • Own search as one channel among many, including SEO and especially AEO, so educators find us in search results and in AI-generated answers.
  • Partner with the marketing team on case studies, customer stories, account-based content, and enablement content for Sales and Customer Success, leading development where relevant.
  • Shape how we tell the Everyday Speech story and set the standards behind it: voice and style guide, clinical accuracy review, and a high bar for AI-assisted work.
  • Own demand results (new contacts, product signups, webinar registrations and pipeline contribution), treating content as an experiment and reporting on what works.

What We’re Looking For

In addition to values alignment…

  • 5+ years in growth marketing, ideally in B2B SaaS or EdTech with a product-led motion, including time owning a content strategy rather than only executing one.
  • A track record of growing leads and pipeline across multiple channels. SEO experience and a point of view on how AI search is changing it are a plus.
  • Exceptional writing and editing. You make complex topics clear and useful, and you can tell expert content from generic content.
  • Experience translating subject-matter expertise (clinical, education, or similar) into content that practitioners trust.
  • Experience running webinars or events that drive registrations and follow-up engagement.
  • Hands-on experience with paid social and content promotion, including managing contractors or agencies.
  • A data-driven approach: you set goals, read the numbers in HubSpot, Google Analytics, or Semrush, and change course without being told.
  • Strong project management. You can run an editorial calendar across several stakeholders and contractors and ship on time.
  • Thoughtful use of AI in your workflow, paired with high standards for originality and accuracy.
  • Genuine interest in K-12 education and empathy for the SLPs, special educators, and counselors we serve. Familiarity with school audiences or district buying is a plus.
  • High ownership: you treat content like your part of the business and follow through.

We know great candidates come from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re passionate about what we’re building at Everyday Speech, don’t hesitate to apply—even if you’re not sure you meet every qualification.

In the short term (the first 3 months), you will:

  • Audit our existing website content, search performance, conversion paths, and content library to find what still works, what's outdated, and the biggest gaps to close first.
  • Build a 6-month content plan tied to Growth team goals, with clear success metrics for each channel.
  • Take over active SEO and AEO projects and contractor relationships as part of the broader channel plan.
  • Relaunch a regular webinar program, with a calendar of topics and speakers.

  • Learn our audience by talking with educators, shadowing Sales and Customer Success, and reviewing what our best-performing content has in common.
  • Establish a monthly reporting cadence on each channel's contribution to new contacts, signups, and pipeline.

In the Long term, you will:

  • Grow organic search and AI answer visibility for the topics our audience cares about most.
  • Run a webinar program that educators look forward to and that consistently fills the top of the funnel.
  • Support district expansion with ABM content and the case studies and customer stories our teams need.
  • Build a community of educator advocates, creators, and partners who extend our reach well beyond our own channels.
  • Turn our clinical team's credibility into a durable trust asset across social, webinars, and the website.
  • Build the case for scaling demand, documenting what it produces, what it requires, and where more investment would pay off.

jobs.title: Director, Marketing Technology
jobs.excerpt: About StepStep's mission is to improve the financial future of the next generation.
jobs.description:
About Step

Step's mission is to improve the financial future of the next generation. Millions of people use our banking and borrowing products to manage, build, and grow their money. Now that we're part of Beast Industries – the company behind MrBeast – we're poised for a new phase of growth to deliver financial literacy and tools at massive scale.

About the Role

Marketing at Step runs on data. Every acquisition channel, lifecycle campaign, rewards drop, and measurement decision depends on clean, connected, well-modeled data flowing between our product, our warehouse, and a dozen marketing platforms. Today, much of that work lands on engineering. We're hiring a Director, Marketing Technology, to own it end-to-end.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role for someone with a software or data engineering background who wants to apply that skill set to growth. You'll be the architect and operator of Step's marketing technology stack: owning our ad channel and attribution integrations, managing our vendor ecosystem (Segment, AppsFlyer, Braze, Funnel, and others), building the data models and analytical tooling the marketing team runs on, and shipping the monthly rewards and offers that drive engagement. You'll act as the bridge between Marketing, Product, and Engineering taking on the technical work that currently pulls engineers away from the core product, and raising the bar on what marketing can measure, automate, and personalize.

You'll start as a hands-on individual contributor with the opportunity to build and lead a marketing technology team as the function scales.

In this role, you will:

Own the marketing technology stack

  • Own the architecture, roadmap, and day-to-day operation of Step's martech ecosystem including CDP, MMP, lifecycle messaging, data aggregation, and analytics tooling along with the documentation, QA, and governance standards that keep it reliable and privacy-compliant
  • Manage all marketing technology partners (Segment, AppsFlyer, Braze, Funnel, and similar), including evaluation, implementation, optimization, and contract/renewal input

Build and optimize ad channel and measurement integrations

  • Configure, validate, and maintain integrations with paid channels (Meta, Google, TikTok, and similar), including server-side conversion APIs, event schemas, setup counting methods, attribution windows, and first-party audience syncs
  • Own attribution and mobile measurement (AppsFlyer/Segment): SKAN/postback configuration, conversion windows, deduplication, and channel-level data quality
  • Partner on GA4 implementation including event taxonomy, funnel conversion configuration, and custom reporting; leveraging GA4 data to fill attribution gaps across channels and inform incrementality analysis

Be the data backbone of the marketing team

  • Build and maintain the pipelines and data models that power marketing reporting, audience segmentation, and campaign measurement with identity, event, and audience definitions kept consistent across product, warehouse, and activation platforms
  • Develop self-serve analytical tools, dashboards, and automations so marketers can answer their own questions (ie. spend pacing, funnel conversion, LTV, incrementality)

Ship marketing programs

  • Own the technical build of Step's monthly rewards and offers program end to end targeting logic, delivery, tracking, and post-campaign readout
  • Support lifecycle and CRM campaign execution in Braze: triggers and data feeds

Partner across the company

  • Serve as marketing's technical counterpart to Product, Engineering, and Data scoping requests, setting priorities, and taking build work off engineering's plate

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 7+ years across software engineering, data engineering, or marketing technology, with meaningful time spent as a hands-on engineer
  • Proven experience owning a modern martech stack at a consumer company: CDP (Segment or similar), MMP (AppsFlyer, Adjust, or Branch), and lifecycle platforms (Braze or similar)
  • Strong SQL and working proficiency in a scripting language (Python or JavaScript); comfortable with APIs, webhooks, event-driven architectures, and cloud data warehouses
  • Deep understanding of mobile and web attribution: conversion APIs, SKAdNetwork, postbacks, deduplication, and incrementality
  • A clear communicator who bridges marketing, engineering, and executive audiences
  • You are hungry for action and you'd rather ship a working solution this week than a perfect one next quarter
  • Experience operating martech at larger scale, ideally through viral moments or campaign-driven traffic spikes

Some of the technology we use:

  • Kotlin
  • gRPC
  • Protocol Buffers
  • Dagger
  • Postgres
  • JOOQ
  • BigQuery
  • Kubernetes
  • Terraform

Logistics

Location: Remote (US) or San Mateo, CA, with occasional travel for team offsites and key meetings

Reports to: Chief Marketing Officer

Education: Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every single qualification. Strong candidates rarely check every box, and we'd rather meet you than miss you.

How we're different

We stand for the side hustlers, the creators, the freelancers, and the investors — people who are not afraid to take on challenges, especially when it comes to their finances. Step is focused on disrupting the banking industry by delivering a differentiated, mobile-first consumer experience, and we operate like the customers we serve: customer obsessed, acting as owners, moving with urgency, and breaking the norm.

Step is a wholly owned subsidiary of Beast Industries, the media and entertainment company founded by Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast), the most-watched person in the world. Beast Industries spans digital media, consumer products, philanthropy, and new ventures, with an audience reach no consumer company has ever had — and Step is tasked with turning that reach into financial literacy and tools for the next generation at massive scale. With Beast's distribution and brand behind it, Step is positioned to scale significantly over the next 12 months, and joining now means helping shape that trajectory from the inside.

Come work with us!

Step is a remote-first company building banking for the next generation. We offer competitive compensation and stock options, generous medical, dental, vision, and company-paid life insurance, a 401k plan with Safe Harbor company matching, a flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays, 12 weeks paid parental leave with flexible return to work, and a company-provided technology package. If you're looking to join a fast-growing company with a strong mission and vision that puts people first, we want to meet you!

Step is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Step is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and interview process. If you need an accommodation, please let us know at and we'll work with you to provide appropriate support.
